items.excerpt: 篠原眞 私の歴史的録音 前衛の探求 Makoto Shinohara Meine historischen Aufnahmen スリーシェルズ 3SCD0083 2026年8月2日発売 制作：篠原眞作品普及会 Text by 齋藤俊夫(Toshio Saito) <収録曲> （全て篠原眞作曲） 『ヴァイオリンとピアノのためのソナタ』(1958) 『ミュージック・コンクレートのための試作』(1960) 『電子音楽の習作』(1962) 『打楽器のためのアルテルナンス（交互）』(1962) 『ピアノのためのタンダンス（傾向）』(1963) 『テノール・リコーダーのためのフラグメンテ（断片）』(1968) 『オーケストラのためのヴィジョン（幻影）II』 『箏・打楽器・声のための「たゆたい」』(1972) （ボーナストラック）『一人の打楽器奏者とテープのためのランコントゥル（出会い）』(1972) なんと、孤独な、音楽で、あろうか……。筆者はこのCDを一聴して自分の心臓が雪女に掴まれたかのような心底冷たい思いを感じた。 篠原眞最晩年の、かのパンデミック下でのコンサートにおいて筆者が生演奏で直に聴
items.body: 篠原眞 私の歴史的録音 前衛の探求 Makoto Shinohara Meine historischen Aufnahmen スリーシェルズ 3SCD0083 2026年8月2日発売 制作：篠原眞作品普及会 Text by 齋藤俊夫(Toshio Saito) <収録曲> （全て篠原眞作曲） 『ヴァイオリンとピアノのためのソナタ』(1958) 『ミュージック・コンクレートのための試作』(1960) 『電子音楽の習作』(1962) 『打楽器のためのアルテルナンス（交互）』(1962) 『ピアノのためのタンダンス（傾向）』(1963) 『テノール・リコーダーのためのフラグメンテ（断片）』(1968) 『オーケストラのためのヴィジョン（幻影）II』 『箏・打楽器・声のための「たゆたい」』(1972) （ボーナストラック）『一人の打楽器奏者とテープのためのランコントゥル（出会い）』(1972) なんと、孤独な、音楽で、あろうか……。筆者はこのCDを一聴して自分の心臓が雪女に掴まれたかのような心底冷たい思いを感じた。 篠原眞最晩年の、かのパンデミック下でのコンサートにおいて筆者が生演奏で直に聴き「神なき世界に生まれた宗教者（略）の慟哭とも言うべきパトスの激流を浴び」たと記した、篠原27歳時の作品『ヴァイオリンとピアノのためのソナタ』の時点で既に、彼が自己の音楽を徹底的に〈客観化〉する態度は現れていた。 音楽の客観化とは、その音楽をある人間（作曲家含む）の主観的な感情・好悪・心理に委ねることを許さず、それらから音楽を断ち切り、あくまで、ある音楽がただある音楽だけの存在とせんとすることを言う。篠原の音楽の厳しさ・美しさ、そして孤独はこの客観化への強烈な指向から立ち現れる。彫琢に次ぐ彫琢を重ねることにより、音楽の客観性は堅固となり、同時に音楽から主観的情緒・感情は排されていく。そのことにより、音楽をどんなに聴いてもその音楽に聴き手である我々が感情移入・自己同一化をすることは拒まれ、ただその峻厳たる音楽と自分とが断絶されて孤独に佇むしかなくなる。 『打楽器のためのアルテルナンス』『ピアノのためのタンダンス』『テノール・リコーダーのためのフラグメンテ』『オーケストラのためのヴィジョン（幻影）II』『箏・打楽器・声のための「たゆたい」』たちの強烈なフォルテの音、聴覚神経にかろうじて届くほどのピアノの音、どれもが孤独だ。これらの音楽をいくら聴いても、どこにも聴いている〈自分〉、そして奏でている〈彼ら＝奏者〉さらには書いた〈彼＝作曲者〉の主観が現れることはない。その孤独な音楽は、しかし〈寂しい〉音楽にはならない。寂しいという〈感情〉〈感覚〉はより〈人情的〉〈感情的〉なものだ。〈人間的〉なものだ。そのような〈人間的〉な主観的なものが篠原の極度に客観的な音楽とそれを聴く我々の間に介在する余地はない。篠原の音楽はただひたすらに〈そこにある〉ことで自足する。どこまでも美しく、孤独なまま、ただそこにある。そのことは、嬉しいことなのだろうか、あるいは寂しいことなのだろうか。それでも、筆者は彼と彼の音楽が在ってくれたことに絶えようもない喜びを感じ、感謝を思ってしまう。 ただし、この篠原の音楽の客観性という観点からして、會田瑞樹の打楽器ソロとテープによる『一人の打楽器奏者とテープのためのランコントゥル（出会い）』はいささか居心地が悪かった。會田の打楽器の腕は買うが、あまりにも感情的、つまり主観的な乱打絶叫は例えば石井眞木のアンサンブル曲ならば良いが、篠原眞にはそぐわないと言わせてもらいたい。 関連記事：Pick Up(2026/6/15)「篠原眞メモリアルコンサート」とCD「私の歴史的録音」をめぐって｜髙久暁 (2026/8/15)
items._genre: avant-garde / contemporary classical / experimental / musique concrète / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了作曲家篠原眞1958至1972年间的前卫作品历史录音，涵盖钢琴与弦乐奏鸣曲、具体音乐试作、电子音乐习作、打乐曲、记录器独奏及筝与打乐器声乐作品等。评论聚焦篠原音乐彻底的'客观化'美学——通过精密的雕琢将主观情感从音乐中彻底剥离，使音乐仅以自身存在的方式自足。评论者以'雪女攫心'形容初次聆听的冷冽感受，认为这种极端的客观性恰恰构成了其严苛之美的来源。评论同时指出，打乐器演奏家會田瑞樹在附赠曲目中过于情感化的表现与篠原的美学原则存在落差。整体而言，这套录音展现了日本战后前卫音乐对声音本体性的持续追问。

items.album: False LP A
items.excerpt: Topdown Dialectic’s solo debut bow on False Aralia draws a line under over a decade of material in supremely elusive style & pattern - all rug-pulling rhythms and hallucinatory fractals wrapped up with proper, hyperreal frisson. Massive chef’s kiss FFO Vladislav Delay, Beatrice Dillon, Paperclip Minimiser, Purelink, Marc... more
items.body:
Topdown Dialectic’s solo debut bow on False Aralia draws a line under over a decade of material in supremely elusive style & pattern - all rug-pulling rhythms and hallucinatory fractals wrapped up with proper, hyperreal frisson. Massive chef’s kiss FFO Vladislav Delay, Beatrice Dillon, Paperclip Minimiser, Purelink, Marc Leclair, T++.

An artist keenly observed since those initial anonymous gestures on /\\Aught in the early ‘10s, and through a cult LP trilogy for Peak Oil during 2018-2021; Topdown Dialectic has become a unique facet of C.21st dub electronics, adored for their grasp of diffused spatio-textural sorcery and wraithlike grooves. Anyone paying close attention to emergent sounds via Peak Oil and its False Aralia offshoot may have guessed at the project’s signature, watermarked imprint on the Borgesian Term EP of late ’25, which can now be confirmed as the work of one and the same Izaak Schlossmann; a photographer and producer patently in possession of heightened proprioceptions and a rewardingly patient approach to lushly dissociative sonification. In other words, he makes some of the sexiest electronic music out there - stuff that genuinely feels like it was made this century - and his latest practically leaves you kissing the sky thru its 80 minutes of lip-biting, skin tingling pressure. 

On 16 tracks timed at exactly 5 minutes each, we’re placed in the presence of suggestive sorcery in a unique ecology of oneiric physics. Never overtly showy or overblown, there’s nevertheless a staggering level of ingenuity and synaesthetic effect to its detailed construction and gaseous fractals resembling the LSD or DMT experience. The label themselves compare its nuance to “the flicker of a candle over a desk of drum machines in a Midwestern basement, or the “first blush of sunlight over a tiny campground as subwoofers creak in the distance”, which proves a perfectly poetic analog to its digitally-smudged refractions and tongue-tip spectral tumescence, and in effect feels like an aesthetic descendent of Torsten Pröfrock’s convulsive prototypes as T++. 

Ultimately, though, it’s a singular pleasure to immerse the senses in Topdown Dialectic’s self-contained soundsphere, and never more substantially so than on ‘False LP A’. Longtime enthusiasts will surely recognise his skill in parsing salient aspects of Basic Channel x Rhythm & Sound, and their descendants in Vladislav Delay or Pole, reframing those templates in far more uncertain space with a real animist magick. Each work feels tangibly, ambiguously alive, breathing with dynamics and more voluminous, macro scales, and iridescent with voices and details that commands attentive listeners who will have a field day zoning in/out to its illusive, holographic projections and syncopated chronics.
items._genre: dub techno / experimental electronic / ambient / IDM
items._cn_summary: 这是制作人Izaak Schlossmann化名Topdown Dialectic的首张全长专辑，发行于其合作的独立子厂牌False Aralia。评论将其置于Basic Channel、Rhythm & Sound、Vladislav Delay一脉的dub电子谱系中加以审视，强调作品对这一传统的重构与超越。专辑由16首时长各为5分钟的曲目组成，构成了一个自足的声音场域。文本反复使用"气体状分形""全息投射""幽灵活体"等意象来描述其声学特质，将其与LSD或DMT引发的知觉状态相类比，并暗示其继承了T++式痉挛原型的不确定性逻辑。厂牌自身的文字以"地下室中蜡烛映照鼓机"等画面形容其细节的细腻度，评论认为这一比喻准确捕捉了作品中数字涂抹般的折射效果与微妙的张力。

items.album: fata morgana
items.excerpt: Weirder, wider, knottier and more hypnotic than its predecessors, L'rain's fourth album closes out her opening act with a vivid firework display of canny cultural references, considered observations and, most crucially, heartbreakingly beautiful songs. It's dumbfounding material, the kind of omnivorous, masterful gear that... more
items.body:
Weirder, wider, knottier and more hypnotic than its predecessors, L'rain's fourth album closes out her opening act with a vivid firework display of canny cultural references, considered observations and, most crucially, heartbreakingly beautiful songs. It's dumbfounding material, the kind of omnivorous, masterful gear that just doesn't come around often enough - a future classic, to put it bluntly, FFO keiyaA, Mabe Fratti, Dawuna, Dijon or even Broadcast.

There's an aura of comprehensiveness that surrounds 'fata morgana'. Taja Cheek has fully broken in her influences and inspirations at this stage and works without hesitation, painting out her experiences of a broken world with a level of insight that's so rare it's almost unparalleled. We already know that Cheek is a forensic listener; 2024's 'I Killed Your Dog' was a chunky "anti-break-up" album that met sorrow head-on with psych rock, indie, classic R&B and haunted folk references, while its predecessor projected Cheek's ambition, embedding shoegaze and ambient influences into a widescreen collage of avant-garde expressions. It wasn't fusion, exactly, it was Cheek's real-world experience - both as an artist and a high-profile curator - inked on thick, deluxe stock in illuminated letters. And the cycle that she began in 2017 with her tape saturated debut comes to a close with 'fata morgana'.

'I Killed Your Dog' was well aware of its lineage, recorded and produced with a level of detail that immediately put it alongside '70s avant-rock and R&B classics, so 'fata morgana' scratches away another layer, making deeper, odder connections. Even the brief 'rumors of light' is anything but throwaway, casually introducing Cheek's voice through a hailstorm of looped interference that's broken up by disarming bouts of silence. This doesn't only slickly establish the record's experimental credentials, it echoes the eerie 'Transmission' tracks on DJ Shadow's 'Endtroducing'. "This is not a dream," a garbled voice memorably stated, and Cheek's utterances hint at the exact opposite, a choppy mess of backmasked syllables, coughs and hesitations that suggest we're being lowered into a surreal fantasy. Fairytale muted piano phrases appear in the distance and 'with time' materializes on the horizon, kinked by buzzing oscillations that blur time just slightly until Cheek's whisper-sung vocals sidestep into the candlelight. 

Already, it's Cheek's most enigmatic track, occupying the confounding spot between an acid-tweaked Laurel Canyon memory, a half-heard gospel standard and Wendy Carlos's iconic 'The Shining' score: beautiful, meaningful and effortlessly cinematic. And Cheek continues to paint outside the lines, concocting half-song 'blue' from tape-mangled brass loops and gunky drum improvisations that she scrapes into a seductive, hazed atmosphere underneath her reverberating chorals. It's tempting to reference shoegaze or dream pop; the end result is similar, texturally at least, but 'fata morgana' is comprised of hardier raw material: minerals crushed by hand from funk, spiritual jazz, reggae, blues and rock 'n roll. That's never more obvious than on the gorgeous 'july 5th', when smudged folk - mixed with screaming feedback and analog bleeps, of course - mutates into a jerky soundsystem banger in its final act, imagining what OutKast's 'B.O.B.' might sound like if Atlanta was swapped out for Kingston.

Then there's the brassy standout 'elmyra', an anthemic start-stop post-pop banger that's part 'Haha Sound'-era Broadcast and part Wire, distorted to a level that would terrify most green-gilled pretenders. All this, and we haven't even mentioned the album's dense, maximalist lead single 'Soulless Cycle', a track that begins with chattering, bit-crushed samples and double-time kicks and lunges towards its glittering, psychedelic wall of sound that stands as an apt metaphor for the melancholy cacophony of contemporary reality. Before the album's done, Cheek slides in a lysergic slow jam ('birthday') and a near-ambient darkjazz diversion ('church of no one'), reminding us that perseverance and resilience is still possible - preferable, in fact.

Seriously, it's one of those albums that reminds you why you started caring about music in the first place, a milestone that's both cognizant of its place in history and hyper aware of the current moment. So, so good.
items._genre: experimental pop / avant-R&B / art rock / electronic / dream pop
items._cn_summary: L'Rain（Taja Cheek）的第四张专辑《fata morgana》是其个人创作周期的收官之作。专辑延续并深化了她将迷幻摇滚、独立音乐、经典R&B、民谣、氛围音乐与shoegaze融为一体的拼贴式美学，被乐评视为她最具实验性也最难以捉摸的一张作品。Cheek以极具细节的制作手法处理声音素材：磁带循环、倒放人声、回授振荡、静默片段与模糊的钢琴动机交织，构建出介于梦境与现实之间的超现实氛围。歌词层面，她以罕见的洞察力描绘破碎世界的个人体验，歌曲既具备电影感又深具情感重量。整张专辑呈现出综合性的大师级艺术视野，融合了70年代前卫摇滚的精密制作逻辑与当代实验音乐的解构策略，是近年不可多得的另类R&B/实验流行标杆作品。

items.album: Loop Finding Jazz Records
items.excerpt: In the 15+ years that have elapsed since 'Loop Finding Jazz Records' first shuffled out of his ambrosially dusty speakers, Jan Jelinek's most famous album has acquired an almost mythical status. Originally released via Pole's defunct Scape imprint, it now finds new life via Jelinek's own Faitiche label, for a new generation to... more
items.body:
In the 15+ years that have elapsed since 'Loop Finding Jazz Records' first shuffled out of his ambrosially dusty speakers, Jan Jelinek's most famous album has acquired an almost mythical status. Originally released via Pole's defunct Scape imprint, it now finds new life via Jelinek's own Faitiche label, for a new generation to marvel at one of the finest examples of loop-based electronic music typical of the early noughties.

Taking what reads like a pretty austere set of ingredients, Jelinek's technique revolves around a trio of elements which consist of second long cuts of 1960's-70's jazz recordings, the loop-finding modulation wheel (do your homework!) and the Moiré effect; albeit rendered in the acoustic as opposed to the image and spectral domains.

If all this sounds a bit academic, be assured that on record it is anything but; as crumbling edifices of mealy rhythms slowly pulse into life and swirl around your head like snow storms clashing with a dust devil. Taking sediments of fathom deep static then skimming the best stuff from the top, Jelinek opens through the dampened echoes of 'Moiré (piano & organ)' wherein a slow-motion thrum of spiraling clicks, rustles and analogue tones conspire to give the impression of recondite perspectives that extend well beyond the constituent elements.

Elsewhere, 'Rocky in the Video Age' instills a gratuitously optimistic blush to the aquatic micro-sound ebb, 'Moiré (Strings)' is a perfect companion to Basinski's disintegrating tape archive, whilst 'Them, Their' represents an aural crease so sleight you can only catch its distinctive gleam from the corner of your eye.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以极简手法将六十至七十年代爵士唱片切成一秒左右的碎片，借助循环搜索调制轮和声学领域的莫尔效应，将微观的声响残片重新编织成层叠的纹理。没有传统节奏的支撑，缓慢脉动的颗粒、锈蚀般的模拟噪点与模糊的回声构成了作品的全部骨架。钢琴与管风琴的残影在慢速处理中延展为螺旋状的咔哒声与沙沙声，弦乐片段则如同正在解体的磁带，呈现出时间侵蚀般的质感。整张作品介于具象音乐与极简电子之间，以考古式的方法从旧唱片中提炼出全新的声响地貌。

items.album: Window Left Open
items.excerpt: Picking up where 2024's 'Trash Can Lamb' left off, Keith Freund blurs the line between acoustic instrumentation and DIY electronics on his latest full-length, unraveling his gentle, jazzy sessions with 8-bit beats and oddball FX. Since the beginning, Freund has been fixated on the character of a sound rather than what that sound, on... more
items.body:
Picking up where 2024's 'Trash Can Lamb' left off, Keith Freund blurs the line between acoustic instrumentation and DIY electronics on his latest full-length, unraveling his gentle, jazzy sessions with 8-bit beats and oddball FX.

Since the beginning, Freund has been fixated on the character of a sound rather than what that sound, on its own, might represent. His piano parts rarely come off as if they've been played by hand; after chopping them to shreds, he inevitably reconstitutes them into player-piano style impossible sequences, re-organizing the notes and re-sculpting the tone completely. On 'Over Sidewalk Bryum', for example, it's the piano that provides the track's rhythm, accented by radio interference and bit-crushed oscillations. And although Freund does less chipping at his horn parts, letting the sax soar over the chattering electronics, it's still subtly tweaked - nothing's ever quite what it seems.

A swamp of discarded blips and glitches help prop up 'I'll Find a Place for Us', and Freund's soft woodwind tones make their way through the noise initially - or at least that's what we're supposed to think. In time, Freund's sax emerges and the soft-hued, woodwind-like sound is revealed to be a red herring. But that's the kind of sleight of hand that Freund seems to revel in, creating glitchy, unstable music from soft, placid sound sources, not the harsh digital detritus you'd expect to find on a Mille Plateaux disc.
items._genre: experimental jazz / electronic / glitch / DIY electronics
items._cn_summary: Keith Freund延续了前作《Trash Can Lamb》的路线，将原声乐器演奏与DIY电子手段深度融合。钢琴部分被切碎重组为自动钢琴式的荒诞序列，声响被彻底重塑，演奏痕迹几近消隐。萨克斯与木管的处理同样微妙，听感柔和，实则经过电子扭曲，乐评以《Over Sidewalk Bryum》为例，指出钢琴提供了节奏骨架，辅以无线电干扰与比特压缩振荡。《I'll Find a Place for Us》则在杂讯沼泽中暗藏声学假象，萨克斯最终从电子拟态中浮现。整体制作以柔和、安静的声源为材料，搭建出不安定的故障音乐结构，不依赖常规数字噪声，而是从声响的内部质感中提取实验性。

items.body: A Vilnius-based Indonesian composer and a Berlin-based Japanese producer have recorded an album in three different nations and released it on an Ugandan imprint. As a result, Abu sounds as if it comes from nowhere and everywhere at once: a “mystifying new landmass, an imaginary island of ash.” To honor the spirit of the release, today’s review was born on one continent and the interview on another. Along the way, one will hear shavings of sound from each artist’s home. Johanes “Mo’ong” Santoso Pribadi and Shigeru Ishihara intermingle gamelan percussion and taiko rhythms with chants and shouts that seem to come from deepest Africa or from the heart of the volcano. The music imitates lava: erupting, flowing, burning and solidifying. Once it has disrupted the elements around it, Abu incorporates them into a new sonic landmass. In “Hai no uta,” two rings of an Indonesian bell preface more abrasive grinds and growls. A Javanese gong is struck; a high flute wails; a miniaturized choir sings a tiny song, recalling the Shobijin. The tension rises as the percussion begs to break through; and on “Abu,” it does. The tribal rhythms and guttural utterances recall KINACT’s Kinshasa in Action, also on Nyege Nyege Tapes; the continents seem connected again, honoring Pangea. The deep bass of “Palau” reflects subterranean rumble: while over too soon, it gives way to the even more enthralling “Wujud,” whose industrial stumbles and starts are melded to mechanical glissandos, an Orcan, deep earth factory. “Hino Tori” is a wild outlier, bursting forth with bangha rhtymns reminiscent of “Get Your Freak On” and swiftly adding a pounding techno beat; one can imagine this as a club killer on any continent. The metallic middle teases a far different audience before finishing a water bottle and plunging back in, even more energized than before. Those waiting for their thrash moment will find it on the chaotic, ensuing piece: a far cry from the Indonesian bells that launched the set only half an hour before. The LP’s primary draw, outside of its stunning juxtapositions of timbre, is its reaffirmation of a world without borders. Over countless millennia, magma has created innumerable landmasses, while the sea has often impassively reclaimed its own. Human borders mean nothing to geologic time. Abu is a reminder of the wealth of international music: entire species of music that much of the general public has yet to discover. We need not fear such encounters, as they do not threaten our own identity; quite the contrary. Instead, as in the case of Takkak Takkak, they broaden our language and deepen our experience. (Richard Allen) Takkak Takkak photo by @mr_guep Johanes “Mo’ong” Santos Pribadi has kindly taken time out of Takkak Takkak’s touring schedule to answer a few questions about the production process for Abu. Your self-titled debut introduced a thrilling collision between DIY instrument building, Javanese traditions, Japanese electronics, noise, gabber and ritual percussion, often with a raw, playful sense of excess. On Abu, those same elements seem to have become part of a much broader imaginary world—less confrontational perhaps, but more immersive and narrative. Did you consciously set out to expand the language you established on the first album, and what did this fictional “island of ash” allow you to express that the debut could not? Johanes “Mo’ong” Santos Pribadi: I don’t think we approached Abu by asking how to expand what we had done on the first album. It was more about continuing a conversation that had already started. By the time we began working on Abu, we had spent more time playing together, building trust and understanding how each other’s ideas and sounds could interact. Naturally, the music started to move into different directions. With the first album, we were discovering the chemistry between us. There was a lot of direct energy finding out what happens when handmade instruments, distorted electronics, ritual rhythms and dance music collide. Everything felt immediate and physical. For Abu, we had already developed a shared language, so we didn’t need to prove that those elements could coexist. Instead, we could ask where they might take us. The fictional island became a useful way of thinking because it isn’t Indonesia, Japan or anywhere else. It is a place where histories, myths, disasters and dreams can exist together without having to explain themselves. Ash is also an interesting material. It can represent destruction, but it is also what remains after transformation. New life often grows from volcanic ash. So Abu became less about representing a culture and more about imagining how things constantly disappear, mutate and re-emerge. One of the most fascinating aspects of Abu is the way it dissolves fixed notions of place and identity. The album was recorded across Yogyakarta, Švenčionėliai and Berlin, while drawing on Indonesian, Japanese and Baltic sonic environments without allowing any of them to dominate. Rather than presenting cultural traditions as fixed inheritances, the record seems to imagine them as constantly shifting landscapes. How did the experience of working across these different locations reshape your understanding of home, identity and collaboration? Johanes “Mo’ong” Santos Pribadi: For me, identity has never been something fixed. Even traditional music is always changing. Every generation changes instruments, techniques and contexts. Tradition survives because people keep transforming it. Recording in Yogyakarta, Lithuania and Berlin reinforced that feeling. Each place has its own atmosphere, but we weren’t trying to collect local sounds like souvenirs. We were more interested in how our listening changed when we moved through different environments. Sometimes collaboration is less about combining different cultures than about creating a third space where nobody completely owns the result anymore. That’s what interests me. Instead of saying, “This is Indonesian,” or “This is Japanese,” we try to build a shared sonic ecology where those categories become less important than the relationships between sounds. In that sense, home is not only a geographical place. Home can also be a process of making things together. Your debut album was stylistically cohesive even with incursions into techno on tracks like “Salamander” and was driven by rhythm. One of the most striking aspects of Abu is its constant transformation and reflective nature. Ritual percussion gives way to hard dance rhythms, handmade instruments dissolve into electronic textures, and tracks such as “Api” and “Hino-Tori” move effortlessly between ceremony, ecstatic propulsion and the dance floor, while quieter moments like “Pulau”, “Nimbal” or “Funka suru mizu” provide spaces of suspension. Yet none of these shifts feels abrupt or arbitrary. How do you approach composition when working together? Do these transformations emerge intuitively through improvisation and experimentation, or is there an underlying architecture that allows such radically different musical languages to coexist so naturally? Johanes “Mo’ong” Santos Pribadi: Our process is actually very fluid. We improvise a lot because that’s how we discover unexpected relationships between sounds. But improvisation is only the beginning. Afterwards we spend a lot of time listening, editing and thinking about how one sound transforms into another. We’re less interested in contrasting genres than in following the energy inside the sound itself. A ritual drum pattern and a gabber kick might seem completely different stylistically, but physically they both work on the body. They both produce collective movement, trance or repetition. Once you stop thinking in terms of genre and start thinking in terms of vibration, rhythm and texture, those transitions become quite natural. The quieter pieces are equally important because they allow the listener to breathe. Silence, space and suspension are also forms of rhythm. Without those moments, the more intense passages wouldn’t have the same impact. So there is structure, but it usually emerges after experimentation rather than before it. Both of your other projects—Raja Kirik (Johanes “Mo’ong” Santoso Pribadi with Yennu Ariendra) and Scotch Rolex (Shigeru Ishihara)—have always challenged musical categories, but Takkak Takkak seems driven as much by joy, humour and curiosity as by experimentation itself. In a musical landscape that often takes experimental music very seriously, especially within an ethnological framework, does playfulness become a creative strategy for opening listeners up to unfamiliar sounds and ways of listening? Johanes “Mo’ong” Santos Pribadi: I think play is a very serious activity. When people hear the word “experimental,” they sometimes expect something difficult or intellectual. But curiosity usually begins with play. Children don’t separate learning from playing; they explore because they’re curious. I think music can work in the same way. Humour also helps remove fear. If listeners feel that they have to understand everything intellectually, they might close themselves off. But if they can laugh, dance or simply become curious, they’re already listening differently. In projects like Raja Kirik and Takkak Takkak, we’re interested in transformation rather than preservation. Traditional culture has always contained humour, absurdity, masks, tricksters and moments of chaos. Those aspects are just as important as the ceremonial or sacred ones. So playfulness isn’t there to make the work lighter. It’s another way of opening possibilities. Once people stop worrying about categories traditional versus contemporary, ritual versus club music, acoustic versus electronic they become more willing to experience sound on its own terms. (Interview by Gianmarco Del Re)

items.body: Wann immer von Post-Punk die Rede ist, sind vor allem Bands wie Gang of Four, Joy Division, The Fall oder Public Image Ltd. gemeint. Musik mit scharfkantigen – angefunkt zwar und doch zu trocken, um wirklich zu grooven – Gitarrenriffs und straffen Rhythmussektionen, über die jemand schreisingt. Kaum jemand aber wird an die Band denken, die den eigentlichen Geist von Post-Punk am deutlichsten verkörperte: This Heat. Im HHV Shop kaufenThis HeatThis Heatab 31.99€ Schon Punk wollte Rock’n’Roll zerstören. Doch reduzierte er ihn letztlich lediglich auf seine Kernelemente: Blues-basierte Akkordfolgen, Verstärker auf elf, absolute Hemmungslosigkeit. Post-Punk übernahm den Do-it-yourself-Spirit von Punk und verband ihn mit rigorosem Experimentalismus, der viele Rock-Klischees hinter sich ließ. In diesem Sinne waren This Heat Post-Punk, bevor überhaupt Punk aufkam: Als sie sich Anfang 1976 gründeten, hatten die Sex Pistols noch nicht in der Lesser Free Trade Hall in Manchester gespielt. Schlagzeuger Charles Hayward war Mitglied der Canterbury-Prog-Rock-Band Quiet Sun des Roxy-Music-Gitarristen Phil Manzanera, als der Multi-Instrumentalist Charles Bullen als Ersatz für den Bandleader hinzustieß. Nach der Auflösung von Quiet Sun gründeten die beiden mit dem Nicht-Musiker Gareth Williams ein Trio. This Heat mieteten sich im Kühlraum einer Fleischpastetenfabrik in Brixton ein und nahmen dort Musik auf. Ihr erstes Demo überzeugte John Peel, für ihre selbstbetitelte Debüt-LP brauchten sie aber zwei Jahre. Freie Experimente über Proto-Sampling This Heat erschien 1979 und damit im selben Jahr wie Unknown Pleasures, Entertainment!, Live at the Witch Trials und Metal Box, wird aber kaum jemals im Zusammenhang mit diesen Alben erwähnt. Das ergibt irgendwie auch Sinn: Die elf Stücke, deren erstes aus 47 Sekunden Stille besteht, wurden aus verschiedenen Studio- und Live-Aufnahmen zusammengestellt, die die drei zu Collagen verarbeiteten. Im Endergebnis ähnelt kaum etwas davon Songs. Selbst die Stücke, die einen Text haben, ergeben herzlich wenig Sinn. Als alle Rock’n’Roll zerstören wollten, gelang das allein This Heat. This Heat war, anders formuliert, das radikalste Post-Punk-Album seiner Zeit. Nach dem Opener »Testcard« (einem von zwei Stücken mit diesem Titel) bricht die Band in »Horizontal Hold« aus, ein dröhnendes Ungetüm mit viel Bass, gelegentlichen Dub-Elementen und verstimmten Funk-Gitarren, die The Pop Group wie die Jackson Five klingen lassen. Strukturen? Kaum zu erkennen, stattdessen nur Veränderungen des Intensitätslevels. Dazu: ein Gitarrensolo, das die richtigen Lehren aus »Boredom« von den Buzzcocks gezogen hatte. Ihrem Motto »All possible processes. All channels open. Twenty-four-hour alert« folgend arbeiten sich This Heat weiter durch »Not Waving«, einer 7½-minütigen Etüde in der Verschmelzung von Musique-concrète-Techniken mit einer Art von Songwriting. Das unheimliche Soundscaping veranschaulicht den dekonstruktivistischen Ansatz des Trios: Sie collagierten und manipulierten Aufnahmen in einer Art von primitivem Proto-Sampling, während sie mit freier Improvisation experimentierten, wie auch »Water« bekräftigt.  Mehr Manifest als Album Dank seines fieberhaften Drummings, den vergleichsweise konventionellen Gitarrenmelodien und seinem gequälten Sprechgesang erinnert »Twilight Furniture« beinahe an Joy Division oder andere Zeitgenoss:innen, doch stellt schon das nächste Stücke ein erneute Zäsur dar: »24 Track Loop« ist ein visionäres Experiment mit quasi-gesampelten, angedubbten Breakbeats, die von kreischenden Akkorden kontrapunktiert werden – eine Art Bindeglied zwischen Karlheinz Stockhausen, Muslimgauze und Jungle womöglich. Unerhörte Musik wie diese bewies: Als alle Rock’n’Roll zerstören wollten, gelang das allein This Heat. Die dahinterstehende Attitüde prägte auch das Drone-inspirierte »Diet of Worms«, eine Collage mit dem treffenden Titel »Music Like Escaping Gas«, den free-jazzigen Freakout »Rainforest« sowie den vorausschauenden Industrial-/Neofolk-Hybrid »The Fall of Saigon«. Das zweite »Testcard«-Stück setzt mit repetitivem Feedback einen unbequemen, unmusikalischen Schlusspunkt unter eine unbequeme und nicht immer musikalische Platte.  This Heat wurzelten in genau jener Musikszene, gegen die Punk aufbegehrte. Doch noch bevor Punk überhaupt in Schwung kam, ging diese Band einen Schritt weiter als jene Gruppen, die bereits verkündet hatten, weiter gehen zu wollen als Punk. This Heat kann kaum als Album bezeichnet werden. War es aber war: ein Manifest – ein Versprechen, die Grenzen des Machbaren weiter zu verschieben als alle anderen. Und obwohl sie nicht zu den berühmtesten aller Post-Punk-Platten gehört: Sie ist die ultimative Post-Punk-Platte.
items._cn_summary: 这张1979年的同名专辑被视为后朋克最激进的实验之作，比同年的《Unknown Pleasures》和《Metal Box》走得更远。This Heat在布里克斯顿一家肉饼工厂的冷藏室中录制，将工作室与现场录音拼贴成十一首曲目，首曲竟是四十七秒的空白。乐队将磁带拼贴、具体音乐技法与杜比元素、解构的放克吉他相融合，结构松散，歌词几乎无意义，强度变化取代了传统曲式。他们沿用"所有可能的流程，所有通道开放，全天候警戒"的信条，在朋克试图摧毁摇滚之前就已开始解构音乐本身，是那个时代最具实验精神的乐队作品之一。

items.body: This, unfortunately, digital only release is a treat, a future hidden gem, probably, for all those interested in the free thinking ethos of improvisation. Jack Wright is on the saxophones (alto and soprano, I believe) and Bennett on the drums and some other percussive objects. Tourne is comprised of three long tracks, each over or around the ten minute mark, and presents their take of playing live. When I’m saying that this is their take, I mean it literally. Even though there’s a certain generational gap when it comes to those two players’ age, they both refer to the early days of free improvisation (we could comment that those days where having jazz as a reference but nothing more) when a new language –every sound is possible and only the players are liable for it- was being formed and presented through playing live. This is how both of them antagonize with their preconceived ideas about playing music: by challenging each other to go further and further, even beyond the margins of what is sound, what is music, what is that should be heard from percussion and saxophones. This is not their first collaboration but, still, they sound fresh and willing not to fall in the shaky ground of presenting “good” music-not even playing “challenging” and “adventurous” stuff. They just are themselves, staying true to the basic ethos of free improvisation. Trying, at least, to present something new each time. Bennett’s playing is agile, feverish and energetic as never before. He seems to be enjoying himself as he releases low level percussive barrages. Wright, restless as ever, follows but also runs in parallel releasing saxophone sounds as if his respected instrument is made of rubber and can bend and displace notes and phrases. I’m not sure if I made my point clear out to you, but this is a joy to experience release that has to be, at least, listened by a lot of people. Tourne by Jack Wright and Ben Bennett Fot.isn Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由萨克斯手Jack Wright与鼓手Ben Bennett合作，收录三首时长约十分钟左右的即兴作品。两人以早期自由即兴的精神为根基，拒绝任何预设的音乐观念，在演奏中不断挑战声音的边界——超越何为声音、何为音乐、何为萨克斯与打击乐应发出的声响。Wright的中音与高音萨克斯被演奏得如同可弯曲变形的橡胶，音符与乐句被不断扭曲和位移；Bennett的鼓击敏捷而狂热，释放出低强度的打击乐冲击波。两人虽存在年龄差距，但合作态度保持新鲜，拒绝落入呈现"好听"音乐的陷阱，也不刻意追求"挑战性"标签。评论指出，这种纯粹的即兴态度让作品具备内在的新鲜感，每一次演奏都试图呈现此前未有的东西，是自由即兴精神的忠实体现。

items.body: Nagoya’s leftfield electronic scene has recently garnered interest from the international music press. This is chiefly thanks to the efforts of producer and all-around scenester Yuya Abe (abentis). abentis has been an associate of Facta & K-LONE’s Wisdom Teeth label since 2021. After a chance encounter with Facta on the platform formerly known as Twitter, Wisdom Teeth featured abentis’ track “Bicycle” in their 2022 compilation To Illustrate. Earlier this year, abentis curated a compilation of Nagoya talent for Wisdom Teeth titled nagoyaka na kaze / 和やかな風 (quiet wind). Entries oscillate from woodblock percussion-fronted minimal house to rootsical UK bass. Now the artist returns with his debut album Dim Grow, the first physical release on his fledgling 2++ label, which he plans to use to promote the Nagoya scene. Dim Grow is fairly short, clocking in at just 41 minutes, but contains enough unique ideas to fill a longer work. “Separate” opens the album with an unhurried cavalcade of brassy splashes and arpeggiation evoking Italian experimentalist Caterina Barbieri. It segues into “In Memories,” the longest piece on Dim Grow at just over nine minutes. It’s maybe too long; physically modeled kalimba dominates the first 90 seconds until the rising tedium is suddenly leavened with bass. A Steve Reich influence looms large for the remaining seven-plus minutes, a twinkling tropical variation on the American minimalist composer’s studied drift between melodic and rhythmic phrases. Especially compelling are the reverberant marimba stabs near the end with a series of showy decay accents—essentially the audio equivalent of crisp serifs. “Far Enough” and “Lune,” channel some of abentis’ Japanese influences, particularly goopy analog synth leads reminiscent of Thousand Knives-era Ryuichi Sakamoto and Haruomi Hosono’s late 70s prog-psych experiments—albums like Cochin Moon and Paraiso that détourned western exotica-kitsch. “Far Enough” is particularly mischievous; one motif is teasing a trap-style snare line only to collapse it into a wash of static. Forays into dance music shade the second half of Dim Grow. The swung 4/4 of “Lune” could earn it a place in a more open-minded house or techno set. “Eachpath” susurrates with the restlessness of 2010s deconstructed club artists like Jam City and Lee Gamble, but grounded in the rhythmic and harmonic grooves of 90s intelligent techno acts like B12, Ken Ishii, and LA Synthesis. “Circulation” is the shortest track on the album and may also be the most dance-oriented: bedroom techno with dubby mallet percussion running in opposite directions over male voices that lie on the threshold of discernibility. It’s easy to envision this music issuing from the soundsystem of a chic Nagoya(ka) sake bar, and if abentis gets his way, audiophile venues the world over. (Marcello Ursic)

items._cn_summary: 名古屋制作人abentis的首张专辑展现了对左翼电子音乐的深厚探索。专辑融合了极简主义作曲家的复调思维——尤其是Steve Reich的渐进式相位位移手法——与当代实验电子舞曲的解构语汇。开篇以铜管质感的合成器琶音与物理建模卡林巴琴引入，贯穿全片的马林巴琴与模块化合成器纹理构建出层次丰富的声学空间。后半部分转向俱乐部语境，在4/4拍摇摆节奏中融入去结构化俱乐部的不安感与九十年代智能techno的节奏逻辑。萨摩摩风格的模拟合成器主音段落向坂本龙一与细野晴彦的七十年代末实验致敬，trap军鼓元素的戏谑解构则体现了扎实的舞曲解构意识。作为名古屋地下音乐场景的推动者，abentis在这张四十一分钟的专辑中呈现了密度颇高的跨界文本。

items.body: Erik Jarl has been extremely prolific for more than twenty years now. With this new release, he has created another album that serves as a follow-up to a trilogy focusing on the brain and nervous system; the title of the new work speaks for itself. Two tracks exceed the twenty-minute mark—a characteristic feature of the Swedish artist’s work by now. In my view, however, they often run a little too long, resulting in a lack of variation within the compositions. I am therefore more impressed by the shorter tracks, even though these still clock in at over six and eight minutes, respectively. Here, Jarl creates a mysterious sonic universe using deep, vibrating analogue tones layered with numerous effects, giving the sound a darker quality than usual. The sustained tones often have a hypnotic effect; at times, they sound almost misty, evoking an imaginary astral dimension. Certain passages possess a strong visual quality that sparks the imagination and totally fit within the realms of Cinematic and Dark-Ambient music. Despite finding two of the tracks somewhat overlong, I consider this one of Jarl’s finest works, with the magnificent “Electrical Impulse 3/4” standing out as a particular highlight. (Rating:8). The album was released on 23 February 2026 on Zoharum and runs four tracks titled “Electrical Impulse – 1/4” through “Electrical Impulse – 4/4”, filling close to sixty minutes. It is available on CD in a six-panel digipack, on cassette and as a download. Listen to “Electrical Impulse ¾”: Electrical Impulse – 3/4 by Jarl About Jarl Jarl is the Dark Ambient and Cinematic project of Swedish artist Erik Jarl, who works from Norrkoping in Ostergotland. The project has been active for more than two decades and is built around a consistent formula of analog sound treatments and slowly repeating, hypnotic passages. Erik Jarl is also known for his work in IRM and Skin Area. Side-Line first covered the project with the double album “Negative Rotation / Intensive Fracture” in 2018. Jarl has released albums on the Polish label Zoharum on a near-annual basis since, including “Inner Domain” (2020), “Hyperacusis” (2021), “Phonophobia” (2022), “Mindrotation” (2023) and “Isolation Colours” (2024), alongside “Spectrum Confusion” on Reverse Alignment in 2022. The trilogy referred to here consists of “Neurotransmitters Sphere Music”, “Receptor Radiation” and “Synapse Variation Report”, released on 7 April 2025, three Zoharum albums that share both theme and sound and that deal in turn with neurotransmitters, receptors and synapses. Zoharum describes “Nerve Cell Threads Electronics” as an informal fourth part of that series, and the label states the tracks carry a darker tone than the earlier instalments while keeping the sequencer-based, analogue approach.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是瑞典艺术家Jarl以大脑与神经系统为题材的系列第四部（前作为2025年发行的神经递质、受体与突触三部曲），共四轨，总长近六十分钟，其中两首超过二十分钟。整体采用深沉的模拟合成器长音配合大量效果处理，在其惯有的催眠式循环结构上营造出比以往更暗的色彩。评论者认为超长曲目内部变化略显不足，篇幅更紧凑的段落反而更具张力，听感如雾气弥漫的星际空间，富有强烈的画面感与电影感，落在暗氛围与电影音乐的交汇地带。其中第四首被特别推荐为整张专辑的亮点。作品延续了模拟音色与序列器驱动的长期路线，呈现出统一而克制的美学取向。

items.body: Prairiewolf has been blending together the adjacent worlds of ambient country, kosmische musik and minimalist spiritual jazz for a handful of years now, yet on this, their third full-length LP, they appear to have finely tuned their craft and developed a sound that is truly their own. Available now on Centripetal Force, Zone Poems finds the trio of Stefan Beck (guitar, baritone guitar and lap steel), Jeremy Erwin (organ, mellotron, guitar and synth) and Tyler Wilcox (bass guitar) leaning into shadowy, tightly-constructed grooves that easily make you feel like you’re floating above your stereo. From the cyberpunk noir meditation that is “The St. Vrain Method” to the wistfully dreamy cosmic Americana textures of “Dream Logic,” this is the band firing on all cylinders. While their past two records were also fantastic in their own right, this album if their first that doesn’t feel like an experiment for what this melding of disparate styles could sound like. Instead, this is a record full of assurance with solidly intentional compositions from a band that genuinely knows itself. That being said, of course, the album still feels loose enough that it appears to have plenty of moments of free improvisation. This is especially true on “Modifications” and “Burning Edges.” Being partially recorded live, I’m sure there is far more spontaneity throughout, but the group is so well-seasoned now, it would be difficult to discern one way or another (the sign of an absolutely cracking jazz band, as my jazz studies professors would always say). While dipping into tastes of exotica lounge (“Viewpoint”) and even hints of electronica (“Everything Ascending”) with streams of flute-like mellotron, waves of melty lap steel and astral guitar meditations drifting over retro drum machine beats, this is a record for a vast variety of different heads with various unique tastes of music. Being their strongest release to date, I for one cannot wait to hear where this band goes to next. Grab your copy on vinyl, CD or digital (with a bonus disc of early sessions!) from Centripetal Force today. -KH Speaking of Centripetal Force, have you also heard the brand new SOMA Kirtan album that cae out on the label back in June? items.album: 注目の一枚｜マックス・デヴロー『レジスタンス』｜齋藤俊夫
items.excerpt: マックス・デヴロー『レジスタンス』 Max Devereaux “Resistance” ALM Records/有限会社コジマ録音 2026年7月7日発売 Text by 齋藤俊夫(Toshio Saito) マックス・デヴロー：『レジスタンス』 作曲およびエレクトリック・ギター独奏によるリアライゼーション(2026) （エレクトリック・ギター独奏による自作自演） Resistance I: Tension Resistance II: Duration Resistance III: Friction Resistance IV: Feedback Resistance V: Constraint 現代においてレジスタンス＝抵抗はいかにして可能なのか、とくに芸術によるレジスタンス＝抵抗はいかにあるべきでいかにして可能なのか。 例えばそれは1969年、アメリカのウッドストックでのジミ・ヘンドリックスがアメリカ国歌『星条旗』をエレキギターの轟音で変奏した事例が芸術による抵抗の見事な一例だとも思える。 あるいはベルリンの壁崩壊直後の1989年ベルリンでの、バーンスタイン指揮によるベートー
items.body: マックス・デヴロー『レジスタンス』 Max Devereaux “Resistance” ALM Records/有限会社コジマ録音 2026年7月7日発売 Text by 齋藤俊夫(Toshio Saito) マックス・デヴロー：『レジスタンス』 作曲およびエレクトリック・ギター独奏によるリアライゼーション(2026) （エレクトリック・ギター独奏による自作自演） Resistance I: Tension Resistance II: Duration Resistance III: Friction Resistance IV: Feedback Resistance V: Constraint 現代においてレジスタンス＝抵抗はいかにして可能なのか、とくに芸術によるレジスタンス＝抵抗はいかにあるべきでいかにして可能なのか。 例えばそれは1969年、アメリカのウッドストックでのジミ・ヘンドリックスがアメリカ国歌『星条旗』をエレキギターの轟音で変奏した事例が芸術による抵抗の見事な一例だとも思える。 あるいはベルリンの壁崩壊直後の1989年ベルリンでの、バーンスタイン指揮によるベートーヴェンの第9番交響曲が「自由の歌」として数万人の観衆と共に歌われた時、芸術による抵抗が花開いたとも思える。 しかし、果たしてその「抵抗」は「本当の抵抗」となるのだろうか？ 何にせよ「本当の～～」をつければその題材は「本当の～～」ではないかもしれない、と簡単に疑問に付して知的優位（？）に立てるという批評・言論術は知りながらも、筆者はここで「本当の抵抗」という言葉を、「現在の日本含む世界における全的な抵抗」たり得るのか、というごくナイーヴな意味であえて使いたい。 （筆者は治安維持法への何個目かの一里塚と見ている）日本の「国旗損壊罪法」に対して、ジミ・ヘンドリックスがアメリカ国歌『星条旗』を変奏したように国旗を変容させた「芸術」は、既にして日本では「罪」となるのは間違いないが、さらには国旗の変容が「罪」とならなかった場合をもって、日本政府の「寛容」を示すことにはならないだろうか。例えば東京都に現れたバンクシーの絵画が小池都知事によって「かわいい」と称賛されて彼女の手に抱かれたように、変容された国旗が「かわいい」と称賛されて政府のものとなることはないだろうか。権力の愚劣さは、権力をより強くさえするが、決してその力を弱めはしない。愚劣さは狡猾な強さと共存する。 人類史上に名を残すであろうほどの愚劣なるかの米国大統領ドナルド・トランプが、もしベルリンの壁崩壊を祝す演奏会に立ち会ったとして、彼は「自由の歌」を斉唱しなかったであろうか？ ベートーヴェンの人類愛は人類の一人たるトランプをも包んで「自由」を「歓喜」する歌として響いたのではないだろうか？ 彼は自分が「自由」を大声で語り、歌うことに何の疑問も抱かないであろう。彼は本当に自分が米国と世界を「自由」にしていると信じており、周りの人間、さらには米国民、そしてさらには全世界人民が自分の「自由」を憧憬するべきだ、と考えているであろう。それが権力の愚劣なる強さである。 その権力の愚劣なる強さへのレジスタンス＝抵抗として、今回取り上げるマックス・デヴロー『レジスタンス』は存在する。ごく簡単な規則による図形楽譜（CDをかけながら読譜すれば解読するのは容易だ）による「物理的抵抗」「形式的抵抗」「方法論的抵抗」の3つを眼目として作曲されている。第4曲「フィードバック」のみエレキギターの轟音がうねるが、その他の曲はポツリポツリと単音が静寂と交代交代で鳴らされるのみ。そこから音楽的快楽・愉悦を得ようとするのは難しい。さらには、この一聴して不条理・無形式な音楽に「意味」を読み取ろうとすることも難しい。だが、その無快楽、不条理、無形式な音の群れにレジスタンス＝抵抗の契機は宿る。快楽、条理、形式の求心的な力に対して、本作の無快楽、不条理、無形式の遠心的な力は、権力を権力たらしめる求心力への抵抗となる。権力に対して、没権力的無関心を決め込むのではなく、反権力的遠心力を発生させ、そこからレジスタンス＝抵抗を始めようとする。それがこのマックス・デヴロー『レジスタンス』の「政治的」可能性だ。 全世界が狂っていく中でのレジスタンス＝抵抗を試みようとする全ての音楽人にとって、本CDは一つの階（きざはし）となるだろう。 (2026/8/15)

items._cn_summary: Max Devereaux《Resistance》是一张电吉他独奏专辑，五首作品以极简规则驱动的图形乐谱谱写，分别从张力、持续、摩擦、反馈与约束五个维度探讨抵抗的可能。评论者将其置于艺术与权力对抗的思想脉络中，从Hendrix在Woodstock改奏美国国歌、Bernstein指挥贝多芬第九于柏林墙边唱响，到当下日本国旗损毁罪法引发的压抑氛围。专辑中除第四曲以电吉他轰鸣的反馈铺陈外，其余多以静默中零星散落的单音构成，音乐快感与可解读的意义均被刻意抽离。评论者认为，这种无快感、无条理、无形式的离心力本身即是对权力向心力的抵抗，为当下尝试以音乐介入现实的创作者提供了一份可资参照的阶梯。

items.album: Pareidolia
items.excerpt: ​Jake Muir back on enmossed with an album of "all goop’d up ambient bits from black and death metal records..." Stirring together and re-seasoning the stickiest bits of his favorite metal records, Jake Muir dreams up an atmospheric, bathhouse-ready reaction to the most extreme soundscapes, enhancing lysergic moments to... more
items.body:
​Jake Muir back on enmossed with an album of "all goop’d up ambient bits from black and death metal records..."

Stirring together and re-seasoning the stickiest bits of his favorite metal records, Jake Muir dreams up an atmospheric, bathhouse-ready reaction to the most extreme soundscapes, enhancing lysergic moments to bring out parallels with gear from Coil, :zoviet*france:, Pinkcourtesyphone, Main or even Ulver.

What makes music heavy, exactly? Is it simply the volume itself, or could it be the spread of culturally assured elements that make our skin prickle and our ears focus in on fight or flight terrors like animalistic cries, rattling chains or grim liturgical chants? Muir has been fascinated with rock music since he was a kid, poring over byzantine, maximal offerings from bands like Meshuggah and Nine Inch Nails. And it's an obsession that's led him through the bullrushes of death and black metal, genres that often veer into experimental territory, crossing the streams with industrial, noise and of course dark ambient. 'Pareidolia' is Muir's celebration of bleak metal's nightmarish atmospheres, sounds that make the blast beats, hoarse vocals and smudgy chords sound even more substantial without technically being loud. 

Pulled away from their context, these textures are compellingly theatrical: whooshing ice winds, creaking branches, scraping metal, chiming bells, plucked strings and heaving drones. They're sounds that situate us in death and black metal's ancestral Northern homeland, in some remote cabin hemmed in by harsh weather and prowling wolves. So heard on their own, it's predictable that we end up trudging similarly cinematic territory as the "dark ambient" forebears like Lustmord and Deathprod or more recent exponents Svarte Greiner and Lussuria. Muir's idea for the album was a little different; spurred on by his back-and-forth with Even Caminiti on 2022's ace 'Talisman' album, he attempted to use these bleak fantasies to power the kind of heady, sexually-charged moods that goosebump'd thru his breakout 'Bathhouse Blues' without losing the folk horror cogitation of last year's sacred meditation 'Campana Sonans'.

In fact, 'Pareidolia' is supposed to play like an illusion - even the name of the album is a reference to this. Muir wants to rope us in with familiarity before waltzing us through a parallel history of isolationist, industrial ambient gear, the kind of guitar-muddling, metal-aware grot that linked Nocturnal Emissions and Z'EV and Robert Hampson's electroacoustic rock duo Main with heady set texts from Eno, Daniel Lanois, Stuart Dempster and Steve Roach. The album isn't just a DJ set of the quiet moments from recent RYM metal side-quests, as you'll hear as soon as you plug into opener 'Beithir'. Between the blustery soundscapes and knife-sharpening SFX, there's a melodic pulse and echoing oscillations that wouldn't sound out of place on an IASOS record, while the dense, Sunn O)))-adjacent bass drone takes on a surprisingly humid character, winding itself around weightless pads and spirit breaths.

On 'Unholy Apparitions' meanwhile, Muir's phantasmagorical scratches and chirps are re-fashioned into brain-tickling ASMR purrs that surf across white noise clouds and low end rumbles, while on  'Cathedral of Decay', environments that sound as if they've been recorded in a damp crypt are shifted to the sauna, each minor key flourish transformed into a furtive glance to the side. It's the air that's heavy, not the music itself.
items._genre: dark ambient / drone / industrial / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: Jake Muir 在 enmossed 厂牌发行的新专辑《Pareidolia》是一次对极端金属声响的解构与重塑。他从黑金属和死亡金属唱片中提取最具氛围感的纹理——呼啸的寒风、吱嘎作响的树枝、金属刮擦声、钟鸣与拨弦——将它们从原始语境中剥离，编织成一种适合桑拿冥想的粘稠氛围质地。评论将其与 Coil、Ulver、Lustmord、Deathprod 等前辈的作品相提并论，指出专辑试图在'黑暗氛围'的传统阴郁中注入更具感官性与仪式感的情绪张力，开篇曲《Beithir》中可见的旋律脉搏与低频嗡鸣暗示了与 Sunn O))) 相邻的重量感。这张专辑延续了他与 Even Caminiti 在《Talisman》中的合作脉络，同时回溯了他早期《Bathhouse Blues》的肉体感与《Campana Sonans》的民俗恐怖沉思，构建出一部关于孤立意象与声音幻觉的平行历史。

items.album: Sworx
items.excerpt: The incomparable Winos dial-up a near-future fraught with glitching techno x surrealist folk artefacts supposed by mainman Morgan Buckley and his pal Ben Donohoe, a 12-track guess-again sprawl ranging from Arthur Russell-esque mood music to screwed Aphex jams. Under the auspices of “Sworx”, an omniscient dialup... more
items.body:
The incomparable Winos dial-up a near-future fraught with glitching techno x surrealist folk artefacts supposed by mainman Morgan Buckley and his pal Ben Donohoe, a 12-track guess-again sprawl ranging from Arthur Russell-esque mood music to screwed Aphex jams.

Under the auspices of “Sworx”, an omniscient dialup modem, they parse coded waveforms in a discrete filing system, combing and recombining its data in a dozen buzzing post-techno chimeras and itchy electro jams. It’s instant classic Wah Wah Wino, freakishly playful and exerting odd sidespins on familiar styles and patterns with a ludic moxie that makes all their music so appealing.

The ‘Sworx’ system speaks its piece in a unique voice of detuned twangs and ululating electronic rhythms, shifting mercurial from what sounds like The Necks doing electro with a prepared piano on ‘OpportuniXt’, to a standout electro zinger with early AFXian vocaloids on ‘The System Works’, and Plone-esque key clatter on ‘dxmmy. pxtsy. rolodex’, thru a centrepiece calling to mind Oval’s most sublime on ‘breathwx (half_life)’. 

‘Western_intel [ frontier 2056 ]’ projects an unusually optimist vision of futurism, less techno dread, more cyber-pastoral, and the trip continues to wend from displaced, outernational folk in ‘Langley Prayer Room 9’, to a masterstroke of pitchbent club sauce in ‘sWORxism_noclocks_notimekept’ that tickles rarest pleasure centres with its piquant wrong-notes and gooey groove.

Collect them all!
items._genre: experimental electronic / glitch / post-techno / electro / surrealist folk
items._cn_summary: 爱尔兰二人组 Morgan Buckley 与 Ben Donohoe 以虚构的调制解调器系统「Sworx」为概念框架，编解码十二首风格游离的电子曲目。专辑在解构的科技声响中穿插超现实民谣碎片，以去音准的拨弦与电子节奏的交替推进。曲目从近似 Arthur Russell 的氛围小品，到 Aphex Twin 早期的扭曲声码器人声，再到 Oval 式的数字拼贴，构成一份后科技舞曲的混合档案。评论特别提及几首高光：开场以预置钢琴模拟电声骨架，中段中心曲接近 Oval 最空灵之作，尾声的弯曲音高俱乐部律动以错误音符与黏稠律动触发稀有快感，整体呈现出一种田园牧歌式的乐观未来主义，与技术恐惧叙事形成对照。

items.album: In Plain Sight
items.excerpt: After marinading in the archive for 30 years, Regis unleashes a spicy batch of hypnotic meat motors hailing from an early crest of his powers, available for the first time. It’s no real secret that Karl O’Connor dispensed dozens of 12”s in the late ‘90s under pseudonyms that are still coming to light. Since 2003, when his energies were... more
items.body:
After marinading in the archive for 30 years, Regis unleashes a spicy batch of hypnotic meat motors hailing from an early crest of his powers, available for the first time.

It’s no real secret that Karl O’Connor dispensed dozens of 12”s in the late ‘90s under pseudonyms that are still coming to light. Since 2003, when his energies were more focussed on the BMB duo with Surgeon, he’s really pushed the techno framework into fascinating new shapes. But, like legion others, we’re all still here for his signature early brand of girder-strength bangers, as spotted ‘In Plain Sight’ here.

The title tune plays to his classic style of white knuckle tension and kinky canter with a discordant, panic-raising lead and warehouse-ready pound, whilst an early, EBM-tooled zinger ‘We Said No’ appears via two unreleased versions; a nastier alt. 1 galvanisation, and an August 1996 mix kitted with a rictus hi-hat backbone. 

Finally he dispenses an August 1996 mix of ‘Backwards Man’, which doesn’t appear on the EP of the same name nor on ‘Hard Eduction 1931’ sets, and fully endures on modern floors for its mind-bending, pitching lead and dead slinky, brutalist gait.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了Regis（Karl O'Connor）自九十年代末存档至今的多首早期未发行作品，呈现出他创作巅峰初期的标志性风格。标题曲以高张力节拍驱动，不和谐的主导音色制造出恐慌感，配合仓库式的强劲低音冲击，展现出经典的硬核techno骨架。'We Said No'的两版混音透露出EBM工业根源，扭曲的合成器线条与金属化节奏交织，其中1996年8月版本以抽搐式踩镫构建筋骨。'Backwards Man'的同期混音此前从未出现在同名EP或'Hard Eduction 1931'合辑中，迷幻式俯仰主导旋律配合冷酷滑溜的低音节奏，具备在当代舞池持续生效的强度。这些曲目共同勾勒出英国地下techno场景在世纪之交对工业原料与舞池功能性的极致探索。

items.album: The Rest Is My Ghost
items.excerpt: Pushing back against "Acid Nostalgia", Lawrence English dreams of a moonlit future on 'The Rest is My Ghost', bringing in assistance from a heap of collaborators, including members of The Necks, Swans, Mats Gustafsson, Rully Shabara and Lena Ito for a strong set that’s more curdled than harmonious, and all the better for... more
items.body:
Pushing back against "Acid Nostalgia", Lawrence English dreams of a moonlit future on 'The Rest is My Ghost', bringing in assistance from a heap of collaborators, including members of The Necks, Swans, Mats Gustafsson, Rully Shabara and Lena Ito for a strong set that’s more curdled than harmonious, and all the better for it.

'The Rest is My Ghost' is more radical and political than anything we’ve heard from English in a while, more in line with 2014's charged 'Wilderness of Mirrors' and its brilliant follow-up 'Cruel Optimism’. Provoked by a conversation with Adam Curtis and driven by texts from Mark Fisher, JG Ballard, Katsuhiro Otomo, Franco Berardi, Kate Crawford and Alexie Yurchak and cultural architectural realities like the loss of Los Angeles' signature street lamps and Japan's Metabolists, English searches for a "political projection of nostalgia" that he can subsequently rupture. "Like acid poured onto a surface," he writes. "this use of nostalgia seeks to erode the complexity and texture of lived connection and longing, which has until recently guided contemplations of nostalgia."

He's talking about the difference between dreaming of your own past and being sold a neatly packaged pseudo-reality, its highs and lows smoothed over for easier consumption. To represent this concept musically, English moves away from dense distortions and instead collects up instrumental performances from a wide swathe of notable players including The Necks’ Chris Abrahams and Tony Buck, Madeleine Cocolas, Mats Gustafsson, Thor Harris, Heinz Riegler and Swans’ Norman Westberg among an all-star lineup. Perusing the personnel list and projecting your expectations on the material is part of the process and so English obscures everything purposefully, shrouding the instrumentation in reverb and gusts of hazed interference. If seeing names like pedal steel player Chuck Johnson gives you pause, that's the point. English engages in his own hauntological process, extracting the essence from the stems and imprinting it on his soundscapes. He's not eroding the material, but rather searching out the triggers that play on the imagination, inspiring futures that have never been more difficult to grasp.

And if it sounds dark, it's really not supposed to. Listen through the nocturnal hums and gentle, thrumming ambiance and you'll discover more than you bargained for - even a glimmer of hope. The result is a record that lands somewhere between classic Vangelis, Les Disques du Crépuscule's post-classical gear, Eno's fourth world experiments with John Hassell and Alan Lamb's influential sound art. In a world of drone and ambient musics that increasingly feel honed to numb the senses, this one tugs at something much deeper and more elemental.
items._genre: ambient / drone / experimental / sound art / post-classical
items._cn_summary: Lawrence English 在这张专辑中延续其声响艺术的脉络，联合多位跨界音乐人——包括 The Necks 成员、Swans 吉他手、Mats Gustafsson 等——以协作演奏为素材，通过混响与干扰层将其遮蔽、重组，构建出一种凝聚性的声音景观。乐评指出，专辑的创作动机源于对"酸蚀怀旧"的批判思考：区分个人真实的过去与被工业化的伪记忆之间的差异。文本上受 Mark Fisher、JG Ballard、Kate Crawford 等理论家的影响，涉及洛杉矶街灯消失、日本代谢派建筑等文化议题。音乐上，专辑被比作 Vangelis、Eno 与 Hassell 的第四世界实验以及 Alan Lamb 的声音艺术，呈现出夜间嗡鸣与低频震荡的质感，在黑暗氛围中保留希望余地，对当代趋于麻木的无人机与氛围音乐构成反思性的回应。
