items.excerpt: KAKUHAN / Sara Udon cellist Yuki Nakagawa takes a solemn yet dreamlike debut solo bow on the Unheard of Hope label - home to Mabe Fratti - intently focussed on holistic examinations of his instrument, revealing its inner voices via various raw and processed strategies. RIYL Leila Bordreuil, Ecka Mordecai, Hildur... more
items.body:
KAKUHAN / Sara Udon cellist Yuki Nakagawa takes a solemn yet dreamlike debut solo bow on the Unheard of Hope label - home to Mabe Fratti -  intently focussed on holistic examinations of his instrument, revealing its inner voices via various raw and processed strategies. RIYL Leila Bordreuil, Ecka Mordecai, Hildur Guðnadóttir, Okkyung Lee or Judith Hamann.

It's hard to explain just how eerily familiar Nakagawa's playing is, but you'll understand what we mean after hearing just a few moments of 'You Haze - I'. We've grown fully accustomed to the way Nakagawa handles the cello without even realizing it, absorbing his technique on records from KAKUHAN, his duo project with Koshihiro Hino, and Sara Udon alongside Naarm duo CS + Kreme. The way Nakagawa rests his bow between tones, picking up animated off-notes that make his sustained drones sound deep, dark and resonant, is genuinely personal, identifiable immediately. And although that aspect of his performance is front and center on his debut's opening track, it's the additional elements that tip us over the edge: the discreet, theremin-like wails that occupy a space just in the corner of the composition. 

After establishing his signature, Nakagawa veers away from his own convention sharply on 'CHU-MA', plucking the cello's strings and bending them as if they were attached to a koto. It's all remarkably stark at first, without much enhancement from Nakagawa's pedals and he slowly teases in different sounds that widen the instrument's range: woody creaks, knocks and growls that fill out its body and piercing overtones that go beyond the usual confines of the strings. Somehow, even using all these extended techniques, Nakagawa still manages to make music that's effortlessly enjoyable. It's bumpy, self-consciously experimental material, but not without roots - maybe best compared to Fred Frith's 'Guitar Solos' or Hans Reichel's 'The Death of the Rare Bird'.

There's even a prettiness to tracks like 'Upper and under the bridge' and 'You Haze - II' that betrays Nakagawa's resolve. But he's best when he's operating on the far fringe, turning his cello into a drum kit on the rickety, brilliant 'Grey test hits' or a vast resonator on the perplexingly huge 'Sange / Tsuki', an 8-minute xenharmonic spiral that sounds like an orchestra of fingerdrummed steel pans and a set of metal sheets being bowed in a concrete cavern. There's nothing else quite like it, we're sure of that.
items._cn_summary: 中川大提琴独奏首作以严谨的实验姿态展开，通过大量扩展演奏技法——弓触停歇、弦间滑音、近似筝的拨奏与弯音、琴体敲击与摩擦——拓展大提琴的声学边界，辅以效果器处理生成类特雷门的游移啸音。作品在沉稳的持续音与尖锐的不和谐泛音之间反复游走，如《Sange / Tsuki》以八分钟非平均律盘旋构建庞大的共振空间，《Grey test hits》则将大提琴彻底转化为打击乐器。整体呈现出介于当代古典、即兴与噪音实验之间的质地，不依赖旋律而以声音物质本身为核心。

items.album: Love's Secret Demise
items.excerpt: Thee most coveted collection of Coil demos surfaces on CD, opening a window onto the recording sessions for their pivotal 1991 release, ‘Love’s Secret Domain’. Originally collated on a demo tape for WaxTrax! records in 1989 under the working title ‘The Side Effects of Life’, these are the raw early iterations of tracks that would... more
items.body:
Thee most coveted collection of Coil demos surfaces on CD, opening a window onto the recording sessions for their pivotal 1991 release, ‘Love’s Secret Domain’. 

Originally collated on a demo tape for WaxTrax! records in 1989 under the working title ‘The Side Effects of Life’, these are the raw early iterations of tracks that would become ‘Love’s Secret Domain’, and arguably one of the ’90s definitive albums. Only a handful of the original cassette are known to exist, and have understandably become important artefacts in their own right, so it’s a massive buzz to finally, physically grasp the album in its entirety, here supplemented by material off the ‘Wrong Eye/Scope’ 7”.

Between the album’s two bookending versions of ‘Fidgit’, which later appeared on the ‘WaxTrax! Sampler #2’ tape in 1989, the album spools familiar yet rawer examples of Coil classics such as ‘Dark River’, ‘Teenage Lightening’ and ‘Love's Secret Domain’, each replete with haphazard fades, cuts and stereo bias, and often with lots of ferric noise. However none of that should put prospective listeners off, with results more faithful to the original than the weirdly pitched version found on YouTube and p2p sites.   

Ultimately it’s a proper find for Coil diehards, but anyone intrigued by the hidden reverse of what was going on in parallel to Rave, grunge and post rock in the phase shift between later ‘80s and early ‘90s, should fill their boots.
items._cn_summary: 这张唱片收录了Coil乐队1991年里程碑专辑《Love's Secret Domain》的原始demo版本，原本以《The Side Effects of Life》为名在1989年编纂成磁带供WaxTrax!厂牌使用。原始卡带存世极少，具有重要的史料价值。此次CD发行完整呈现了专辑成型前的粗糙形态，收录了《Dark River》《Teenage Lightening》《Love's Secret Domain》等经典曲目的早期迭代，以及《Wrong Eye/Scope》7寸单曲中的补充素材。录音保留了偶然的淡出、剪切、立体声偏移和大量磁带噪声，但相比网络上流传的变速版本更忠实于原始面貌。两端的《Fidgit》版本此前曾出现在1989年的《WaxTrax! Sampler #2》磁带中。对于Coil的忠实乐迷而言这是一次重要的考古发现，也为研究九十年代初期与锐舞、垃圾摇滚和后摇滚并行的地下实验场景提供了珍贵文本。

items.album: The Rose Of Nevada (Original Score)
items.excerpt: One of the UK’s most distinctive filmmakers returns to the sea, replete with his original synth score - as on ‘Bait’ and ‘Enys Men’ - but notably damper, deeply blue; surely evoking fellow Cornish native AFX’s ‘SAW II’, BoC interludes, Mordant Music, classic folk horror OSTs. Centred around the tale of a trawler that returns... more
items.body:
One of the UK’s most distinctive filmmakers returns to the sea, replete with his original synth score - as on ‘Bait’ and ‘Enys Men’ - but notably damper, deeply blue; surely evoking fellow Cornish native AFX’s ‘SAW II’, BoC interludes, Mordant Music, classic folk horror OSTs.

Centred around the tale of a trawler that returns, sans crew, to a Cornish harbour years after it was thought lost, ‘The Rose Of Nevada’ typically draws on what Mark Jenkin knows best - the people, places and metaphysics of the Atlantic peninsula - whilst ideally emphasising the atmosphere with his special ingredient score. His palette of tape-smudged analog synths feels especially washed out and suggestive of his subject in its briny tone and oceanic scale, which evidently works a treat as a discrete work in its own right, severed from imagery. 

There’s possibly a Kernewek word for “hiraeth”, or “sehnsucht” - a sense of longing, nostalgia - that we’re not aware of, but may perfectly fit the feeling of Jenkin’s music here. Sea-legged loops and sustained drones colour the air with a palpable melancholy in passage from the bittersweet tang of ‘Kneebone Barton’, as used on the trailer, and throughout the album’s patches of decaying wheeze, staining the surface like rust or efflorescence on weathered coves. 

And in the day-dreamiest sense it all fades in/out of consciousness with a perfectly ghostly wow and flutter, as leaching from ‘Through The Gaps’ parts into the slurred whorl of ‘What’s Your Name,’ ephemeral concrète of ‘Look At It’, and final folksy shuffle off into the horizon with ‘Rose of Nevada.’ Here’s looking forward to the film.
items._genre: ambient / experimental synth / drone / folk horror OST
items._cn_summary: Mark Jenkin 为其电影《The Rose Of Nevada》创作的原声配乐延续了他在《Bait》和《Enys Men》中标志性的合成器路线。整张专辑以磁带质感的模拟合成器为主体，声音经过刻意模糊处理，带有潮湿的蓝灰色调，营造出浓郁的海洋氛围。循环乐句与持续低音在空气中铺展，赋予音乐一种深沉的忧郁感和思乡情怀，如同对失去的人与远去的土地的无声呼唤。专辑曲目之间以颤音与抖动效果衔接，形成幽灵般的进出感，末曲则以民谣式散拍缓缓消隐于地平线。作为一张脱离影像独立聆听的作品，其声音设计精致且富有层次，将合成器音色与英国康沃尔海岸的文化质感紧密结合，呈现出独特的地域性实验氛围。

items.album: Serpentine
items.artist: Christer Bothén, Oren Ambarchi, Johan Berthling, Andreas Werliin
items.excerpt: Swedish jazz icon Christer Bothén returns to Black Truffle backed by Ghosted's Oren Ambarchi, Johan Berthling and Andreas Werliin, playing bass clarinet and donso n’goni over the trio's signature kraut-jazz grooves. Hypnotic, trance-inducing biz FFO Natural Information Society, Don Cherry's 'Organic Music Society', Jon Hassell... more
items.body:
Swedish jazz icon Christer Bothén returns to Black Truffle backed by Ghosted's Oren Ambarchi, Johan Berthling and Andreas Werliin, playing bass clarinet and donso n’goni over the trio's signature kraut-jazz grooves. Hypnotic, trance-inducing biz FFO Natural Information Society, Don Cherry's 'Organic Music Society', Jon Hassell, The Necks.

If you're up on your Swedish jazz, there's no way you won't have stumbled across multi-instrumentalist Bothén. He's still best known for palling around with Don Cherry when the jazz great moved to Scandinavia, even teaching him how to play the donso n'goni, a sacred "hunter's harp" from the Wassoulou region in West Africa that Bothén had picked up when he was in Mali. And he's continued to perform with various local artists and outfits, conspicuously appearing on Ghosted's 2022 debut album just mere moments before Ambarchi's Black Truffle imprint re-issued his lost Afro-fusion classic album 'Trancedance'. Last year, Bothén finally issued his first solo n'goni album and now he's back on Black Truffle with this fleshed-out collaboration with the Ghosted crew, leading Ambarchi's Leslie-cab guitar drones, Berthling's bass and Werliin's drums.

Berthling and Werliin take the lead at first on the title track, hammering out a rotating groove before Bothén lets rip on bass clarinet. And playing a side role, Ambarchi might have the most important presence, using his signature phased, organ-like tones to provide anchoring drones for Bothén's spirited improvisations. He's even more pivotal on 'Antigorite', playing cascading staccato notes over those Leslie moans and creating an rhythmelodic foil for the other three players' more traditional interplay. But it's when Bothén plays the n'ghoni that the album really hits its stride; on 'Lizardite', those buzzing tones offset Ambarchi's crystalline twangs, filling in for Werliin's imposing basslines. It's the moment where everything else just drops into place, creating a structural crescendo before the album careers into darkness on the brilliantly moody closer 'Chrysotile'.
items._genre: spiritual jazz / afro-fusion / krautrock / drone / improvisation
items._cn_summary: 瑞典爵士前辈Christer Bothén携低音单簧管与西非猎人之琴顿索恩戈尼回归Black Truffle厂牌，与Ghosted三人组展开合作。Ambarchi标志性的相位处理吉他持续嗡鸣为基底，Berthling的低音与Werliin的鼓击构筑循环律动，Bothén在此之上展开自由即兴。开篇曲先以三人组的律动铺设轨道，随后低音单簧管切入激昂独奏；中段Ambarchi的级联断音与Leslie音箱轰鸣交织，形成节奏与旋律交织的张力；恩戈尼琴登场的曲目使整体真正进入高潮，蜂鸣般的音色与Ambarchi清澈拨弦、鼓手厚重的低音线相互填补。最终曲以阴暗忧郁的氛围收束全篇，呼应专辑标题所暗示的矿物意象与地质质感，整体呈现出仪式性的催眠特质。

items.excerpt: Stefan Betke aka Pole’s hugely influential debut LP of frayed dub experiments resurfaces for a 20th anniversary reissue, taking us back to smoked out nights at the turn of the century and some of the finest post basic-channel dub echoes ever released. Essential listening if you’re into anything from Rhythm & Sound to Vainqueur... more
items.body:
Stefan Betke aka Pole’s hugely influential debut LP of frayed dub experiments resurfaces for a 20th anniversary reissue, taking us back to smoked out nights at the turn of the century and some of the finest post basic-channel dub echoes ever released. Essential listening if you’re into anything from Rhythm & Sound to Vainqueur, Jon Hassell to Jackie Mittoo.

As legend goes, Pole took his name from a malfunctioning Waldorf 4-Pole filter which produced hisses and pops which weren’t really controllable or predictable, much like a living organism. Betke realised the potential and came to alchemically morph and render them with judicious FX dubbing into a groundbreaking sort of minimalist electro-dub that sounds exceedingly good with a spliff and glass of booze. Working somewhere between the variants of abstract techno on Chain Reaction and Mille Plateaux’s cutting edge minimalist strains, Pole’s first trio of albums inarguably helped lay the foundations for dub techno as it’s come to be known and are held in the highest regard by practically everyone who owns them. 

The Pole aesthetic is patently laid out in ‘1’, where his organic clicks ’n pops come out to play accompanied by lilting organ and jazzy bass channelling Jackie Mittoo via Jon Hassell and Rhythm & Sound into a uniquely, gauzy, gaseous state.  So strong was the impact of the album on the late ‘90s underground, they even generated a “pastiche” that was unwittingly issued (and subsequently deleted) by Fat Cat on their split series, but was purportedly made by V/Vm in a snidey but frankly hilarious prank, albeit one that demonstrates just how ubiquitous and influential Betke’s sound was at the time. More than that, it’s fair to say the 20 year cycle hasn’t rinsed out the appeal of this triptych one bit; it remains one of electronic music’s most enigmatic and strangely moving, tactile bodies of work.
items._genre: dub techno / minimal electronica / experimental dub
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Stefan Betke化名Pole的处女作，源于一台失灵的Waldorf四极点滤波器所产生的不可控嘶声与爆音。他将这种'故障之声'视为有机生命体般加以塑造，通过精妙的延迟与混响处理，炼金术般地转化为极简电子杜布风格。专辑中有机的咔嗒声与风琴、爵士贝斯线交织，在缥缈朦胧的音景中游走。评论追溯其对九十年代末地下场景的深远影响——曾有厂牌误发了一张仿作，这从侧面印证了Betke声音在当时的高度辨识度。二十年过去，这套三部曲仍未失去其触动人心的质感，评论将其定位为电子音乐中最具神秘色彩与情感深度的声音档案之一。

items.album: SKY
items.excerpt: All upward lift and kosmiche synth iridescence from Seoul’s blissed family band, back on the Far East’s leading krautrock revival label, Guruguru Brain... “The blissed family band is back! TENGGER have always moved together, through time, space & genre. 'SKY' arrives as a new chapter: a little more still, a little more inward, while... more
items.body:
All upward lift and kosmiche synth iridescence from Seoul’s blissed family band, back on the Far East’s leading krautrock revival label, Guruguru Brain...

“The blissed family band is back! TENGGER have always moved together, through time, space & genre. 'SKY' arrives as a new chapter: a little more still, a little more inward, while keeping all the warmth that's always been at the heart of what they do.

Embodying the band name meaning "endless sky" in Mongolian and "vast sea" in Hungarian, their 8th album 'SKY' centres on the feelings of boundless, infinite expansion. Conceived as one continuous environment rather than a collection of tracks, the album unfolds slowly through luminous synths, patient drones and Itta's breath-like vocals.

Like a soft big sky you can actually float on: 'SKY' is vast, warm, and wide open.

"Rather than a specific emotion, we hope the record opens a certain awareness — that the sky is not just something to be seen. Through it, we sense a connection to something much larger — a feeling of being linked to the wider universe. This sense of connection runs through the entire record.””
items._genre: kosmische / ambient drone / krautrock revival / synth iridescence
items._cn_summary: 来自首尔的家庭乐队 TENGGER 在日本独立厂牌 Guruguru Brain 发行第八张专辑《SKY》。专辑以蒙古语「无尽天空」与匈牙利语「浩瀚海洋」的双重语义为核心概念，试图传达一种超越视觉的、与更广阔宇宙相连的感知。整张作品被构思为一个连续的环境而非独立的曲目集合，通过发光的合成器音色、缓慢展开的持续低音以及主唱 Itta 类似呼吸般的人声铺陈开来。乐评将其形容为「可以真正漂浮其上的柔软巨大天空」，强调其在温暖与广阔之间取得的平衡。相比以往作品，这张专辑更为沉静与内省，但保留了乐队一贯的亲和力与温度。整体呈现出冥想式的氛围漫游特质，适合作为长时间的背景聆听体验。

items.album: November 89
items.excerpt: Finally, Kompakt issue a true GAS outlier on vinyl for the first time, recorded in 1989 and containing some of Wolfgang Voigt’s earliest and starkest recycling of magisterial Wagner loops, closest to the ends of The Caretaker, Philip Jeck, Kevin Drumm. One of those releases that has lurked on our shelves since 2008 as a book and... more
items.body:
Finally, Kompakt issue a true GAS outlier on vinyl for the first time, recorded in 1989 and containing some of Wolfgang Voigt’s earliest and starkest recycling of magisterial Wagner loops, closest to the ends of The Caretaker, Philip Jeck, Kevin Drumm.

One of those releases that has lurked on our shelves since 2008 as a book and CD, ‘November 89’ exists in the margins of Wolfgang Voigt’s GAS canon as its creepiest and most occluded evocation of long walks in the Bavarian forests. While other GAS classics ooze a sort of dappled warmth breaking thru the trees in their widescreen dub techno strolls, you can fully feel the light dying over the horizon and the forest drawing in on this particularly gloomy, hour-long suite. 

As the title suggests, it was mostly, remarkably, made in ’89, back when Voigt was finding his feet between techno, house and indie-pop, and nearly a decade before he co-founded Kompakt with Michael Mayer & Jürgen Paape - by which time he was a full-fledged rave dynamo as Love Inc. and myriad others notable projects. And, in that sense, it can be heard as his ‘Selected Ambient Works 89-95’ - or perhaps more pertinently with SAW II vibes - in his nascent attempt to chase the ambient dragon, which surely endures for its strangely nostalgic, unheimlich qualities.

An educated guess leads us to think the first three were made in ’89, taking in the nightfall scenery of smudged symphonic strings and icy crackle to ‘Der Wald’, plus the muddied bass waltz and spectral pall of ‘Das Moor’, thru the self-evidently titled centrepiece ‘1989-11-01’, bristling with a digitally iridescent dread. ‘Tal 90’ and ‘Nah Und Fern’, which shares its title with the 2008 boxset, were most likely made a little later, and find the wintry doom thawing to the GAS-eous forms we’ve all come to deeply know and adore. 

A true evergreen for deep ambient techno connoisseurs, no less
items._genre: ambient / dark ambient / experimental electronic / drone
items._cn_summary: GAS的《November 89》是一张录制于1989年的早期作品，展现了Wolfgang Voigt在创立Kompakt厂牌和dub techno风格成型之前的探索阶段。整张专辑以瓦格纳式的循环采样为核心手法，将模糊的交响弦乐、冰冷的数字裂纹与泥泞的低频融合，呈现出一种在巴伐利亚森林深处漫步时的阴郁氛围。评论将其与The Caretaker、Philip Jeck的碎片化怀旧美学并置，指出其具备一种'不亲和的'、令人不安的特质，与Aphex Twin早期ambient作品的精神遥相呼应。前三首作品明显带有更早期的实验粗糙感，而后两首则预示了后来GAS更为人熟知的温暖氛围形态。这张专辑将暗潮氛围的压抑与电子实验的解构手法结合，是深度氛围音乐收藏中不可忽视的一环。

items.album: Somewhere in the Wind
items.excerpt: Recorded live in Brooklyn, 'Somewhere in the Wind' is Loren Connors & David Grubbs’ third album and their first as a guitar duo, showcasing their free-er, noiser side with two extended, ecstatic jams. Thankfully, we didn't have to wait another two decades to hear Grubbs and Connors collide again. Their first album, 'Arborvitae'... more
items.body:
Recorded live in Brooklyn, 'Somewhere in the Wind' is Loren Connors & David Grubbs’ third album and their first as a guitar duo, showcasing their free-er, noiser side with two extended, ecstatic jams. 

Thankfully, we didn't have to wait another two decades to hear Grubbs and Connors collide again. Their first album, 'Arborvitae', appeared way back in 2003, not long after the duo had first met when Connors shared a bill with Gastr del Sol. But it wasn't until 2024 that they rekindled that magic, shaking things up a little and swapping roles on keys and guitar, with Connors even moonlighting on drums. 'Somewhere in the Wind' might be the perfect companion to that record, recorded last year at Blank Forms, it's their first session featuring both players on electric guitar and it's a joy to engage with on every level. Both distinctive players carry an unmistakable signature style, complementing each other by leaning into the noise and freedom of their collaboration in a way we hadn't witnessed until now. 

If their first two records dug into crepuscular space, the domain of Roy Montgomery and Harold Budd, this one takes its cues from the physicality of their instruments and the knowledge they've acquired along the way. You feel as if you're practically in the room with them as Connors's blurry post-blues recitals casually interact with Grubbs' obsessively tuned intonations. On the first side, we walk into what might as well be a prayer, each note played in reverence to something or someone. But as the piece accumulates weight, so too do the notes, lovingly distorted and pushed off track until all that's left is raw emotion. On the flip, the duo sound even more possessed, kicking up the energy so the notes bounce around the very edges of the recording space. It's a document of two players who don't have anything left to prove.
items._cn_summary: 这是洛伦·康纳斯与大卫·格鲁布斯第三度合作的专辑，首次以双吉他编制呈现，两首现场录音的即兴长曲充满自由与噪音张力。与此前作品偏向暮色氛围的探索不同，此作更强调乐器的物理质感与两位演奏者数十年积累的技巧交互。康纳斯模糊的后布鲁斯语汇与格鲁布斯精调音准的持续音形成对话，A面音符层层堆积直至变形为粗粝情感，B面则更具能量，音符在录音空间的边缘跳跃碰撞。整张作品记录了两位无需证明任何东西的演奏者之间的纯粹协作状态，展现了即兴音乐中对话与倾听的核心美学。

items.album: Arc
items.excerpt: On Kirk Barley’s definitive solo gem, alternative tunings and a tactile feel for pitching rhythms generate their gentlest and most absorbing work, twinkling amid a microcosm of similar, exploratory productions from Mark Fell & Rian Treanor thru to Aleksi Perälä, Beatrice Dillon, Terry Riley & Jon Hassell. Building on a decade of... more
items.body:
On Kirk Barley’s definitive solo gem, alternative tunings and a tactile feel for pitching rhythms generate their gentlest and most absorbing work, twinkling amid a microcosm of similar, exploratory productions from Mark Fell & Rian Treanor thru to Aleksi Perälä, Beatrice Dillon, Terry Riley & Jon Hassell.

Building on a decade of work spanning cuts for Brownswood thru to jams with Matthew Herbert and Matt Davies, ‘Arc’ finds Yorkshire-bred artist Barley fully indulge formative passions for microtonal just intonation - as seeded in Terry Riley’s ‘Shri Camel’ - and slippery syncopation to the fullest. Half solo, proper, and half peppered with percussion by regular spar, Matt Davies, it follows his nose for open frontiers of alternative tunings and wonky meter with the blend of low key modesty and prism-pushing tekkerz that have long endeared his work to lovers of lower case experimental music. 

Sweetly balanced between timeless, folk-soul-wise and futurist sensibilities, the half hour suite knits hyaline synths and rippling gamelan metallophonics with clarinet and guitar in lissom, sloshing shapes that effortlessly seduce, rather than demand, the listener’s attention. In particular we are drawn to the bits in duo with Davies, floating sublime ideas in the dreamlike, inverted dub architexture of ‘Ion’, settling on mind like a strangely bucolic Incus work on ’Sundry’, and thru the exquisite, tip-toed rhythms of ‘Ecstatic’, to a trippier, bittersweet type of ante-chamber music on ‘Fret (Hear)’.

He’s also deeply charming when left to his own devices. Ambient opener ‘Billow’ calls to mind the tenderness of Cotton Goods works, and ‘Knead’ chases a certain geist of Irdial or Plaid-esque gamelantronica into the sublime title tune, while ‘Prism’ most beautifully ties all his interests in a melting dream sequence which he caps with the harmonic nightlight glow of ‘Column’.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Kirk Barley十年创作脉络的集大成之作，围绕微分音律与非常规调律体系展开，融合了爪哇甘美兰金属音色、单簧管与吉他的有机质感，以及低调动效电子节拍。半数为纯器乐独奏段落，半数与打击乐手Matt Davies合作，营造出半透明的合成器织体与滑动的切分节奏。作品在民谣的质朴灵魂感与未来主义美学之间取得平衡，以半小时的组曲形式串联起多首短曲，既呼应Terry Riley的微分音传统，也带有Mark Fell式的低保真实验电子气质。从Irdial、Plaid到Hassell的影响痕迹清晰可辨，最终凝结为一种轻柔却极具沉浸感的低音实验音乐形态。

items.album: Ethiopian Musics 1971 - Recorded by Ragnar Johnson and Ralph Harrisson
items.excerpt: Anyone obsessed with those two incredible ‘Begena Songs…’ comps on Death Is Not The End will be properly enchanted by this more expansive - yet still intimate - suite of snapshots from Ethiopia, 1971, spanning the unique, twanging harp sound thru to Amharic poetry, chants, and spellbinding flute dances... One that catches the... more
items.body:
Anyone obsessed with those two incredible ‘Begena Songs…’ comps on Death Is Not The End will be properly enchanted by this more expansive - yet still intimate - suite of snapshots from Ethiopia, 1971, spanning the unique, twanging harp sound thru to Amharic poetry, chants, and spellbinding flute dances...

One that catches the breath with seldom felt sensations, ‘Ethiopian Musics 1971’ patently owes as much to the incredible performers as their faithful representation in Ragnar Johnson & Ralph Harrisson’s recordings. All secreted to tape on a Uher Report L stereo reel-to-reel recorder, they epitomise an era of ethnomusicological preservation, when the likes of labels such as Lyrichord and  Folkways were already decades deep “in the field”, documenting long-held traditions practically untouched by an encroaching, western modernity. And perhaps most crucially, the recordings beautifully render the acoustic settings and vivid vibes with an immersive quality in stark opposition to the era of dry, so-called audiophile studio recordings of ethnic musics to come - all the better for immersing in this wonderfully unfamiliar world.

The abundance of singular tones and strong, rare feels they produce is quite staggering to our northern english ears, and we reckon also for anyone else, for that matter. Opening to a joyful couplet of a bluesy ’Song about the beauty of women’, and the almost shanty-like swing and hard rhythm of ’Tej Beit Song’, the set reels to distinctive pieces of Ethiopian Christian song set to begena, or ‘Harp of David’, buzz, and a landscape-scale, 13 minute ‘Love Song (Mary Armede)’. A gripping ‘Drum Song (Jigsaw)’ will be mana to rhythm fiends, and a number of standout flute pieces reprise the frisson of our first encounter with this discipline on Sublime Freq’s ‘Staring into the Sun - Ethiopian Tribal Music’ set of 2012, most potently on the pluming twin pipes of the ‘Fila Flute Dance’ parts, whilst the pentatonic craar (6-stringed lyre) parts surely strike nerves for lovers of the rawest blues, and hail the liberated legacy of Mary Armede, a folk singer-fashion designer of Azmari heritage who surely warrants further investigation. 

No doubt this is one of the most striking archival discoveries of 2026, acutely advised to anyone enchanted with music from this corner of the world from Éthiopiques to begena harp, thru to Ragnar Johnson’s other arenas of research for Ideologic Organ in Yemen or Papua New Guinea. Dive in without delay.
items._genre: ethnomusicological field recording / Ethiopian traditional / harp music / folk poetry
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了1971年由Ragnar Johnson与Ralph Harrisson使用Uher Report L立体声开盘录音机在埃塞俄比亚实地录制的音乐档案，涵盖独特的拨弦竖琴begena（"大卫竖琴"）、阿姆哈拉语诗歌、吟唱与迷人的笛舞。录音以高保真品质忠实再现了原声环境与现场氛围，与后来干涩的录音棚式民族音乐制作形成鲜明对比。内容从歌颂女性之美的布鲁斯式旋律到十三分钟的爱之歌、从节奏紧凑的鼓乐到pentatonic六弦琴craar的演奏，展现了埃塞俄比亚丰富的传统音乐谱系。尤其值得关注的是Azmari出身的民间歌手兼时装设计师Mary Armede的遗产。整张专辑是民族音乐学保存工作的典范，将未被西方现代性触及的传统以沉浸式方式呈现给当代听众。

items.body:
Coltrane’s invigorating ’66 spiritual free jazz salvo - the follow-up to ‘A Love Supreme’ (1965) - is unleashed from the Verve Vault, spotlighting his classic line-up tearing out on templates set by Ornette Coleman years prior, along with more reserved moments of beauty. An evergreen..

"Following the genre-redefining revelations of A Love Supreme in 1965, John Coltrane began a dramatic shift toward spiritual free jazz, abandoning familiar forms in favour of a more abstract sonic palette and bold questions he'd spend the rest of his life and career pursuing. Meditations, released by Impulse! in 1966, continues that emotional throughline while retaining, for the last time in full, the classic quartet that propelled Trane to greatness: pianist McCoy Tyner, bassist Jimmy Garrison and drummer Elvin Jones. (They're further augmented by Pharoah Sanders on tenor sax and additional drummer Rashied Ali.) Meditations pushes Coltrane’s spiritual jazz into heightened realms of energy and abstraction — a powerful document of transformation, intensity, and devotion in Coltrane’s recorded legacy."
items._genre: free jazz / spiritual jazz / avant-garde / improvisation
items._cn_summary: 这是约翰·柯川在1965年《至高之爱》之后的延续之作，标志着他从结构化爵士转向精神自由爵士的关键节点。专辑保留了经典四重奏阵容——钢琴手麦考伊·泰纳、贝斯手吉米·加里森和鼓手埃尔文·琼斯，并加入次中音萨克斯手桑德斯和第二鼓手拉希德·阿里，形成双鼓配置带来的张力与多层次节奏对话。柯川在此推进了更为抽象与高能的探索，引入科尔曼早年开创的自由爵士语汇，同时穿插内省的静谧段落。这种从狂热即兴到沉思冥想之间的动态对比，既是对宗教虔诚与精神蜕变的音乐化记录，也展现了柯川晚期语言的开端。整体制作既保留了即兴爵士的核心精神，又呈现出打破调性框架的实验特质。

items.album: Stochastic Parrot
items.excerpt: Roping in Pierre Bastien and Mark Cunningham to provide brass, Mike Cooper turns in his most kaleidoscopic fourth world dream sequence to date, drawing on dub and exotica to harmonise with Andrew Pekler's marooned soundscapes... Cooper admits in the liner notes that although he's often compared with Jon Hassell, it's... more
items.body:
Roping in Pierre Bastien and Mark Cunningham to provide brass, Mike Cooper turns in his most kaleidoscopic fourth world dream sequence to date, drawing on dub and exotica to harmonise with Andrew Pekler's marooned soundscapes...

Cooper admits in the liner notes that although he's often compared with Jon Hassell, it's German painter Mati Klarwein fantastical album covers that always reminded him exactly why he was doing what he was doing. Because Cooper makes music for imaginary places, not tangible soundtracks but half dreamed, half lived experiences that course through his catalog of experiments. And his process has never been quite so vivid as it is on 'Stochastic Parrot', a suite of vertiginous reverberations that are struck through with Cooper's "real and virtual" lap steel twangs, collaged together from samples and field recordings that wobble like heat haze. 

Different pockets of rhythm bash into each other on 'ARCHAEOPTERYX', accompanied by Bastien and Cunningham's spiraling brass improvisations. And Cooper holds the sounds together with his lulling repeated phrases; the hand drums might sound as if they're in conflict with the cycling drum machine crashes, but that's the point - it's not like channeling a dream so much as it's like being subjected to three or four dreams simultaneously. It's the ghosts of jazz fusion being raked over coals at midnight: just tune into 'SUMATRA SAMPHIRE', with its distant animalistic wails and popcorn drums, or the granulized 'HAT YAI', that sounds like the prelude to a druggy ritual.
items._genre: fourth world / dub / exotica / experimental / field recording
items._cn_summary: Mike Cooper 的《Stochastic Parrot》邀请 Pierre Bastien 和 Mark Cunningham 贡献铜管声部，构建出一幅万花筒式的第四世界梦境图景。Cooper 在此延续其一贯的创作哲学——为虚构之地而非真实场景创作音乐，融合采样、田野录音与 lap steel 滑棒吉他音色，声响如热浪般摇曳颤动。专辑中不同节奏层相互碰撞，手鼓与循环鼓机看似冲突实则并行，如同时身处三四场梦境之中。Brian Eno 的《Fourth World》美学在此被进一步推进：dub 律动、exotica 异国情调与爵士融合的幽灵被笼罩于午夜余烬之下。曲目如《SUMATRA SAMPHIRE》呈现动物般的远距嚎叫与爆米花鼓点，《HAT YAI》则颗粒感十足，宛如致幻仪式的序曲。整体作品将记忆与幻觉编织成漂浮的听觉地图。

items.album: New History Warfare Vol​.​1
items.excerpt: Colin Stetson’s breakthrough album of gripping bass sax innovations still buzzes like few others. In 2007 ‘New History Warfare Vol.1’ asserted Stetson as an indomitable player of wind instruments, here letting off on Alto, Baritone and Bass Saxophones, plus Clarinet, in a deftly muscular display of his skills which had... more
items.body:
Colin Stetson’s breakthrough album of gripping bass sax innovations still buzzes like few others.

In 2007 ‘New History Warfare Vol.1’ asserted Stetson as an indomitable player of wind instruments, here letting off on Alto, Baritone and Bass Saxophones, plus Clarinet, in a deftly muscular display of his skills which had previously been employed on record and in live tours for Arcade Fire, Tom Waits, Bon Iver, LCD Soundsystem and whoever the heck else needed a set of lungs as good as a blacksmith’s bellows.

While perhaps best known for wielding a massive Bass Saxophone that's responsible for some of the wildest sounds on this album, Stetson proves to be a sensitive beast capable of articulating the instrument’s full range tonal in his own voice, which variously comes out resembling a purring big cat and the dying wildebeest it just stalked, attacked and slaughtered in ‘Time Is Advancing With Fitful Irregularity’, while he uses the same broad tone to describe natural scenes as textured with soil and moisture and wind as an Anne Guthrie piece in ‘As a Bird or Branch’, while ‘Nobu Take’ sounds like a manic 8-bit computer game soundtrack and ’Tiger Tiger Crane’ adds a tight percussive workout for good measure, but trust its all acoustic, instrumental, hands-on, somehow not processed. 

Still a stonking good record, this, ripe for re/discovery.
items._genre: experimental / avant-garde jazz / solo saxophone / free improvisation / contemporary classical
items._cn_summary: Colin Stetson的突破性专辑以低音萨克斯为核心乐器，在单一声学管乐器的框架内展现出惊人的力度与音色跨度。他一人同时担任演奏者与呼吸循环系统，利用循环呼吸技巧在不使用任何效果器或后期处理的情况下，构建出层层叠加的厚重声场。专辑中《Time Is Advancing With Fitful Irregularity》以暴烈的低音萨克斯吹奏模拟大型猫科动物的撕咬与喘息，从低沉的喉音骤然攀升至尖锐的高音泛音；《As a Bird or Branch》转向阴郁的抒情段落，木管音色被拉伸成持续不断的环境音层；《Nobu Take》则以快速吐音制造类似8位电子游戏音效的密集音流。尽管所有声音均为原声管乐器实时演奏，却呈现出超越传统爵士语汇的实验性声响雕塑感。Stetson此前曾为Arcade Fire、Tom Waits、Bon Iver等乐队担任巡演乐手，这张专辑则是其作为独立艺术家的首次完整宣言，确立了其在当代实验管乐领域的位置。

items.body: Field of Coincidence is the debut album documenting the collaboration between LA-based artists Jesse Perlstein (Sontag Shogun, AxOxH) and Michael Robert Chadwick (Fake Sword, Plum Professional), aka Trellis. Perhaps the perception of coincidence can serve as a link to folk psychology and philosophy as well as supernatural, occult, or paranormal claims, psychological reasoning, and the statistical probability of chance events. A surreal flow of sound as art music for careful listening Field of Coincidence by Trellis   Field of Coincidence is the debut album documenting the collaboration between LA-based artists Jesse Perlstein (Sontag Shogun, AxOxH) and Michael Robert Chadwick (Fake Sword, Plum Professional), aka Trellis. Perhaps the perception of coincidence can serve as a link to folk psychology and philosophy as well as supernatural, occult, or paranormal claims, psychological reasoning, and the statistical probability of chance events. Perlstein: vox, roland ju06a, OM-1 cassette synth, various pedals & field recordings. Chadwick: kobol expander, korg minilogue xd, yamaha sy35, lexicon mx200, roland DEP-5, polyend tracker. Complex art collage cover and layout by Trellis. I think of this surreal flow of sound as art music for careful listening, the sound can trigger a search for meaning or hidden patterns, with no design of providing the relief of therapeutic sleeping. First build a machine by adding parts, let it run, and then after a good duration, shut it down. Of course, you can dream while the motor runs. This experience connects events that are causally unrelated, and yet their occurrence together has meaning for the person who observes them. Field of Coincidence flows slowly, builds in secret, and glitters with life around every measure’s bend. At times dark and brooding, at other times consonant and crystalline, this multi-hued suite of songs showcases the depth and range of a project burgeoning out of its fruitful first pursuit. “A circular or spiral motion unfolds, as if the collage forms the oceanic currents driven by the wind and planetary gravitational rotation.” ~Robin B. James Opening with what could be waves or surf in the distance, “At The Tiller” (4:45). Soon there emerges a strange carnival merry-go-round soundtrack, with a melting fun house feeling, and a haunting kaliope. A tiller could be on a boat, or for digging the fields, or a shoot sprouting. A firefighting tiller is the second driver on a big hook and ladder truck. The sound feels upbeat and positive, and certainly as artificial as electronic music might be, synthesizers just can’t help it. The second track opens into strange brightness, building a weave of electronica and interesting sky hooks, “Sacrificial Anode” (2:51). Perhaps the anode does not want to be an offering and goes along very slowly. “Stars Our Destination” (4:23) opens in mystery, during a long journey. The tempo is somewhat subdued. This might be a lullaby, the feeling is very calming and quiet. We are out in space, smaller vessels approach the big ship, machines are running, things are slower here. Next, heading into a cinematic opening that is rippling with hope and uplifting the spirits. As the sun rises, flute-like drones emerge, “Ashen Rain” (4:57) paints a picture of planets in motion. The title track suggests to me a long helix formation spiraling slowly, in constant motion, adding new bits as we go behind a hall of mirrors loop. Perhaps there is a simulated choral element. “Field of Coincidence” (5:09)  leads into a wilderness populated by unseen creatures that call and cry, with room for a little drama at the end. A circular or spiral motion unfolds, as if the collage forms the oceanic currents driven by the wind and planetary gravitational rotation, “Gyres” (5:14) is panoramic, suggesting thick gases or fluids flowing on a grand scale, leading a steady exploration of this beautifully strange and peaceful place where nothing seems to happen. “Along the way new electronic things show up as the end approaches, the feeling is heavenly and dark, always both.” ~Robin B. James The birds were here first, “Ominous Dawn” (4:34). Soon electronics slip in slowly under the birds, the other instruments also emerge slowly, and below all that, the sound of something bumping about in the chamber swells the tableaux. Something complex is coming up from below, the realm down there is huge, it gets into our world through echoes, iron chimes, an electronic choir with solo drone vocalists, the birds, and a sleepy Martian, who is present only for an instant. “Tunneled” (4:33) is a long slow atmospheric excursion where nothing happens and we accumulate overlapping atmospheres, maybe that bell is from a distant foggy harbor. I think something is waiting in the dark tunnel, signalling to bring us to enter the mystery, so I give in. My God! It is sunny and bright in hereI I was expecting more gloom. It is still a subterranean tunnel in the end, and we are deep below the surface of the Earth. From one of the most dangerous tunnels, “Luciferin Haze” (4:52) makes a slow entrance, like a sunrise, a slow drone of long sustained layered tones. The feeling is rather uplifting and positive upon reflection, often in soft focus and fanciful. Nothing is real here, perhaps we are in a sweet cosmic funeral. I think I hear unconnected events at the same time or place, purely by chance, I hear water, the snowflakes are dancing, suggesting a sparkling atmosphere. “Eddies” (3:56) evokes distant ocean surf, or water in the cave in the short distance. Somehow we are with the choir out here, and the keyboard is over there in the big cave. Pareidolia is the tendency for perception to impose a meaningful interpretation on a nebulous stimulus, usually visual, so that one detects an object, pattern, or meaning where there is none. The unknown forces cause what is perceived as just the peaks, or groupings of coincidences. A coincidence is a remarkable concurrence of events or circumstances that have no apparent causal connection with one another, contrasting with fatalism, a doctrine which holds that that events will happen in the exact manner of a predetermined plan. Along the way new electronic things show up as the end approaches, the feeling is heavenly and dark, always both. Recorded & Mixed by Trellis in Highland Park, LAMastered by Michael Robert ChadwickCover art and layout by TrellisAlthough ambient in scope, these pieces employ pop structures, natural environmental recordings, and FX-laden sound design, released on May 12, 2026 to tell emotive stories in abstract auditory theatre. Between swarms of vocal layering and harmonic analog synthesizers, there’s a timbral warmth to these tracks that feels refreshing in this AI-driven age of algorithm.This is not a synth album designed in a laboratory, nor on a perfectly grid-mapped sequencer, the subtle blemishes and analog acoustic artifacts that populate this record throughout serve to remind us that this is human music, made by people (friends, together), for people. Like Hiroshi Yoshimura‘s 1982 Music for Nine Postcards. Yoshimura‘s music lies mostly in the minimalist genre of kankyō ongaku, or environment music—soft electronic melodies infused with the sounds of nature: babbling brooks, steady rain, and morning birds. Famously, Yoshimura said that he was inspired by “the movements of clouds, the shade of a tree in summertime, the sound of rain, the snow in a town.” He wanted to create music that was “as close to air itself.” His beloved 1984 tape Watering a Flower, finds a delicate grandiosity in the private intimacy of a lamplit domestic space; evolution is driven by adapting to new environments. Field of Coincidence is available on Aural Canyon. [Bandcamp] Field of Coincidence by Trellis The post Trellis :: Field of Coincidence (Aural Canyon) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: Trellis 是洛杉矶两位艺术家 Jesse Perlstein 与 Michael Robert Chadwick 的合作项目，《Field of Coincidence》是他们的首张专辑。作品以 Roland JU06A、OM-1 卡带合成器、Korg Minilogue XD、Yamaha SY35、Polyend Tracker 等多件硬件设备为载体，融入田野录音与效果器处理，呈现出缓慢铺展、暗中建构的声音流程。乐评将其描述为'需要仔细聆听的艺术音乐'，音景在黑暗低沉与透明清澈之间交替流动，时而带有诡异嘉年华般的旋转质感，时而展现电子织体中的开阔天空意象。专辑名称暗示巧合与意义感知之间的张力，音乐本身也如同在不相关的事件之间建立联想，鼓励听者在声波运动中寻找隐藏模式。整体呈现出实验电子与氛围音乐交融的特质，适合沉浸式聆听。

items._cn_summary: ASCETA这张专辑以超过20分钟的开篇曲《The Fool Leading the Blind》展开宏大构想，过程感强于结论感，弥漫在谜团氛围中。第二首《Temple Of Mirrors》动态更紧凑，巴松管与大提琴的对位线条成为亮点。评论者最青睐《Everything Stopped》，认为其张力构建与旋律主题的融合最为凝聚，巴松管段落尤为突出。《Memento Mori》则展现快速调性切换与突然停顿的控制力，呈现出受控的混乱感。整体录音室制作较前作略有退步，但专辑仍具备丰富的探索空间。专辑融合室内乐编制与前卫摇滚结构，巴松管作为核心乐器贯穿始终，与弦乐、钢琴共同构建出层次复杂的声景。

items.body: Although Dirk Serries may have retired the Vidna Obmana moniker years ago, albums continue to be released under the name. While these are usually reissues or live recordings, this particular series is generating significant interest. The third installment in the “Twilight Of Perception Redux” series compiles rare and previously unreleased recordings from the Belgian project’s archives, spanning the years 1996 to 2006. The three CDs contain a total of 18 tracks, no fewer than 13 of which fall into the category of—let’s call them—‘curiosities’. Each disc features six tracks that immediately draw the listener into Vidna Obmana’s unique world. These are long, elaborate compositions characterized by generally slow, tribal rhythms that merge with deep, astral, and dreamlike soundscapes. Dirk Serries’ universe evokes a sense of mystery—and at times, a certain darkness—accentuated by field recordings and various forms of sound manipulation. At times, you feel as though you are wandering through a labyrinth of crystalline sounds; moments later, you are drawn towards an imaginary black hole, only to undergo an almost abyssal experience on the next track. Occasionally, a guitar emerges, played in an Ambient style that adds a touch of diversity to the overall atmosphere. Vidna Obmana was a project that fused different styles into a unique whole—a universe where Tribal and Ambient music formed a symbiotic relationship, sweeping the listener away into an imaginative world of richness, even on the darker tracks. This album is a perfect addition to the Vidna Obmana discography for many enthusiasts. Even decades after their creation, these tracks retain an irresistible allure—like a forbidden space where you simply have to discover what is unfolding inside. (Rating:8). Listen to “Threshold Of Obstruction”: Threshold Of Obstruction by Vidna Obmana About Vidna Obmana Vidna Obmana is the pseudonym of Belgian composer Dirk Serries, born in 1968. Serries recorded as Vidna Obmana from 1984 until 2007, when he officially retired the name, moving his active work to the Fear Falls Burning project. The name is Serbian for “optical illusion”. Working in Ambient, Minimal and Drone music, Serries released albums through labels including ND Records, Hypnos Recordings, Soleilmoon Recordings and Projekt Records, and collaborated with artists such as Steve Roach, Asmus Tietchens and Bass Communion. The original “Twilight Of Perception” appeared on Projekt in 1997. “Twilight Of Perception Redux Volume Three 1996 – 2006” compiles archival recordings from that period on Zoharum.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是比利时作曲家Dirk Serries以Vidna Obmana名义发布的第三辑档案合集，收录了1996至2006年间罕见与未发表的录音，共三张CD十八首曲目。作品以缓慢的部落节奏与深邃空灵的音景为核心，通过田野录音与多种声音处理手法构建出神秘而略带暗色的听觉空间。部落与氛围音乐在此形成共生关系，层层递进的旋律结构让听者仿佛穿行于水晶般的声波迷宫中。偶尔浮现的吉他音色以氛围化方式演奏，为整体增添了多样性。这些曲目虽跨越数十年时间，但依然保持着原始的吸引力，为该项目的唱片目录提供了重要补充。

items.album: Palagoma
items.excerpt:

is not only the first release from Nairobi-based label Cool Waters, it also marks the first time German-born, Kenya-based percussionist Sven Kacirek has collaborated with Ogoya Nengo and Olith Ratengo at the same time. items.body: Palagoma is not only the first release from Nairobi-based label Cool Waters, it also marks the first time German-born, Kenya-based percussionist Sven Kacirek has collaborated with Ogoya Nengo and Olith Ratengo at the same time. Odd Okoddo, the duo of Kacirek and Ratengo, has been performing since 2018, but with the inclusion of the 83 year old Nengo, a singer from the eastern part of the country, there�s an added traditional depth to the music. A 2025 performance shows Nengo�s lifetime of experience singing Kenya�s dodo tradition around 2 and half minutes in (see below). Furthermore, her inclusion on this album allows her and Ratengo to toss the vocals back and forth as they reference their shared roots (Ratengo and Nengo live minutes from each other). Musically, however, the tracks are driven by Kacirek�s Buchla synth, hand percussion, and occasional kit drumming, which serve to buoy the voices without blotting out the music�s origins. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Bara,� for example, begins with the dime-store thwack of a repeated pattern, a stiff juxtaposition to the voices; yet, as the song rolls along, a 4/4 clink appears, then a burbling bass, and finally, what sounds like a xylophone. Layers of synthesized polyrhythms keep presenting themselves with a subtlety almost unnoticeable, until, by the track�s end, it feels organic, as if it�s all been underneath the two voices all along. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Sarah,� perhaps the album�s most intense track, features a lead vocal from Ratengo and tentative, percussive spittles from Kacirek. And while the technology never tries to overtake the vocals, it does sneak up and punctuate the track�s urgency, as edgy distortion sneaks in here and there just as Ratengo�s voice reaches its peak. The term �folktronica� has been bandied about as a way to house the type of music on offer here. In fact, exploratory collaborations such as Chouk Bwa & The �ngstr�mers as well as much of Kampala, Uganda�s Nyege Nyege label house sounds that might be �folktronic� in some way. What�s more interesting and important about this music, though, is how truly global so much of it is while maintaining a deep connection to Africa and its diasporic communities. The music on Palagoma , as well as much of what�s linked above (and available in countless other recent recordings) demonstrates a real willingness for cultures to respond to each other without trampling traditions altogether. Instead, roots become avant-garde and innovations become seemingly thousands of years old. Certainly the inclusion of an 83 year old traditional Kenyan singer only recently making her global debut as she tours with a duo whose instrumental voice is a white male saturated in electronic Kenyan rhythms demonstrates this blurring. The music this trio makes is certainly of the 21st century, but it�s often hazy, sparse, and open, keeping it from a quick sell-by date or confining it to a specific genre. Instead, it�s a beautiful example music as grace.
items.label: Cool Waters
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是内罗毕新厂牌Cool Waters的首发作品，由德国裔肯尼亚鼓手Sven Kacirek与Olith Ratengo组成的二人组Odd Okoddo，联同83岁传统dodo歌者Ogoya Nengo共同录制。Nengo的加入为音乐注入了东肯尼亚传统歌唱的深度，她与Ratengo因地域相近而展开人声对话，Kacirek则用Buchla合成器、手打击乐和架子鼓为声部搭建层次。合成器多层次复节奏以隐蔽方式逐渐铺陈，至曲末已与嗓音融为一体。编曲策略是电子元素始终辅助而非压制传统人声，技术手段恰到好处地点缀并强化声乐紧迫感。这种合作模式体现了当代跨文化音乐的特征：根源音乐变得前卫，前卫创新则呈现出古老质感，传统与现代、电子与口传文化在同一空间内协商共存。

items.album: Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari
items.artist: Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy
items.excerpt:
Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release,
Under an Endless Sky
.
In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari,
Songs of Compassion
is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics.
Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. The title track from the 2023 U.S. of Alchemy recording Under an Endless Sky by Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy Further reading Cris Derksen - The Visit (Review) Tiny Sun - Vanishment (Review) Maria Ka - Di Mashin (Review) Further listening You will find a number of Dorothy Moskowitz's works on Race The Sky , most recently on Podgrammes #022 and #019.
items.label: Songs of Compassion
items._cn_summary: Dorothy Moskowitz 联合前卫作曲家 Paladino 与诗人 Ferrari 组成的 United States of Alchemy，以《Songs of Compassion》延续其 1960 年代实验乐队传统。专辑包含十一首作品，以钢琴为主轴，辅以弦乐、木管、合成器声场与金属质感音色，旋律脱离传统功能和声逻辑，呈现非线性、模态化、极简主义的特征，借鉴 Steve Reich 与 Philip Glass 的减法美学。歌词层面延续六十年代抗议歌曲传统，以富诗意而尖锐的当代笔触触及权威主义、种族主义等政治议题，同时穿插对死亡与宇宙位置的哲学冥思。Moskowitz 的演唱苍老而富权威感，钢琴作为另一重声部参与叙事。整张专辑在实验声响与严肃社会关怀之间取得平衡，对惯于西方调性思维的听者构成挑战，也为前卫音乐与时代对话提供范例。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 用废弃杂物自制乐器——tassofons、kitchenofon、didjerimou 等——在现代录音条件下展现出精准的音高与丰富的音质。专辑延续首作《Hirsute Farfelus》的杂糅路线，将克莱兹默、昆比亚、非洲节拍、桑巴、中东旋律等世界各地音乐元素并置，乐手以即兴段落展示娴熟的演奏技艺。评论指出乐器与曲风之间高度匹配：拉花单簧管演绎克莱兹默主题，笛声承载昆比亚旋律，非洲节拍轨道由木鱼、摇铃环绕，marimba 配以钟钹即兴。整体听感兼具趣味性与文化包容度，传递出音乐人不拘形式、就地取材创造声音的核心理念。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: 挪威Camilla Hole Trio在专辑《Langs》中延续了前作《Eventyrferd》的跨界探索精神，但将重心从科幻合成器音色回归到更具大地气息的声响。主奏乐器高音萨克斯暗示了爵士根源，首曲《Springleik》取材自挪威西部传统春季舞蹈旋律，由低音提琴和鼓构成节奏基底，叠加模块合成器与颤音琴增添色彩层次。乐评特别强调该三重奏的核心特征在于角色分配的模糊性——成员间不断交换主奏、节奏与和声功能，低音提琴手卡尔曼在即兴段落中以旋律线与霍尔齐奏，鼓手内斯海姆则以开放式的节奏展开推动整体游离。作品从传统民谣主题出发，经由集体即兴重新解构，在保留挪威民间音乐素材的同时注入自由爵士与电子实验的语汇，形成跨领域的对话。

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源于2021年新冠封锁期间，钢琴家在意大利萨奇莱的Fazioli钢琴音乐厅完成的两小时无脚本独奏即兴录音，后期混入人声采样、打击乐、循环音效、田野录音等环境声音元素。古巴钢琴家与作曲家Omar Sosa延续其拒绝重复的创作哲学，专辑展现沉思而不断演进的艺术风格。Sosa在采访中表达了对流媒体算法与市场分类的抵触，强调以自由即兴状态演奏，崇尚"少即是多"的美学与初录即灵魂之声的理念。录音发生在他婚姻结束与演出取消的特殊人生节点，使整张作品带有内省与精神追寻的气质。他明确避免被归类为爵士、拉丁或古典，但尊重各种形式，在空旷音乐厅中的独奏与后期声响层叠形成冥想般的听觉空间。

items.body: Eye New Dark Adore self-released Eye New Dark is the solo project of Null Device’s Jill Sheridan, and while it shares that modern synthpop act’s lushness and melodic bent, departs from it in some interesting ways. Sheridan has always been a powerful vocalist with excellent control and feeling, and the major contrast in the material on Adore is in hearing her over some more bright and even brash sounding material. Single “Backwards Through That Door” features spritely synth arpegios and peppy drum programming, with Sheridan riding the beat, choosing her spots to move into her upper range for emphasis, the phrasing as important to the song’s feeling as any given sound design element. Similarly, when she sings on the rhumba-beat driven “Real Life”, its her clarity and measured performance that allows her to cut through the brushy percussion sounds, big pads and swelling bells, recalling some of OMD’s more baroque moments. Perhaps the most revelatory moment is closer “Eyes in the Dark”, a track that is musically designed around a sort of stop-start rhythmic movement, the spaces between each small burst of instrumentation smoothed by the lush and layered vocal recordings, filling the space without crowding it. It’s a lovely collection of tracks that shows off versatile takes modern and classic synthpop styles, driven by a genuinely skilled performance. Adore by Eye New Dark Circa Tapes Climbers LVLZ You’ll always be getting a slightly rejiggered formulation of the styles and influences which shape Adam Sieczka’s work as Circa Tapes every time you check in with it, and new EP Climbers is no exception in that regard. Traces of left-field pop and post-punk, along with some of the project’s longstanding interest in minimal wave can still be found in the corners of these four tracks, but it’s a dark and metallic approach to body music rhythms which holds sway (Ortrotasce might be the only other current American act pulling from the same corners, though the trajectories of the projects have been quite different). The metallic reverb which swirls above the snares of “Pulse Fate” might connote either vintage Underworld or possibly Sieczka’s previous work in Kill Memory Crash, while the smoky and dense waves of feedback chopped into “Stukka”‘s acidic EBM brings the underrated work of European experimentalists NTRSN to mind. Colour, funk, and a distinctly American sardonicism blur the jagged edges of Climbers‘ beats. Climbers by Circa Tapes The post Observer: Eye New Dark & Circa Tapes appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._genre: synthpop / minimal wave / EBM / darkwave / post-punk
items._cn_summary: 本乐评以Observer专栏形式同时评介两张独立厂牌作品。Eye New Dark由Null Device成员Jill Sheridan个人操刀，在保留合成器流行饱满旋律性的同时，引入更明亮甚至尖锐的音色搭配，编曲涉及琶音合成器、明快节奏编程与伦巴律动，嗓音控制力突出，收尾曲通过间断式节奏与多层人声填空展现空间感。Circa Tapes的EP则聚焦暗黑金属质感与身体音乐节律的交汇，snare上方盘旋的金属混响、粗粝的反馈波切割酸性EBM节拍，左场流行、后朋克与极简暗潮元素并存于四角，整体透露出干燥的美式冷幽默色彩。两张作品均为自发行或小厂牌出品，在合成器流行与暗潮电子的交汇地带做出了风格上的微调与延续。

items.body: Portion Control released a video for “Displaced Hybrid Refugee” on August 14, 2026, the same day their first archival box set, “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…”, arrived on Artoffact Records as a 4xCD set, a digital edition and a limited red vinyl LP. The London electronic and industrial group posted the video to their own Portion Control VMAG channel. Portion Control rebuild ‘Refugee’ as ‘Displaced Hybrid Refugee’ “Displaced Hybrid Refugee” sits at track 56 of the 77-track set and reworks “Refugee”, originally on the 1984 album “..Step Forward”. The band explain where the footage came from rather than what the song means: “This song is a rework of ‘Refugee’ and the video is built from the visuals used whenever we play it live.” It is the second rebuild of that song to surface from the project. Rhys Fulber of Front Line Assembly produced “Refugee (Rhys Fulber Rebuild)”, the first preview issued when the box set was announced. What the ‘Hit The Pulse to Purge’ box set collects The set gathers the 1983 mini-LP “Hit The Pulse”, the albums “..Step Forward” (1984) and “Psycho Bod Saves The World” (1986), the 12-inch singles “The Great Divide”, “Go-Talk” and “Raise The Pulse”, and the “Purge” EP (1986), plus B-sides, compilation tracks, rarities, remixes, demos and two concert recordings from 1984 and 1985. Paul Lavigne remastered all 77 tracks at Kontrast Mastering. Sixteen are previously unreleased and a further twelve appear on CD and digitally for the first time. The 4xCD edition comes in a five-panel ecopak with a 24-page booklet of archive photos, designed by Stefan Alt of ant-zen. The red vinyl LP carries ten tracks. 1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge… by portion control Side-Line covered the set when Artoffact announced the box set “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…” in June. Two further previews followed over the summer: the live recording “Tex-Mex”, taped at Dolce Vita in Lausanne in December 1985, and the demo “H.O.T. Matter” from the “Psycho Bod Saves The World” period. All three earlier tracks are on the box set alongside “Displaced Hybrid Refugee”. The 4xCD box, the LP, the digital edition and a run of six vinyl test pressings are sold through Bandcamp. The set is also on Spotify, Apple Music and Amazon Music, with physical copies handled in the UK by Lexer Music. Portion Control live dates October 24, 2026 – Zwickau, Germany – Elektrisch Festival July 1-4, 2027 – Canterbury, United Kingdom – Shadowlands About Portion Control Portion Control formed in South London in 1979 around Dean Piavani, Ian Sharp and John Whybrew. The group built a minimal, rhythm-led sound from sequenced synthesisers, drum machines, early samplers and clipped vocals, and issued a run of cassettes before their first vinyl album, “I Staggered Mentally”, in 1982. The mini-LP “Hit The Pulse” followed in 1983 and “..Step Forward” in 1984, the year they toured with Depeche Mode. “Psycho Bod Saves The World” closed the period in 1986. Their records from these years are cited as an influence on Nitzer Ebb, Skinny Puppy, Front Line Assembly, Nine Inch Nails and Orbital. The band stopped in the late 1980s and returned in 2004 with “Wellcome”, followed by “Filthy White Guy” (2006) and “Pure Form” (2012). Side-Line spoke to them in 2020 in an interview with Portion Control, and covered the 2022 reissue of the “Dissolve” material after the original run was pressed on self-destroying discs. Three “SEED” EPs appeared between 2020 and 2025, the last of them, “SEED EP3.1”, marking the point where Portion Control joined Artoffact in late 2025. “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…” is the first box set in the reissue programme that deal set up, and “Displaced Hybrid Refugee” is the track the band chose to mark its release.

Matter》——也已先行释出。Rhys Fulber (Front Line Assembly) 亦参与制作了首个重制版本。该组合以序列合成器、鼓机与早期采样器构建极简律动导向的声音，作为英国早期工业/EBM场景的重要代表，此套档案梳理了其早期创作脉络。

items.body: Swiss pianist and composer Raphael Loher releases “Figuren” on 4 September 2026 through the Lucerne publishing platform Präsens Editionen. The eight-track album comes out digitally and as a limited vinyl edition with artwork and four inlays by Ukrainian-American artist Mykola Haleta. Loher built the record from his own concert recordings rather than from new performances. The tracks are titled “Figuren I” through “Figuren VIII”. Figuren by Raphael Loher How Raphael Loher made ‘Figuren’ The source material is ten intimate concert recordings of Loher performing pieces from “Keemuun”, his debut album. He took those tapes into a residency in the Blenio Valley in Ticino, where he separated out individual melodies, tones and resonances and reassembled them into new configurations. That work produced around thirty initial pieces and also fed his second album, “Hug of Gravity”. He then ran the fragments through a Revox B77 tape machine, shifting their pitch before digitising and reshaping them again. The results range from layered rhythmic microstructures to sparse melodic fragments and long looping passages. Präsens Editionen describes the album as “shaped by intuition, experimentation, and a deliberate distance from his primary instrument – the piano.” Loher expands the piano itself with preparations, effect pedals and tape, which puts the record closer to ambient and electronic composition than to solo piano recital. Raphael Loher live dates 2026 Loher tours Europe from the release date onward: 4 September – Meakusma Festival, Eupen, Belgium (solo) 5 September – Bad Bonn Kilbi, Düdingen, Switzerland (solo, and with Remo Helfenstein) 12 September – Trial & Error Festival, Tribute to Franziska Lingg, Lucerne, Switzerland 30 September – Periscope, Lyon, France (solo) 3 October – Festival Pour Les Oiseaux, Le Havre, France (solo) 30 October – Heiliggeistkapelle, Lucerne, Switzerland (solo) About Raphael Loher Raphael Loher is based in Lucerne, Switzerland, and combines experimental electronic music, ambient and minimalist composition in his work. His debut solo album “Keemuun” came out on three:four records in October 2022. His second, “Hug of Gravity”, followed on the Swiss experimental label Hallow Ground in 2025. He plays in two trios. Baumschule pairs him with guitarist Manuel Troller and drummer Julian Sartorius for long-form improvisation, also released through three:four records. KALI Trio, formed in 2015 with guitarist Urs Müller and drummer Nicolas Stocker, released its third album “The Playful Abstract” in early 2025, and co-wrote the score for “Nemesis”, the documentary by Swiss director Thomas Imbach, alongside Lukas Langenegger. Loher has also played and recorded with Gerry Hemingway of the Anthony Braxton Quartet and with Martina Lussi. He has toured across Europe and appeared at the Montreux Jazz Festival, Willisau Jazz Festival, Cully Jazz Festival, One Of A Million Festival, Jazzfestival Schaffhausen and Unerhört Festival, among others, and his records have been played on BBC 6 Music and BBC Radio 3. “Figuren” is his third album and his first for Präsens Editionen, a Lucerne platform founded in 2011 that publishes magazines, books and records. It moves his catalogue further from live piano documentation and towards tape-based composition.
items._cn_summary: 瑞士钢琴家与作曲家Raphael Loher的新专辑《Figuren》以独特的解构与重组方式完成：素材并非新录音，而是取自其首张专辑《Keemuun》的十场现场录音。他将磁带带入提契诺州Blenio山谷的驻留项目，从中分离出独立的旋律、音色与共鸣，重新编排成全新结构。片段随后经过Revox B77开盘机变速处理，再数字化重塑，形成从层次化节奏微结构到稀疏旋律碎片乃至长段循环段落的多样形态。Loher通过钢琴预备、效果器踏板与磁带操作扩展了钢琴本身的表现力，使作品更接近氛围与电子作曲范畴。专辑由卢塞恩独立出版平台Präsens Editionen发行，同时推出含乌克兰裔美国艺术家Mykola Haleta设计的限量黑胶版。

items.body: 《光よ、灯火の息吹よ》《ゲンブリ奇想曲》《リラ》 Text by 浦部 雪(Yuki Urabe): Guest 先月の記事で今月は2作品をご紹介するというように書きましたが、掲載を考えていた2作品に関連したものを含めた計3作品について書こうと思います。 3) 光よ、灯火の息吹よ (2025) Venne la luce, un soffio della luce 編成： イングリッシュ・ホルン、ヴィオラ 初演： ルツェルン・フェスティバル・アカデミー in JAPAN 2025 2025年11月29日 ハクジュホール 佐竹真登(Ehr.)、迫田圭(Va.)の各氏による https://youtu.be/R_HkPJJQIbU 演奏は上述のもの KAJIMOTOと文化庁による若手音楽家育成プロジェクトの一環として行われた演奏会に向けて書かれた作品。 同年8月にスイスのルツェルン・フェスティバルへと石川健人さん、中瀬絢音さん、田中弘基さん（以上作曲）、齋藤友香理さん（指揮）、そしてメンターとしてご同行された桑原ゆうさん、小室敬幸さんらと共に行き、フェスティバルの作曲アカデミーを見学する貴重な機会をいただきました。 ルツェルン・フェスティバルには個人的に以前も何度か行ったことがありましたが、講習会の中へのアクセスはそれまで叶いませんでしたので大変ありがたく、そこでそれぞれが大胆に内面をさらけ出すプレゼンテーションをしそれに対し真摯に言葉を交わし合う世界中から集まった受講生の侃侃諤諤の様には大きな刺激を受けました。それと共に期間中に行われたLucerne Festival Contemporary Orchestraとジョナサン・ノットさんによるコンサートのためのリハーサルも見学させていただいたのですが、ノットさんのまるで魔法のような指揮によってブーレーズの『Répons』を奏するオーケストラが文字通り踊っていたことを鮮明に記憶しています。そういう風にブーレーズを聞けるとは全く想像していませんでしたので、本当に強烈な衝撃でした。 この11/29のハクジュホールでのコンサートは、ルツェルン・アカデミーの作曲セミナーに受講生として参加していた作曲家の中から4名を我々が現地で選び、そこに日本から派遣された我々4名の聴講生とメンターである桑原ゆうさんと藤倉大さん（ルツェルン・フェスティバル委嘱作曲家、メンターとしてイギリスから参加）の作品の計10作品を並べて演奏するというものでした。 8月にルツェルンへ行っていた時、1日だけ空いていたフリーの時間を使い、日帰りで以前の留学先であるミラノへとFlixbusで行きました。その目的こそがサンタンブロージョ教会を訪ねることで、ルツェルンへと日本から発つ前からこの作品を書こうということが頭の中にあり、そのためになんとしてでもヨーロッパ滞在中にミラノへ行くことを決めていたのです。 聖アンブロージョとは4世紀に活躍しミラノ司教を務めた聖人で、つまりは6世紀に活躍した聖グレゴリオよりも先の時代を生きた聖人でした。留学中ももちろん教会を訪れたことはありましたが、改めて見る教会の空気と美しさと響き、そして最奥に眠る聖アンブロージョの遺骨は、過去から未来へ長い時間続いていくそこで生きる人々の力強い営みを感じさせるのには、短く局所的な滞在ではありましたがあまりにも十分なものでした。その聖アンブロージョの作曲したと言われている‟Deus Creator Omnium”が宙に霧散していきまた最後に形を取り戻していくというこの作品の構造はその教会の中で見つかった種から育ったもので、その後書き上げるまでは多くの時間はかからなかったように記憶しています。 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Lz4iklIQGo&list=RD3Lz4iklIQGo&start_radio=1 ハクジュホールでの本番では、佐竹さん迫田さんのお二人には本当に感動的な演奏をしていただきました。教会で歌われる聖歌をイメージした作品でしたから、ハクジュホールの豊かな響きも大きな助けとなり、空気をたくさん含んだ温かい演奏に思わず胸が熱くなる思いでした。作品の途中で長く続くホワイトノイズを多く含む場面、そしてその後に聖歌が段々と霧が晴れるように聞こえてくる音の景色は、霧の出た夜に乱反射した月からの光を見て不意に感じた長大な時間の経過と人の作った歴史に思いを重ねて見えてきたものでした。 編成：フルート（アルトフルート）、オーボエ（イングリッシュホルン）、B♭クラリネット（バスクラリネット）、ファゴット、３カルカバ、ヴァイオリン、ヴィオラ、チェロ、コントラバス 初演： 浦部雪作曲個展 2025年12月19日 トーキョーコンサーツ・ラボ 内山貴博(Fl.)、大木雅人(Ob.)、西村薫(Cl.)、坪谷陸(Bn.)、安藤巴、岡田満里子、沓名大地(Perc.)、田中里奈(Vn.)、永田薫(Va.)、北嶋愛季(Vc.)、山本昌史(Cb.)の各氏による https://youtu.be/PzwjHi4UN-o 演奏は上述のもの この二つの作品は「連作」というほどに密接な繋がりがあるわけではないのですが、モロッコのグナワという人々の持つ文化からモチーフをもらっているため、同じ枠組みに属する作品と言えます。そのために2作品をまとめてここに書き記したいと思います。 始まりは長く仲良くしている北嶋愛季さんからの委嘱によります。チェロソロのための短めの作品で、チェロでやってみたいと思っていることをやってほしいというリクエストを受けました。そのようなリクエストを受けたものの、なかなかチェロでやってみたいことというものがすぐに思い付かずしばらく考え込んでしまったのですが、調べ物の末に辿り着いた「グナワ」からこの作品が生まれることになります。近年は《Rainbow Serpent》をはじめとして、異国やその文化への自分なりのアクセスを試みる作曲をすることが多く、この作品群もまさにその範疇のアプローチで書かれたものです。 「グナワ」は主にモロッコに暮らす、西アフリカにルーツを持つ歴史的・宗教的・文化的共同体を指す言葉です。彼らの文化には、スーフィズムの影響を受けたイスラムと、西アフリカ由来の先祖崇拝や精霊信仰が融合した独特な宗教体系が見られ、とりわけ興味深いのはそれによる彼らの音楽文化です。より正確に言えば、それは単なる音楽ではなく、宗教儀礼や治療の実践を含む総合的なもので、その中心にあるのが「Lila（リラ、アラビア語で「夜」の意）」と呼ばれる夜通し行われる儀式に伴う音楽です。この2作品は、まさにそのLilaの音楽や儀礼的要素から着想を得たものになっています。 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PG1pJcaUYH0 Capriccio guembrese p3 Capriccio guembrese p6 チェロソロのための《ゲンブリ奇想曲》は、Lilaでも使われるゲンブリという楽器、それをもって奏でられる音楽をチェロで模した作品です。 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=28W3XKqIKp8 チューニングを通常の5度調弦ではなく、下からC-G-C-Gにした、ただそれだけのことで全くチェロのような音に聞こえなくなったというのが実際の演奏を聞いた上で最初に感じた印象で、これは予想よりも遥かに際立ったこの作品特有の性質となりました。そのチューニングで、さらに音選びもペンタトニックしか使わないというだけで、全く西洋音楽の枠組みを飛び出した楽器にすら見えるというのは非常に興味深いことです。且つそれでも、例えば三味線のような調弦などのコンディションが同じ他の国由来のものには全く聞こえないというのは、音階や調弦だけでは到底規定され得ない、その文化の固有性たらしめるものの存在の妙を感じさせました。 Lila p1 Lila p36 Lila p122 ゲンブリやカルカバという鉄製のカスタネットを用いて行われる儀式「Lila」は、音楽、歌、舞踊、香などを通して精霊との接触による心身の癒しを目的とすると言います。その儀式の中で長時間音楽と共に踊り続ける人は「トランス」へと導かれますが、その状態こそにこの大アンサンブルのための《Lila》は焦点が当てられています。カルカバが休みなく執拗に一定のリズムを奏で続ける中、同型反復をしながら少しずつ形を変えていく音の洪水の中に身を置くと時間感覚が曖昧になり、まさに異様な精神の体験をしたように感じます。「個展」での本番の演奏家の皆さんから発せられる茹だるような熱気は今思い返しても鳥肌が立つほど、言ってしまえば恐怖すら思わせるものでした。その極限のトランス状態の獲得のためにはどうしてもカルカバが、それも複数必要だったのは疑いのないことでした。 結果として、様々なご縁の末にグナワと強い接点を持つ稲垣力さんと映画監督の栗村実さんとの出会いがあり、カルカバを貸していただくことで演奏の実現に漕ぎ着けることができました。そしてお二人とはそれだけではないこの先の様々な展開への希望も感じることができています。まだはっきりとしたことは書けませんが、こうして音楽を通して新たな縁が続いて広がっていくことに感謝を思うばかりで、このような展開が起こるとは《Capriccio guembrese》を書き始める時には夢にも思っていませんでした。 音楽によって新たな縁が生まれ、そこからまた新しい世界を知る。そして、その経験がさらに次の縁へとつながっていく。その連鎖の中に自分がいることで、自身が音楽によって生かされているということを強く実感します。今回のメルキュール・デザールとのご縁も、まさにその一つです。このような機会を与えてくださり、今回3本の記事を書かせていただくきっかけを作ってくださった齋藤俊夫さんに心より感謝を申し上げ、これをもって筆を置きたいと思います。 —————— 浦部 雪 1991年千葉生まれ。東京芸術大学作曲科卒業後ミラノ国立音楽院作曲科、ミラノ市立音楽院指揮科、ミュンヘン音楽大学作曲科にて学ぶ。作曲を安良岡章夫、野平一郎、ガブリエレ・マンカ、イザベル・ムンドリー、指揮を杉山洋一の各氏に師事。 指揮者としては日本をはじめ、イタリア、ベルギー他様々な場所で新作初演等に携わる。2021年サントリーホール・サマーフェスティバルにおいてマティアス・ピンチャー氏のアシスタントを務める。サントリーホール・チェンバーミュージック・ガーデンや紅葉坂プロジェクト等に出演。 作曲家としては芸大フィルハーモニー、Ex Novo Ensemble、低音デュオなどにより作品が演奏される。2025年12月に自身の作品個展を開催。東京芸術大学在学中に長谷川良夫賞を受賞。 公式ウェブサイト https://sites.google.com/view/yuki-urabe/
