items._cn_summary: 乐评聚焦日本青年作曲家浦部雪的三部室内乐作品。《光よ、灯火の息吹よ》为英国管与中提琴而作，灵感源自米兰圣安布洛乔教堂与早期基督教圣歌，结构上以圣咏在白噪声中消散又重聚为核心。《ゲンブリ奇想曲》为无伴奏大提琴而作，取材于摩洛哥グナワ文化的节奏与吟唱。《リラ》为大室内乐编制，延续同源的文化动机。乐评夹杂大量作者留学与采风见闻，对作品的音响特征描写有限，但清楚呈现了作品从异文化汲取材料并融入当代古典语法的创作路径，整体偏向学院体系内带有世界音乐色彩的当代作曲实践。

items.album: Coldtron2
items.excerpt: Peak Oil sublabel FO returns with a strong debut of late night, air-fried trip hop from Cold Light, flocking like moths to an illbient flame tipped FFO Jabu, Tricky, Sleepdial, Shell Company, Space Afrika. Cold Light are Bristol’s Birthmark & Withdrawn, Portland’s Best Available Technology, Rael & Eldon out of London, and Hungarian... more
items.body:
Peak Oil sublabel FO returns with a strong debut of late night, air-fried trip hop from Cold Light, flocking like moths to an illbient flame tipped FFO Jabu, Tricky, Sleepdial, Shell Company, Space Afrika.

Cold Light are Bristol’s Birthmark & Withdrawn, Portland’s Best Available Technology, Rael & Eldon out of London, and Hungarian CSNL. Some half a decade after a ‘Live at the Laundromat’ tape introduction, the collective unveil ‘Coldtron 2’, a sparingly sensuous slant on the lush pastures between trip hop, smoked-out dub soul and illbient jazz, inflected with the voices of Elaine Malone, Akeko and British-Nigerian sound designer Tony Onuchukwu. With remarkable restraint - especially considering so many hands are on board - they keep everything pared-back to creaking, atmospheric fundamentals for 40 minutes of smouldering storytelling, passing the torch across chapters of zoot-end poetic monologues, from stylised rap to spoken word, in a spectrum of accents speaking to the group’s far flung coordinates. 

Call it downbeat neo-noir or trip hop 2.0, the sound is clearly in thrall to the ‘90s OGs - Tricky, Portishead, Massive Attack - yet gauzily distinguished from its forebears by the production’s pall of dematerialised textures and an enervated feel for screwed subs and glimmers of sounds that emerged in trip hop’s fall-out. The Bristol night air is thick with sferic crackle and diffused sax in ’Smoke Signal’ thru the Memotone-esque eldritch of ‘Troposphere Test’, taking in a tacit nod to Mobb Deep via Tricky on the smouldering ‘Riot’, or even Civilistjävel!’s low-key electrodub in ‘Lean Wid It…’,    and Sleepdial’s slurred drums on ‘I’ve Known Fires’. But they’re most potent on ‘Fields in B’ with eight mins of smudged Rhythm & Sound steppas bass anchoring the bluest sax plumes and blunted bars, ideal for ashtray dreamers.
items._genre: trip hop / illbient / electronic / dub / neo-noir
items._cn_summary: 这是Cold Light集体——由布里斯托尔、波特兰、伦敦及匈牙利成员组成——在Peak Oil子厂牌FO发行的首张专辑Coldtron2。专辑在trip hop与illbient jazz之间开辟了一条克制而暗沉的道路，以去物质化的声音质感、拧曲的低频与弥漫的萨克斯为骨架，编织出40分钟的深夜叙事。风格上承袭Tricky、Portishead等九十年代前辈，同时引入Sleepdial式的slurred鼓点与Civilistjävel!式的electrodub肌理，配合说唱与口语的章节式人声。亮点在于八分钟的Fields in B，以Rhythm & Sound式的steppas低音托起最忧郁的萨克斯与含混的念白。多文化坐标与多语种人声为作品带来跨大西洋的地理纵深感。

items._cn_summary: 本期《The Wire》杂志呈现多组跨领域实验作品：Space Afrika以曼彻斯特-柏林俱乐部文化与七十年代地下电台网络为线索重塑声音地图；黎巴嫩作曲家Jad Atoui聚焦植物与硬盘的内在运转；葡萄牙作曲家Nuno Canavarro回顾其1988年 cult专辑；韩裔音乐人Lucy Liyou以板唱（pansori）剧场元素结合语音合成技术探讨身份议题。唱片评论部分涵盖自由即兴、前卫摇滚、当代古典、电子实验与世界音乐等多条线索，包括Ivo Perelman的多组即兴合作、Tyshawn Sorey与Pat Thomas的钢琴对话，以及多组来自不同国家的地下实验项目。整体内容偏重即兴与声音探索，地理覆盖广泛。

items.album: The Remains: Short-Run Regional Releases from the Lao People's Democratic Republic
items.excerpt: Colour us enchanted with this otherworldly hour of airborne flute, Saw-U, vocal and drum spirits sourced from the night markets, museum shops and cafés of Laos, by Gary Sullivan ov Bodega Pop, who aptly compares them with Laurent Jeanneau’s forays in the same zone of interest for Akuphone & Sublime Frequencies. Check for... more
items.body:
Colour us enchanted with this otherworldly hour of airborne flute, Saw-U, vocal and drum spirits sourced from the night markets, museum shops and cafés of Laos, by Gary Sullivan ov Bodega Pop, who aptly compares them with Laurent Jeanneau’s forays in the same zone of interest for Akuphone & Sublime Frequencies. Check for the uncanny frissons of ‘Lam Cheung’ and its slew of piquant percussive works, all shimmering with the type of timeless lustre we’ve come to expect from Sullivan & DINTE’s magpie picks...

"In Lao PDR, music was seemingly everywhere. Walking through an open field outside Savannakhet to the sound of someone playing a khaen on a distant porch, the bracing rush of electronic molam from of one of Vientiane’s many aging malls, the awkward blending of the blind so u player’s voice with the bustling sounds of Luang Prabang’s night market.

It was in that UNESCO World Heritage Site that I found most of the CDs and CD-Rs from which I’ve ripped the tracks for this compilation. I’m almost certain I picked up a thumb drive at the night market that held many hours of additional music that could have been included, but if so, I’ve misplaced it, lost it for good, or simply misremember purchasing it in the first place. What I do remember is that these discs were literally the last copies in the cafe, museum, bookstore, and night market where I bought them, and not all of them played all the way through without sonic deterioration.

The sounds compiled here play in stark contrast to the more contemporary recordings I found in Laos, most of which featured some form of upbeat digital workstation molam or children’s songs. In addition to the ever-present khaen, this collection includes recordings of the sanai, a single-reed instrument fashioned from a water buffalo horn, the ceremonial khong nyai gong, the pi and similar free-reeds, and at least a dozen more traditional instruments played by Lao and ethnic minority artists. While some of these tracks were laid down in Vientiane or Luang Prabang, most were recorded near where the artists lived, from the legendary Vat Phou in the far south to the former Pathet Lao capital Xam Neua in the northeast.

Unlike Laurent Jeanneau’s more focused Lao collections for Akuphone and Sublime Frequencies, which remain among my favorite albums of all time, the present cassette-only selection is literally all over the PDR map. The sequencing is entirely in response to rhythm and texture and includes recordings from the 1970s, 80s, 90s, and early aughts. This may frustrate those with more of an ethnomusicology bent, but my hope is that the listener experiences something akin to wandering for the first time through this majestic country, encountering the last copies of forgotten recordings one after another, and hearing in these remains fragments of the past and a living musical landscape."

–Gary Sullivan (Bodega Pop)”
items._genre: world music / field recording / traditional folk / Lao ethnic music
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑汇集了来自老挝各地的稀缺录音，从夜市、咖啡馆和博物馆商店的末版CD中抢救而来，时间跨度涵盖1970年代至2000年代初。曲目以传统乐器为核心，包括芦笙、单簧管水牛角sanai、khong nyai锣仪式乐器及众多自由簧乐器，由老挝本土艺术家及少数民族音乐人演奏。编曲者Gary Sullivan将选曲按节奏与质感排列，强调田野录音的原始质感与年代层次，部分曲目带有物理磨损的声学痕迹。收录地横跨老挝全境，从南部的Vat Phou到东北部前巴特寮根据地Xam Neua。整体呈现一种漫游式的聆听体验，介于民族志档案与个人收藏之间，与Laurent Jeanneau在Akuphone及Sublime Frequencies的同主题探索形成对照。

items.album: Geffen
items.excerpt: 15th Anniversary Remaster of Barnt’s "Geffen" via Magazine. "Cologne-based record label Magazine celebrates the 15th anniversary of Barnt’s visionary anthem Geffen. One of electronic music's most defining tracks of the 2010s will be reissued in a 2026 remaster edition, marking the first time it receives its own dedicated... more
items.body:
15th Anniversary Remaster of Barnt’s "Geffen" via Magazine.

"Cologne-based record label Magazine celebrates the 15th anniversary of Barnt’s visionary anthem Geffen. One of electronic music's most defining tracks of the 2010s will be reissued in a 2026 remaster edition, marking the first time it receives its own dedicated standalone release.

Originally published on the legendary Cómeme imprint as part of the Various Artists EP The Power Of Now, the track rapidly became a global phenomenon. Looking back, one can hardly imagine Geffen without the 2010s, or, conversely, maybe even electronic music of that era without it. The composition mirrors the expressive possibilities of bedroom producers at the beginning of that decade—an era where artists could launch tracks into the world and have them resonate through their sheer sonic power, without major marketing efforts.

Barnt remembers: "It was one of my earliest tracks. I had just entered art school and didn't own much equipment. My MIDI keyboard only had two octaves. I would always play notes with my right hand while simultaneously shifting through the octaves with my left. This is how the hook line came to life. The production only consisted of seven or eight stems, and barely any equalizers were used during the mixdown. In hindsight, this sparse approach to production probably made it sound different and is why it hits so hard on big sound systems (while sounding unfinished to some on YouTube). At that time, we were doing a small festival on a playground in the center of Cologne. When I played the CDR there, Matias Aguayo demanded it right after. That is how it ended up on Cómeme."

The release comes with two very Magazine-esque reinterpretations from the label's two other co-founders alongside Barnt: a powerful atmospheric club remix by Jens-Uwe Beyer, and Magazine Hallucination, a wild, collaborative, psychedelic mutation by Crato and Beyer.

Jörg Burger, who already mastered the original track, is also responsible for the mastering of this release."
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Barnt经典电子曲目《Geffen》迎来15周年重新发行版本，由Cologne独立厂牌Magazine发行2026年remaster版。该曲最初收录于Cómeme厂牌的合辑EP中，仅由七八个音轨组成，几乎未使用均衡器处理，以极简的制作手法呈现出强劲的声场冲击力。创作者在仅有双八度MIDI键盘的条件下，通过双手同时操作音符与八度切换，完成了标志性的hook line。重发版本附带两位联合创始人的重新诠释：Jens-Uwe Beyer的氛围俱乐部混音以及与Crato合作的迷幻变奏版本。整体文章偏向新闻通稿风格，内容以发行信息和创作背景为主，缺乏深入的音乐分析。

items.album: Coltrane
items.excerpt: Trane’s first album as bandleader surfaces on Craft Recordings’ guided reissue tour of classic jazz totems, spotlighting a vital period of modal jazz development from his years with the Prestige label, circa playing with Thelonious Monk and Miles Davis. Recorded in May, 1957 and published in September that year, ’Coltrane’... more
items.body:
Trane’s first album as bandleader surfaces on Craft Recordings’ guided reissue tour of classic jazz totems, spotlighting a vital period of modal jazz development from his years with the Prestige label, circa playing with Thelonious Monk and Miles Davis.

Recorded in May, 1957 and published in September that year, ’Coltrane’ marks the point when the great saxophonist began to transcend the acclaim of his peers for much wider recognition, with record sales numbers to follow suit. At the head of band including Red Garland on keys, Paul Chambers’ bass, Albert Heath on sticks, and Sahib Shihab’s baritone sax, Coltrane’s sound matures with a unique balance of smoky quintessence and modal experimentalism that would greatly inform jazz music in moving forward, outward.

That's all ideally illustrated on the daring modal suss of opener ‘Bakai’ with its switches between dervishing brass and angular rhythm to cooler stroll, and the contrast with its proceeding ‘Violets for your Furs’, and again in the closing couplet of ‘While My Lady Sleeps’ with its almost frenzied darts between the romantic and curiously exotic, and extended jazz-blues trip ‘Chronic Blues’.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Coltrane作为乐队领袖的首张录音，1957年5月录制于Prestige厂牌时期，标志着他从Miles Davis和Thelonious Monk身边的sideman逐步走向独立表达的转折点。乐队配置包括Red Garland钢琴、Paul Chambers贝斯、Albert Heath鼓和Sahib Shihab巴里内克萨克斯，整体呈现出烟雾缭绕的硬波普质感与早期模态爵士探索的混合。开场曲'Bakai'在旋转的铜管与棱角分明的节奏间切换，'Violets for your Furs'形成对比，而'While My Lady Sleeps'在浪漫与异域风情间急速跳跃，末尾的'Chronic Blues'则展开一段延伸式的爵士蓝调旅程。这张作品处于Coltrane从传统框架向更自由语汇过渡的关键节点，对理解他此后走向impulse!时期的彻底实验具有铺垫意义。Craft Recordings的再版让这段历史脉络得以重新被聆听。

items.album: revelations of divine love
items.excerpt: Lower case, gently effervescent electronica from the softer underbelly of the US scene, turning extramusical cues from the collected writings of Julian of Norwich - the earliest writing of any woman in English. “On revelations of divine love, jason calhoun’s fifth release for Dear Life Records, Calhoun has assembled an especially... more
items.body:
Lower case, gently effervescent electronica from the softer underbelly of the US scene, turning extramusical cues from the collected writings of Julian of Norwich - the earliest writing of any woman in English.

“On revelations of divine love, jason calhoun’s fifth release for Dear Life Records, Calhoun has assembled an especially potent album of work that whirrs, hums, and glows. Unlike his recent output centered around extended, hypnotic compositions, the fourteen tracks here immediately request your attention and curiosity. Their concision only underscores one of his greatest strengths: the ability to capture an evaporating, fleeting moment, and hold it close.

The title is a nod to British Anchoress Julian of Norwich, whose collected writing of the same title is the earliest of any woman written in English. Here it serves as a unifying theme for Calhoun's particular palette of restless textures and tentative melodies. This is personal music, to be sure, but it also feels tactile, almost taffy-like in its presentation—and with such a potent combination, it is hard to resist a smile while listening. Like when the insistent pulse grounding 'last one' suddenly changes color as yawning tones reveal themselves, or how 'eye dilation' tiptoes into the room with each note sounding like a carefully chosen step. Though never precious or fussy, the album remains resolutely intimate.

Calhoun puts it plainly: “Julian of Norwich says “‘All shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well’. These days, I’ve been having my doubts that this is true. As no solution to the issue at hand, I look for the revelations of divine love in my life, and I find them--in my partner asleep on the floor in our studio, my survival of a social interaction with a stranger, being bad at chess. Don't ask me what they mean-I'm still figuring that out myself. Maybe we can figure it out together.” It is from this place of doubt, searching, and openness that the album finds its footing.

When asked about the origin of the album's cover art, Calhoun explained, "I see this spot all the time on my commute home from work". A true statement of how the mundane and meaningful are interwoven, from someone who celebrates that union better than most. Unlike Julian of Norwich, Calhoun is no hermetic mystic himself-but in his daily life he works at an oncology center, doing routine but necessary work to provide treatment for those in need of it. While he might resist any analogizing, it is sincerely easy to say that Calhoun's body of work, which is only fortified by revelations of divine love, also offers care and company.”
items._cn_summary: Jason Calhoun 的第五张专辑以十四首短小精悍的电子小品组成，灵感来自英国女性作家朱利安·诺里奇的中世纪灵性文集。音乐呈现出轻盈发泡的质感与不安分的织体，旋律试探性地游走于音色边缘，每首作品都试图捕捉转瞬即逝的瞬间并将其凝固。整体风格亲密而不矫饰，节奏与音色在'last one'与'eye dilation'等曲目中不断变换色彩与层次。作者在肿瘤中心工作的日常与对神圣之爱的追寻成为专辑的内在线索，将平凡与意义的交织作为创作根基，作品既具个人化温度，又保持开放与自省的姿态。

items.album: Lost, Discarded Or Simply Forgotten (Demos 2009-13)
items.excerpt: Dalhous's first demo collection, originally released on Blackest Ever Black back in 2015. RIYL Ekoplekz, Christ or Forest Swords. Officially established by Edinburgh-based duo Marc Dall and Alex Ander in 2012, the name Dalhous was really just a formality - the duo had already been working on material together, under the name Young... more
items.body:
Dalhous's first demo collection, originally released on Blackest Ever Black back in 2015. RIYL Ekoplekz, Christ or Forest Swords.

Officially established by Edinburgh-based duo Marc Dall and Alex Ander in 2012, the name Dalhous was really just a formality - the duo had already been working on material together, under the name Young Hunting, for years. This is the era that's properly dredged up here, compiling the demos that Ander and Dall originally compiled for an Intergalactic FM broadcast, eventually dubbing it to tape to fill a gap after the release of 'Will to be Well'. And it's good material, especially if you're interested in tracking the project's evolution. Picking up where that other notorious Scottish electronic duo left off when they wrote 'Twoism', Ander and Dall are fascinated by the kind of moods that disappeared when VHS was traded up for DVD. Not completely in thrall to B-movie soundtracks and documentary themes, Dalhous prefer to muddle their sound with rusted industrial grot, amping up the distortion and making sure the beats fall neatly off the grid. At 21 tracks, it's a lot to plow through, but it's tidy listening if you've already exhausted the duo's proper albums.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dalhous的首张demo合集，收录了2012年前后两人以Young Hunting名义创作的作品，原始素材曾用于Intergalactic FM广播节目。整体氛围带有VHS时代质感的怀旧情绪，借鉴B级片配乐和纪录片主题的灵感，但刻意混入锈蚀感的工业粗糙颗粒，将失真推到极限，节拍也刻意偏离常规网格。编曲上偏好模糊和混浊的声场处理，而非清晰的电子舞曲结构。这种介于暗潮、工业和实验电子之间的声音实验，展示了Dalhous在形成完整专辑美学之前的声音探索轨迹。对于已经熟悉两人正式作品的听众，这些demo提供了追溯其风格演变脉络的窗口。

items.album: Lifestyle
items.excerpt: Reissue of the debut by A.G. Cook & Danny L Harle’s earliest duo, Dux Content, initially dispensed on Gamsonite, a predecessor of P.C. Music, and teasing out strands of makina, electro-house, bardcore and trap with combo’s of ludic, recombinant suss & sharp sound design that became their calling card. Scrolling back to what now... more
items.body:
Reissue of the debut by A.G. Cook & Danny L Harle’s earliest duo, Dux Content, initially dispensed on Gamsonite, a predecessor of P.C. Music, and teasing out strands of makina, electro-house, bardcore and trap with combo’s of ludic, recombinant suss & sharp sound design that became their calling card.

Scrolling back to what now feels like a distant world - the up-for-grabs edges of early 2010s - ‘Lifestyle’ maps out formative aspects of the two producers, still relatively fresh from music studies at Goldsmiths, and making their mark in a burgeoning “internet music” scene. Of course they’re both now chart-topping songwriters/producers with credits for Charli xcx, Dua Lipa, Oklou, et al, but here they’re positively bubbling over with wild, yet disciplined, fusions of upfront hard dance with jazz, contemporary classical and pop that, with the benefit of hindsight, place them in a contemporaneous cultural slipstream with likes of Cracksmurf/T C F or James Ferraro, and soon-to-be spar, SOPHIE.

‘Lifestyle’ is the sound of two minds scything thru cultures and sounds they grew up with - Harle coming from a family background spanning his Geordie dad, John Harle’s BBC scores and early taste for makina’s stacked melodies - and bonding over a shared love of Captain Beefheart, Archie Sheep, and Tim & Eric, all evident in their grasp of shiny, commercial hooks and complex rhythm wrapped up with daft grin and wink. Shake a wand anywhere and you’ll hit a mad one, from the crazed midi piano house of ‘Voice of an Angel’, thru the jazz-fink of ‘City Break’ and ‘Hero Next Door’, free wheeling jazz trance of ‘Heart of Death’ and pitch bent panpipes of ‘Business Class’.
items._cn_summary: 这张作品是A.G. Cook与Danny L Harle早期二人组合Dux Content的首张专辑再版，源于2010年代初PC Music前身Gamsonite厂牌。两人当时刚从Goldsmiths音乐专业毕业，将makina、electro-house、bardcore与trap等多种风格进行重组融合，呈现出狂野却克制的硬核舞曲与爵士、当代古典及流行的杂糅。专辑横跨crazed midi钢琴house、爵士trance、变调排箫等多元形态，体现出他们对Captain Beefheart等艺术家影响的吸收，以及早期互联网音乐场景中独特的实验精神。作为两人后来共同成为Charli xcx、Dua Lipa等艺人创作核心的起点，这张作品展现了hyperpop美学诞生前的雏形，对理解后续整个PC Music运动的文化脉络具有重要参考价值。

items.album: Lynboril Lisinopril
items.artist: Adam Bohman, Sue Lynch & Crystabel Efemena Riley
items.excerpt: Recorded last year, 'Lynboril Linsinopril' is a lengthy session from seasoned improvisers Adam Bohmen (on strings and amplified objects), Sue Lynch (on woodwind) and Crystabel Efemena Riley (on percussion). All members of London's Horse Improvised Music Club, Bohmen, Lynch and Riley are motivated by the act of... more
items.body:
Recorded last year, 'Lynboril Linsinopril' is a lengthy session from seasoned improvisers Adam Bohmen (on strings and amplified objects), Sue Lynch (on woodwind) and Crystabel Efemena Riley (on percussion).

All members of London's Horse Improvised Music Club, Bohmen, Lynch and Riley are motivated by the act of playing, something that's evident immediately. There's a refreshing freedom to their approach; it's relatively straightforward free improv gear, with Riley's tuff rhythm section providing an anchor for her collaborators' wildest skronk-y expressions, but breathes outside of the usual boundaries, never falling into the expected locked grooves. If you follow Cafe Oto's orbiting improv scene, this'll be worth a closer look.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是三位伦敦即兴音乐人Adam Bohman（弦乐与放大物体）、Sue Lynch（木管）与Crystabel Efemena Riley（打击乐）于去年录制的长时段即兴会话。三人同属伦敦Horse Improvised Music Club，演奏动力纯粹来自"演奏"这一行为本身。作品呈现自由即兴的典型面貌，但又不落入常规套路：Riley坚韧的节奏部为两位合作者最狂野的噪音表达提供了锚点，整体在惯常边界之外呼吸，从不滑入预期的固定律动。文本虽短，但信息指向明确：对Cafe Oto周边即兴场景感兴趣的听众，这张专辑值得深入聆听。

items.album: Sound And Experiment X Museum Brandhorst
items.excerpt: Munich’s modern art gallery Museum Brandhorst field wide ranging responses to an exhibit of works and concerts focussed on the works of John Cage, Merce Cunningham, Jasper Johns, Robert Rauschenberg and Cy Twombly, ranging from the sound poetry of Sofia Biazzi; to the sublime levitations of Maria Margolina; avant ambient... more
items.body:
Munich’s modern art gallery Museum Brandhorst field wide ranging responses to an exhibit of works and concerts focussed on the works of John Cage, Merce Cunningham, Jasper Johns, Robert Rauschenberg and Cy Twombly, ranging from the sound poetry of Sofia Biazzi; to the sublime levitations of Maria Margolina; avant ambient pop of water lily; the pulsating technoid attack of focus baby; andCaroline Kretschmer’s subaquatic intrigue.

“Museum Brandhorst has invited Sound and Experiment to create a series of performances, audio works, and concerts in relation to the exhibition Fünf Freunde: John Cage, Merce Cunningham, Jasper Johns, Robert Rauschenberg, Cy Twombly. The event took place on June 27, 2025, as part of the Junge Nacht and the opening night of the annual Kunstareal Fest in Munich. The program featured newly produced pieces by Sound and Experiment participants Sofian Biazzi, Ilinca Fechete, focus baby, Daniel Gianfranceschi, Bruno Haas, Caroline Kretschmer, Bradley Leonard, Camilla Metelka, Maria Margolina, rosi and water lily. 

In a preparatory, biweekly seminar, discussions addressed conditions such as spectrotemporal displays, sharing time and frequency domains with different sound pieces simultaneously, and eventual performance constellations. An additional point of departure was a close reading of the indirect role of American artist David Tudor in some of the positions exhibited in Fünf Freunde, the function of the organization E.A.T. (Experiments in Art and Technology), and auditory scene analysis and synthesis in general.

The pieces featured on this CD are related to the presented performances, yet newly produced and with the audio CD format in mind.”

items._cn_summary: 这是一张围绕慕尼黑现代艺术博物馆Brandhorst的展览《五位朋友》（聚焦John Cage、Merce Cunningham、Jasper Johns、Robert Rauschenberg、Cy Twombly）而策划的声音合集，由Sound and Experiment项目出品。参与者在为期数周的研讨会上探讨了频谱时域分析、听觉场景合成，以及David Tudor在展览作品中的间接作用。专辑收录的曲目均为全新制作，呼应现场演出但专为CD媒介重新构想。内容涵盖声音诗、氛围流行、技术脉冲、水下式声响探索等多种取向，整体呈现对极简主义遗产的当代回应与延伸。作品在概念上承袭Cage以来实验音乐传统，但在声音处理与媒介适配上具有当代视角。

items.album: Nuh Skin Up Dub
items.excerpt: Thee darkest, weirdest dub perennial from Keith Hudson, 1979, blooms on vinyl for first time in years, ready to scatter smoke and minds into the late and early hours... First released in 1979 and highly in-demand ever since, the dub sibling to Keith Hudson’s ‘Nuh Skin Up’ pushes that album’s already stark blooz and The Soul... more
items.body:
Thee darkest, weirdest dub perennial from Keith Hudson, 1979, blooms on vinyl for first time in years, ready to scatter smoke and minds into the late and early hours...

First released in 1979 and highly in-demand ever since, the dub sibling to Keith Hudson’s ‘Nuh Skin Up’ pushes that album’s already stark blooz and The Soul Syndicate’s deadly riddims hard into the echo chamber with a balance of experimental nous and heads-down grooves that has assured its place in the pantheon of the most haunting dubs. 

Out of print for decades until a 2007 pressing spiked it back in the water table, the album firmly holds up nearly a half century since its original release on the basis of a future proofed minimalism that continues to haunt successive generations with its bony percussion and a dematerialised soul exemplary of dub metaphysics at its transcendant best.

Up there with the likes of Lee ‘Scratch’ Perry in terms of his dual role as songwriter and desk-tweaking dub maverick, Hudson really gets inside his own tunes, and The Soul Syndicate’s instrumentals, with the uncanniest insight, turning the likes of its title corker into clouds of pillowy steppers bass and streaking echoic contrails.

The way he inverts the vocals on ‘Ire Ire’ to sound properly wrong-end-of-telescope against the foregrounded crack of congas and spectral organ is just magic, and lays the groundwork for so much dub experimentation to come from the likes of everyone from Rhythm & Sound to Tricky, along with the likes of his spellbinding, skeletal steppers dub masterwork ‘Troubles’.
items._cn_summary: 1979年发行的dub专辑终于再版面世，Keith Hudson与Soul Syndicate的演绎将原作中已经极为冷峻的布鲁斯骨架与致命律动进一步推入回声深渊。整张专辑建立在极简的瘦削打击乐之上，人声被倒置、消散、扭曲，与前景中爆裂的康加鼓和幽灵般的风琴形成超现实的听觉空间。制作人以词曲作者兼调音台操作者的双重身份深入自己的作品内部，将器乐拆分重组，制造出绵密如云的低频和拖曳着回声尾迹的声轨。既有沉稳的steppers基底，又充满实验性的声响探索，这种平衡使其成为dub美学的典范之作，影响了从Rhythm & Sound到Tricky等后世实验者。

items.album: Music To Watch Seeds Grow By 010: KiF PRODUCTIONS (Passiflora)
items.excerpt: Mu-inspired space cadets KiF Productions livicate their play of Japanese environmental ambient electronics, Hassellian 4th world, the KLF’s ‘Chill Out’, and Eno-esque harmonic perfumes, to the dearly departed Keith McIvor​. "Passiflora (Passifloraceae) is a genus of around 550 species of flowering plants, native to the tropical... more
items.body:
Mu-inspired space cadets KiF Productions livicate their play of Japanese environmental ambient electronics, Hassellian 4th world, the KLF’s ‘Chill Out’, and Eno-esque harmonic perfumes, to the dearly departed Keith McIvor​.

"Passiflora (Passifloraceae) is a genus of around 550 species of flowering plants, native to the tropical and subtropical Americas. The Passion Flower is a plant of improbable beauty - its blooms almost too intricate to be real, its climbing habit a quiet kind of determination. It has been used for centuries as a remedy for anxiety and sleeplessness, something that slows us and the world around us down.

Fresh from last year's triumphant debut by KiF; Still Out, Passiflora, the album, follows the plant from its very beginning. It opens in darkness - 'Secret of the Seed', dormant, waiting - before the first tentative stir of 'First Movement' and the long, instinctive reach of 'Seeking Light'. From there, the journey unfolds with the patience of something that has no choice but to grow: drinking, climbing, flowering. 'Song of the Vine' carries the plant's quiet insistence upward, while 'Florescence' and 'Pollination Dream' catch it at its most open - that brief, extraordinary moment of full bloom. Then the turn. 'Fruiting (Slight Return)' and finally 'Return to Earth' - the cycle completing itself, giving back what it always borrowed.

Each track is a stage. The whole is a life cycle."
items._genre: ambient / fourth world / environmental electronics / drone
items._cn_summary: KiF Productions 以日本环境氛围电子为底色，融合第四世界音乐元素与英式迷幻氛围传统，向已故 Keith McIvor（Jah Wobble）致敬。专辑以西番莲的生命周期为隐喻，从种子萌发到开花结果再到回归大地，构成一个完整的生长叙事。每首曲目对应生命的一个阶段——'Secret of the Seed'在黑暗中沉睡，'First Movement'象征萌动，'Song of the Vine'与'Florescence'捕捉攀爬与绽放的高光时刻，'Return to Earth'则完成闭合循环。整体结构遵循植物生长的天然节律，音乐像缓慢蔓延的藤蔓，具有强烈的冥想气质与生态意识。这种将植物学意象与氛围声音设计相结合的手法，使专辑兼具概念深度与听觉沉浸感，为环境音乐注入了新的叙事维度。

items.album: Around Here, The Birds Plant The Trees
items.excerpt: Ambient composer Natalia Beylis leads an ensemble of Nyahh’s finest in her landscape-shaped evocation of a field in Leitrim, Éire, quietly meditating on the natural logic of birds and trees. ‘Around Here The Birds Plant The Trees’ is Beylis’ slow-burn, long-form arrangement for quintet - Eimear Reidy (cello), Tola Custy (fiddle)... more
items.body:
Ambient composer Natalia Beylis leads an ensemble of Nyahh’s finest in her landscape-shaped evocation of a field in Leitrim, Éire, quietly meditating on the natural logic of birds and trees.

‘Around Here The Birds Plant The Trees’ is Beylis’ slow-burn, long-form arrangement for quintet - Eimear Reidy (cello), Tola Custy (fiddle), Ailbhe Nic Oireachtaigh & Ultan O’Brien (violin), and Willie Stewart (percussion) - seeded in her reading of a blackbird’s dawn chorus, and subsequent conversation with a local farmer on how “birds are the architects of the living landscape”. It follows some 40 solo albums over the past 20 years (not to mention jams with Woven Skull and Tomuttontu) with a considered approach to what lies just beyond her home; typically drawing on her attentive reading of the rural soundsphere to transmute the poetry of birdsong and the natural world into expressive musical metaphor.

The low bowed cello tone of regular spar Eimear Reidy underlines and opens out a breezy space where where the fiddle and violinists criss-cross air in reserved melodic flight and plucky figures that alternate like the play of light on Ireland’s remote North West. The piece unfolds to boggy pockets of percussion and passages of barely-there, hushed gloam, as though the wind itself was generating the players’ gestures, which rise to cloud castle hover around the midway, only to depart for Nyahh label boss Willie Stewart’s rolling drum thunder and scrape of Ailbhe Nic Oireachtaigh's fiddle rooted in the rolling landscape. Ultimately the folk soul of the turf rises in its final section, resembling a rousing, swaying folk song voiced by the strings in ideally creaky discord.
items._cn_summary: Natalia Beylis 带领五重奏根据爱尔兰利特里姆郡田野的自然环境创作了长篇器乐作品，灵感来源于黑鸫的黎明合唱以及当地农民关于鸟类塑造景观的讲述。作品以 Eimear Reidy 的低吟大提琴为基座，拉开一片清朗的空间，小提琴与提琴在其中交错飞行，拨弦与弓弦的纹理如光线在爱尔兰西北部的土地上交替闪烁。展开后引入鼓手 Willie Stewart 的沼泽质地打击，以及 Ailbhe Nic Oireachtaigh 的提琴摩擦声响。中段音乐升至云端般悬浮，随后才转入 Willie Stewart 的鼓鸣与泥煤大地般的和声运动。最终乐章回归民间音乐的灵魂，弦乐以松散的频率起伏构成一曲摇摆的民谣奏鸣。整体对自然声学环境作了细致而克制的转译。

items.album: Echospace [Detroit] Presents: "Altering Illusions" [1/3] REMASTERED
items.excerpt: Cloud-seeding dub techno sorcery x Rhythm & Sound worship by Stephen Hitchell’s cult cv313 and Radius projects, recorded in the heart of Detroit and preserved for posterity by Pole’s faithful remasters at Scape Berlin. Echospace co-pilot Stephen Hitchell mans the cockpit solo on six sterling examples of Motor City dub... more
items.body:
Cloud-seeding dub techno sorcery x Rhythm & Sound worship by Stephen Hitchell’s cult cv313 and Radius projects, recorded in the heart of Detroit and preserved for posterity by Pole’s faithful remasters at Scape Berlin.

Echospace co-pilot Stephen Hitchell mans the cockpit solo on six sterling examples of Motor City dub techno purism within the 1st volume of ‘Altering Illusions’. His hallucinatory, synaesthetic tekkerz are in palpable effect from the damp bass thru to its noctilucent synth haze, bathing bodies in blissed-out arrangements that unfold up to 20 minutes in length, as with the echoes of BC’s ‘radiance’ registered in expansive parting piece ‘standing still’, and dredged up from drizzly depths on the cv313 rewire of Radius’ ‘Interpolation Tapes’.

Clubs are in the rearview for an 80 min trip deep under the hood of Echospace’s classic sound, fathoming deepest levels of sunken subs and elemental attrition on ‘i s i s’, and hingeing on Rhythm & Sound’s skankers' templates in ‘hypnosphere’ and mesmerising metallic resonance of ‘irradiate’, while ‘above clouds’ rises above the weather system into clearer, blue-skied dub techno lushness; think post-storm Lake Erie panoramas diffused by Wolfgang Voigt’s GAS.
items._cn_summary: Stephen Hitchell以cv313名义独立操刀，在底特律完成了六首dub techno作品，专辑《Altering Illusions》第一卷由柏林Scape厂牌以Pole监制的remaster工艺重新呈现。每首曲目时长可达二十分钟，以潮湿的低频骨架与夜光般的合成器雾气构建空间感，律动借鉴Rhythm & Sound的skank模板，同时延伸至更深层的sub-bass与极简声响雕塑。曲目编排从深沉的水下氛围逐渐过渡到开阔的高空dub质感，尾声借鉴BC厂牌作品的放射感余韵，并通过Radius项目的cv313版本回溯磁带质感。整体定位为俱乐部之外的长时间沉浸聆听，以GAS式的环境弥漫与底特律dub purism为核心美学。

items.album: aa in reverse
items.excerpt: Derek Bailey, Loren Connors and Bill Orcutt fiends will be in their element with Nathan Roche’s 2nd salvo of experimental twangers for a resurrected Celluloid; the legendary label with roots in post-punk & NYC mutations, who would also issue ‘The Lambada’ - the biggest selling global single of ’89. Hailing to France, via... more
items.body:
Derek Bailey, Loren Connors and Bill Orcutt fiends will be in their element with Nathan Roche’s 2nd salvo of experimental twangers for a resurrected Celluloid; the legendary label with roots in post-punk & NYC mutations, who would also  issue ‘The Lambada’ - the biggest selling global single of ’89.

Hailing to France, via Townsville, North east Queensland, and Sydney, Australia, Nathan Roche has carved out an uncompromising catalogue of guitar abstractions since the ‘00s with myriad outfits, including turns on Siltbreeze, London’s World of Echo, and France’s excellently titled Gone With The Weed label.

After helping reboot the Celluloid label with his very psych-garage-rock LP ’35 Rue du Théâtre’ in 2025, the dozen succinct bits of ‘aa in reverse’ mark a sharp departure from the classic composure of his previous works, and into fractious deconstructions of blues guitar vernacular, very much in the vein of iconoclasts, Derek Bailey, Bill Orcutt, or Tetuzi Akiyama, but accented with his own twang.

In this abstract blues mode Nqthqn reserves the right to really jangle and pluck the listener’s nerves in tart, prickly expressions that favour microtonality and dissonance over more consonant, Western pleasures. The warp and weft of his material snags from the off with the distended notes of ‘astra’ thru the rudely detuned mix elegance and grunt in ‘aa’, pulling into Loren Connors-esue midnight melancholy on ‘aka’ and relatively stretching out into 3 mins of curdled to finely melodic chops on ‘adversary’.
items._genre: experimental guitar / free improvisation / abstract blues / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: 澳大利亚吉他手Nathan Roche在这张专辑中对布鲁斯语言进行激进解构，十二首短小精悍的曲目以微分音和不协和音取代传统调性，尖锐的触弦与微颤的反馈构成张力。作品横跨多个情绪区间：从'astra'的拉伸单音到'aa'中失调的粗粝质感，再到'aka'的深夜忧郁和'adversary'三分钟的即兴摸索。整体思路延续了Derek Bailey、Bill Orcutt等吉他即兴大师的脉络，但保留了演奏者自身的乡村律动底色。专辑由后朋克传奇厂牌Celluloid复活后发行，延续了该厂牌对都市音乐异端的关注传统。

items.album: Disco Devil Vol. 3 (5 More Classic Discomixes From The Black Ark Studio 1977-9)
items.excerpt: All killer, no filler trotters from a golden period of Lee ‘Scratch’ Perry’s foundational work at fabled studio, The Black Ark. This 3rd in a prized series spies the wee madman conjuring multidimensional spectres from vocal recordings of regular spars: Max Romeo, The Jolly Brothers, Leroy Sibbles, The Mistic, and Devon Irons... more
items.body:
All killer, no filler trotters from a golden period of Lee ‘Scratch’ Perry’s foundational work at fabled studio, The Black Ark.

This 3rd in a prized series spies the wee madman conjuring multidimensional spectres from vocal recordings of regular spars: Max Romeo, The Jolly Brothers, Leroy Sibbles, The Mistic, and Devon Irons. Perry’s visionary, innovative application of studio-as-instrument tekkerz come to the fore in the music’s layered diffusions, which we may take for granted in contemporary music, but was radical back then, and whose uncanny appeal has only steeped with age. 

Including a solo standout in the ghostly, harmonised roots wooze of his ‘Dread Lion’ gem as King Scratch, it spans the signature, lysergic sparkle of his ‘Conscious Man’cut with The Jolly Brothers, thru a stepping 12” mix of Max Romeo’s ‘Norman’ (1978), and heat-hazed sway to Leroy Sibbles’ ‘Garden of Life’, along with The Mistic’s eyes-down devotional ‘Forward With Jah’, and sloshing nyabingi of ‘When Jah Comes’ for Devon Irons.
items._genre: dub reggae / discomix / experimental production / roots reggae
items._cn_summary: 这是Lee 'Scratch' Perry在传奇黑方舟录音室黄金时期作品的第三辑精选，收录了1977至1979年间与Max Romeo、The Jolly Brothers、Leroy Sibbles、The Mistic、Devon Irons等多位合作者的混音作品。Perry将录音棚作为乐器来操控，对人声录音进行多维度的解构与重组，创造出层层叠加的声场扩散效果。这种在当时极具前瞻性的制作手法，在当代音乐中虽已被广泛沿用，但其独异魅力反而随时间沉淀愈发浓郁。专辑横跨多种风格，既有The Jolly Brothers合作曲中迷幻的根源雷鬼光斑，也有Max Romeo曲目的律动十二寸混音，Leroy Sibbles作品的闷热摇摆与Devon Irons的浓重尼亚宾基鼓击各具色彩，加上Perry以King Scratch身份呈现的'Dread Lion'独唱佳作，展现了其作为制作人的多面创造力。

items.body:
Techgnostic pied piper of Latin club, Tra Tra Trax co-founder Verraco hustles a class handful of techno, electro and hard groove bustlers for German compilation series The Third Room.

The Colombian producer-DJ takes The Third Room’s brief, to create a “place where different cultures existing and correlating to each other, mix and transform into hybrids” his own way, after precedents laid by Oscar Mulero, Freddy K, and GiGi FM, among others.

An exclusive ’Stone Version’ of Substance & Vainqueur’s 2007 dub techno ace ‘Libration’ opens a set spanning Skee Mask’s frisky deep techno swanger ‘Clear Sky 909’, thru the shearing sound design of Verraco’s own ‘Untitled (Teamgeist Mix)’, to the polyrhythmic hard groove charge of LA’s 1morning, and compatible tackle of ‘PatumPa’ by Monterrey, Mexico’s Regal86.

items._cn_summary: 这是德国The Third Room厂牌推出的合辑系列第三辑，由哥伦比亚制作人Verraco（Tra Tra Trax联合创始人）担纲选曲。合辑主题围绕不同文化的碰撞与交融，Verraco精选了techno、electro和硬律动风格的作品。开场是Substance & Vainqueur 2007年dub techno名曲的独家'Stone Version'混音版，中间穿插Verraco本人带有剪切式声音设计的作品，结尾收入洛杉矶1morning的复合节奏硬律动作品以及墨西哥Monterrey厂牌Regal86的兼容之作。选曲逻辑体现出拉丁俱乐部场景对欧洲techno传统的重新解读，融合了声音设计的实验性处理与跨地域的地下俱乐部美学。

items.body: MoE, the vocals, guitar and bass duo of Guro Moe and Håvard Skaset, is one of the most interesting rock acts around today, merging aggression and a punk attitude and with a love for improvised and experimental music. On this release they're joined by frequent collaborator Ikuro Takahashi on drums and alto saxophonist powerhouse Signe Emmeluth. While collaboration and experimentation are to be expected with this band this record is notable for mainly two reasons: it was recorded live in concert (which came as a surprise to me because their chemistry is so great that I'd assumed a lot of their records were recorded live) and it's the first MoE album in which frontwoman and backbone of the band Guro Moe trades her trusty electric bass for a double bass. While each of the six untitled tracks has its own identity, the album is a full gig recording with the dynamics of a concert as a consequence. After a short minute of mood setting and acclimatization the four musicians get straight to business with pummeling, fluid drumming, furious guitar bashing and driving bass setting the stage for Emmeluth to shine on her sax. This no holds barred first track immediately shows just how tight this band is and will be throughout the album, the especially fantastic interplay between the sax and the guitar being a highlight. The second track brings the energy down a bit and rests on Moe's signature bass playing, simultaneously gluing the band together and laying down a delightfully off-kilter groove. Takahashi and Skaset take a step back, the former focusing mainly on the cymbals and the latter turning his guitar into something that resembles a synth pad, leaving the bass and sax to their polyrithmic dance. Track four, the midpoint of the concert, introduces hints of psychedelia, with its effects-heavy guitar and a saxophone that at times sounds like a half-remembered dream, but the music and the mood are in constant evolution and the underwater feeling is soon spirited away by a massive bowed bass riff and a desperate shriek. In the latter half of the album the music takes on a mysterious quality and something else takes center stage: Moe's fantastic vocal performance. While the vocals and lyrics are present throughout the record (MoE is a rock band at their core at the end of the day) it feels like at a certain point all four musicians collectively decide to give priority to the vocal performance for a while. And what a performance it is! Full of passion, melody and angst, ranging from hissing whispers to operatic highs, often in conversation and sync with Emmeluth's altissimo notes, it's endlessly engaging and captivating Takahashi and Skaset then take on a more active role, guiding the band towards a final crescendo of distortion, blister-inducing bass playing and squealing sax overtones. For the second time on the record the band proves to be just as capable at bringing the energy down as building it up, something arguably harder to do convincingly, and they close the concert out with a slithering bowed bassline enveloped by Moe's soaring vocals. All four musicians are extremely talented and have a very assertive voice. The challenge for the band then becomes creating music that's balanced and doesn't particularily revolve around any one musician and I think they pass this challenge with flying colors. The players know exactly what and when to play, when to be active and when to play support in order to serve the music first and foremost. Emmeluth in particular is fantastic at exchanging ideas with the others, always picking the right notes to embellish a guitar chord or supporting a vocal melody,. There are no flashy solos or traditional jazz or even rock forms, just collective creation of a kind of music that revolves around attitude and emotion. It's an elating, moving and lively album, beautifully recorded and presented. I hope to hear this lineup together again soon. Released on digitally and on CD by Conrad Sound . Live at Børsen Kulturhus by MoE & Ikuro Takahashi featuring Signe Emmeluth Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以室内乐编制为核心，将古典器乐（大提琴、小提琴、钢琴、单簧管、巴松）与摇滚元素结合，呈现典型的RIO/Avant-Prog风格。七首曲目采用套曲结构，从阴暗的室内乐前奏展开，经历中世纪风格段落、复调对位、主题变奏、即兴钢琴独奏，最终以室内乐尾声收束。乐评者特别强调了乐器间的复杂对话——小提琴与钢琴的抗衡、弦乐与巴松的衔接、不同段落间的突然转折以及多主题交织的变化。整体编排以器乐组合为驱动，注重结构感与即兴段落并置，适合对前卫融合与当代古典交叉领域感兴趣的听众。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — ASCETA, the "ascetic ones" have emerged from their chamber prog hideaway somewhere in the the regionof the greater Santiago metroplex in Chile only to unleash their third lauded release THE FOOLLEADING THE BLIND which continues their uncanny ability to channel their inner Univers Zero, ArtZoyd, Rational Diet and other prerequisite classic chamber music oriented RIO acts that have keptthe musical underground electrified for the past half century. As an octet of classically trainedmusicians undergoing Cirque du Soleil musical acrobatics, this band weaves a conceptual tale offalse leadership through mass manipulation in an all-instrumental processions of classic avant-prog,chamber rock and avant-garde angularity. The album opens with the band's most energized and ambitious effort yet, the 21 1/2 minute titletrack which tackles the classic prog excesses in full dynamics. A versatile enigmatic excursionthrough a never-ending labyrinthine maze of motifs and crafty cadences, ASCETA goes for the progjugular right from the get go which continues the band's amazing display of instrumental interplaysounding like a seasoned symphony that has been in existence for decades but in actuality only amere six years in the making. With epic grandeur and bassoon-backed blazing bravado the title trackcatapults ASCETA to the top ranks of modern chamber prog, an exhilarating entryway to the band'sthird offering but also a bit of a false climatic start as it steals the thunder from the rest ofthe album's playlist.Although it swallows up nearly half of THE FOOL LEADING THE BLIND's playing time of 53 minutes, thetrack finally cedes to the following "Temple Of Mirrors" which offers a mesmerizing shorter arrayof twisted melodic constructs along with rock guitar grittiness and eccentric time signature changesrun amok, the quintessence of wily crazy complex prog along with dark and angsty atmospheres. "WhenThey Arrive" serves as the album's, uh ballad perhaps? A slow eerie and oozing instrumentalpowerhouse that remains true to the complexities of the album's true nature albeit with a touch ofmelancholic surrender. "Everything Stopped" on the other hand delivers a more bombastic introfollowed by a phantasmic slower procession of alternating instrumentation that has been compared toa cinematic score that offers an intensity that deserves some sort of visual counterpart. The albumends with the 10-minute closer "Momento Mori" which offers some of the strongest polyrhythms andavant-prog excess.Another strong album by one of South America's most dedicated chamber prog acts on par quality withthe greatest since the advent of the style's hybridizing effects that were spawned by the greatHenry Cow. An active album indeed as an inattentive listening session may result in jet lag howevercareful dedication to the procession of sounds that emerge will result in a most satisfying displayof modern avant-chamber prog in the finest of forms. If any complaints are to be made, i guess itfeels that ASCETA is very much going through the motions as traditionalists rather than offeringsome new stylistic rejuvenation and as mentioned, the title track seems to usurp the remainingalbum's intensity however despite a few nitpicking quirks that keep it from perfection, ASCETAcontinues to generate some of the most brilliant doses of this musical style since Rational Dietfolded in 2010. Add to that the entire concept thing seems a bit contrived as it seems like a progcheck list feature that really has no relevance to this music that seems to meander wherever itfeels. Nevertheless, amazing musicianship and captivating music.

items._cn_summary: ASCETA 是一支来自智利圣地亚哥都会区的八重奏室内前卫乐团，由受过古典训练的乐手组成，2026年推出第三张专辑《The Fool Leading The Blind》。整张专辑以纯器乐方式讲述关于虚假领导与大众操纵的概念故事，音乐风格延续 Univers Zero、Art Zoyd、Rational Diet 等经典 RIO 室内乐前卫血脉。开篇同名曲长达二十一分钟半，是全专最具野心与能量的作品，以巴松支撑的炽烈音响、迷宫般繁复的主题动机与节奏变化贯穿始终，颇有史诗级交响乐团的气象。随后的《Temple Of Mirrors》以扭曲的旋律结构与硬朗的吉他质感呈现紧凑的复杂节拍；《When They Arrives》放缓为阴郁黏稠的氛围段落，带有忧郁的克制张力；《Everything Stopped》则以恢宏引子衔接如电影配乐般的层次铺陈；终曲《Momento Mori》汇聚了全专最强的复合节奏与前卫锋芒。乐评认为此作是南美室内前卫领域近年最具分量的出品之一，与 Henry Cow 开创的杂交传统处于同一水准，但需要高度专注的聆听投入方能完整接收其层次。

items.body: Review by XixoTheRock — Rodrigo San Mart�n is mostly known as an argentinian niche, musician oriented content creator, hehas a decent presence on the community and has, alongside bands like Qu�sar (which I've reviewedpreviously) organized progressive rock festivals in the recent years, he's a relevant figure in theargentinian underground scene although his music remains relatively obscure, he currently works as amusic teacher.He's had a LOT of projects both solo and band oriented, and as he himself has stated, for a while heleft music and composed only to himself, due to the lack of commercial success and recognition,which is a sad assessment of the reach and interest of the general public on prog rock. Still hiswork remains high quality and interesting, this, "Otro d�a en la distop�a" is his latest LP release,it dwells on relevant topics ranging from surveillance states, algorithmic numbness, the destructionof communities and life after the pandemic...therefore, it *will be a strongly emotional album*.As it is my tradition, I would like to start off by dissecting the quality of the compositionsthemselves, which, is quite consistent throughout the entirety of the album's run-time. The range ofthe compositions oscillates between two (theoretically as in practice it *works*) opposing forces :Heavy, energetic and aggressive vs emotional, quiet and intimate music. These 2 blocks are bestrepresented by the 2 opening tracks, "Las palabras que negu�" (a track that opens and closes thealbum as it's split in two parts, just as "Shine on you crazy diamond" and "The sky moves sideways"were) is by far the album's emotional core, intimate, slow and deliberately tension-building, thetrack relies on a piano and guitar leitmotifs alongside sensitive, jazz, tango and ballad likerhythms overlaped with ambient textures, the track builds tension that is released with a swirlingand bluesy guitar solo, a feeling which inspires images of cozy blankets on an otherwise bad day, itresembles Pink Floyd and Porcupine tree's early works (I didn't mention them just as a fun fact!)and the small acoustic moments are like the golden hour, this bloc of (mellow) songs can beinterpreted as representations of a decaying humanity and the mental health crisis we are currentlyexperiencing as a society. On the other bloc, the title track "Otro d�a en la distop�a" is heavy,flute leaning (very akin to bands like Jethro Tull and Spanish band M�go de �z) and has a hightempo, aggressive playing and lots of distortion, with a slower paced yet still as energetic chorusthat has a mellotron in it, it represents the aggressive most machine like side of modern society...despite that, I consider the actual heavy song of the album is "La mirada que devuelve el reflejo"which has an absolute killer riff. Overall, the compositions are all very interesting and consistentin quality, each one is creative and takes a spin on already established music tendencies,therefore, despite being progressive, they are actually quite easy to digest, this recalls an auraof bands like argentinian group "Sui generis", and Spanish bands "Extremoduro" and "Asfalto", everysingle track is quite enjoyable and they all keep the same emotional core which is an aura ofnumbness, loss, confusion, fear and paranoia, I could definitely picture myself reading HoracioQuiroga's works (yes I know he's Uruguayan but still) to the instrumental sections of the record.Without getting too much into the production, I can say it's crystal clear, this is incredibleconsidering the fact that, after all, this is a record that was recorded, mixed and mastered on ahome studio, settings like that don't usually end up making gourmet production but this isn't thecase, granted San Mart�n is both as technically formed an engineer and a musician. You can feel theweight and dread of every instrument and the pitches hit precisely in tune, the way the layers arearranged and programmed on the Bandcamp software is milimetrically precise, nothing is ever off abeat, the mixing is great although I could actually enjoy the album a little more if the bass wasmore audible and there's no problems like reverberation, feedback, bloated audio etc. For being aone man project, the production is as precise as if it were done by a team of professionals on agreat studio.Now...not everything is sunshine, lollipops and rainbows, this album has two fatal flaws thatseverely hurt the experience and lower the quality of the record overall, these two flaws being thelyrics and the vocals.I'll start with the vocals...and I'd like to compare it to the situation of Rush's early records,remember how Geddy Lee used to sign obnoxiously high pitched, like he wasn't breathing and superrough? Yeah that also sums up the situation of the vocals here perfectly. San Mart�n attempts tosing WAY higher than his actual vocal range and tries to keep his voice soft and heartfelt, thesetwo end up turning into a negative feedback and they both end up harming the record. His voice isdifficult to listen through most of the records, specially in those moments where he adds littlechoruses and secondary vocal lines, eclipsing the wonderful instrumentals with rough vocals. Attimes this can make you even want to stop listening to the record all together since it is so onyour face and difficult to dismiss, taking into account that San Mart�n is a professional, skilledmusician, this is also contradictory to his training, and is something he could actually improve. (As a side note, his new band "Auguria" released a single around 2 months ago, where anothervocalist is doing the singing and that only shows how prominent this problem is on his own soloworks [despite the single not being great either])The lyrics are also quite poor, despite dealing with visceral, relevant and deeply polemic topicsrelated to our new status quo, something which should result in string lyrics, they are very cliche,hollow and amateurish, not nearly as polished compared to other contemporary Hispanic bands of thisday and era like Chilean band Hesse Kassel, nor do they live up to San Mart�n's inspirations such asRoger Waters. They don't really do justice to the topics, and explore them so dimly and on such asurface level, non metaphoric ("I don't want to be one's and zero's, really? We're talking about a compatriot of Benedetti, Cort�zar and Borges...come on) way that they are not a good piece of poetry by any means. Add this tomy previous critique to the records vocals and you'll understand why I say this significantlyhinders the experience you can get out of this album.Overall, it's an album of mixed quality, technically and musically impressive but weak lyrically andthus, emotionally (as lyrics are what's most important to emotions in concept albums, with theexception of adaptations to literary works such as camel's "The snow goose"), it's something I'drecommend to symphonic rock fans but adding the nuance of it's strong downsides, it's an enjoyable record despite it's flaws, instrumentally wonderful, weak on concept execution and lyrics...it's a piece of art that will resonate more with those who value instrumentation over lyrics.
items._genre: progressive rock / crossover prog / art rock
items._cn_summary: 阿根廷独立音乐人Rodrigo San Martín发行概念专辑《Otro Día en la Distopía》，以Crossover Prog为载体探讨监控国家、算法麻木、社群瓦解与后疫情生存等当代议题。整张专辑在两种对立的情绪张力间游走：一面是钢琴与吉他主导、融合爵士、探戈与民谣节奏的私密慢板段落，氛围内省而张力暗涌，尾声以布鲁斯吉他独奏释放情绪；另一面是以长笛为核心的高速重型段落，辅以失真吉他与mellotron，呈现机械般冷峻的现代性图景。作品在Pink Floyd、Porcupine Tree、Jethro Tull、Mägo de Oz等乐队之间寻找平衡点，体现出作曲层面的连贯品质与对既有类型语言的个性化重塑。拉丁美洲独立音乐人背景与严肃的题材选择使其具备独特的文化视角，整体展现出地下前卫摇滚特有的概念完整性。

items.body: Seventeen selfish dreams Where liquid stars almost bleed The act of taking one’s own life can sometimes be caused by mistaking a passing configuration of feelings and events for the whole of existence. The mind, cornered by pain, declares that because this moment is unbearable, all moments must be so. Yet life is less like a verdict than a river: no state remains fixed long enough to become absolute. To destroy the self in order to escape suffering is to assume the self is a solid thing, when it is always changing, dissolving, becoming. The tragedy is that the decision is permanent while the despair that inspires it is not. One cannot know what new shape life might take after the next bend. Nearly a decade into Bizou’s existence, the Los Angeles band has acquired the strange advantage of interruption. After 2021’s Tragic Lover, its members dispersed: Josiah Mazzaschi formed Child Seat with Madeleine Matthews; Marisa Prietto wrote with Some Ember’s Dylan Travis; bassist Nicole Fiorentino returned to Garbage for touring. When Mazzaschi and Prietto reconvened at Cave Studio in the summer of 2025, they came back with enough distance to hear what Bizou could become. That answer begins to surface on Widow, the band’s forthcoming September EP, whose six-sided title conceit — a hexagonal prism, in the group’s description — suggests an appetite for examining a familiar object from peculiar angles. Bizou’s established vocabulary remains recognizable: shoegaze density, post-punk propulsion, synth-pop architecture, industrial pressure, and the narcotic drag of trip-hop… however, Death Mag, the record’s emotional center, makes those ingredients feel unusually exposed. The song concerns suicide, though its deepest subject may be the dangerous authority granted to a single unbearable moment. Its verses withdraw into near-private space, with the vocals carrying the bruised composure of someone trying to speak without disturbing the room. Then the chorus opens dramatically, almost euphorically, and the scale of the music changes. Despair remains present, but so does the stubborn biological fact of continuing: another breath, another measure, another chance for circumstance to alter its shape. The arrangement is elegantly devastating. Here, density becomes psychological. Guitars blur at the edges, synthesizers deepen the horizon, and the rhythm section keeps the song from surrendering to weightlessness. Suicide promises an ending to pain by treating that pain as permanent, while Death Mag places emotional certainty inside music that continually changes beneath it. The song expands and contracts, presses forward and recedes, allowing form itself to make the argument. For listeners acquainted with this particular kind of loss, its beauty may feel almost cruel; comfort comes cautiously, without slogans or easy redemption. With a reunion performance forthcoming and Widow due in September, Bizou sound newly alert to contradiction: pleasure beside grief, enormity beside intimacy, and life continuing while the mind briefly insists that it cannot. Listen to Death Mag below and pre-order Widow here: Widow by Bizou Follow Bizou: Instagram Facebook Spotify Bandcamp The post “It’s Such a Heavy Weight” — Bizou Returns With Devastating Single “Death Mag” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: Bizou 乐队在近十年沉淀后重组，发布即将问世的EP《Widow》，其中单曲《Death Mag》是整张作品的情绪核心。歌曲以自杀这一沉重命题为表层关切，深层指向的是人在某一不可承受瞬间所赋予痛苦的那种危险的绝对权威。歌词将生命比作河流而非判决，强调绝望虽真实却非永恒。编曲上延续乐队已建立的语言：shoegaze的密度、post-punk的推进、synth-pop的结构、工业的压力，以及trip-hop的麻醉感，但此次这些元素显得更为裸露。主歌退入近乎私密的低语空间，人声带着试图不惊动空气的克制伤痛；副歌则戏剧性地敞开，几近狂喜，音乐规模骤然改变。绝望与继续呼吸这一顽固的生物事实并存。密度在此具有了心理学意义，吉他边缘模糊，合成器加深地平线，节奏段落阻止歌曲彻底失重。形式本身成为论证：情绪的确定性被置于持续变化的音乐结构之内，歌曲不断扩张与收缩、前进与后退。对经历过此种丧失的听众而言，美可能近乎残酷，安慰来得谨慎，没有口号式的救赎。

items.body: Never mess with Murdoch’s society Crashing and burning oh what a pity Tracky Nike fourth reich vitriol spray Commonplace everyday wreck of the UK Modern life has become one long argument with a screen, a boss, a stranger, a lover, or the idiot currently screaming beneath a flag in a supermarket car park. Shaven Primates have mined the exhaustion and alchemized it into a new EP, Kill The Algorithm. The Oxford quartet turns private dependency, political resentment, male grievance, and algorithmic manipulation into four rough-and-tumble songs powered by post-punk tension, industrial abrasion, art-rock unease, and guitars that sound ready to put somebody through a wall. Saviour starts from the most private wound. Its language treats affection as narcotic relief, the beloved transformed into medicine for absences that began much earlier, somewhere around the missing mother, missing father, and the suspicion that another person might finally close the hole. The 1990s references make sense: Placebo’s bruised glamour, Nine Inch Nails’ compulsive machinery, A Perfect Circle’s heavy-lidded grandeur. The emotional centre remains ugly enough to feel dangerous. Love becomes dosage, fantasy becomes diagnosis, and the repeated appeal to a saviour keeps curdling into evidence that salvation has been outsourced to somebody equally mortal. Pioneer Way drags that anxiety into public, where the nervous breakdown has flags tied to the lamp posts. The track takes aim at a Britain of workplace exhaustion, tabloid conditioning, immigrant scapegoating, screen addiction, and everyday fury looking for a body to blame. There is something grimly comic about a man screaming at an indicator while the country around him rehearses imperial fantasies beside a roundabout. The Sex Pistols influence is less about imitation than permission: permission to sneer at the pageantry, to notice how easily personal failure gets repackaged as national grievance, and to turn the resulting disgust into a hook sharp enough to draw blood. Then Feed goes after the salesmen. These are the grievance merchants who discover lonely young men, tell them tenderness is weakness, sell coercion as confidence, and monetize every insecurity they helped aggravate. The band brings in the clenched attack of Rage Against the Machine and Metallica, but the song’s ugliest idea is economic. Misery has become a business model. The customer is kept hungry because a satisfied customer might stop clicking. That thought detonates fully in Kill The Algorithm, where social media becomes less a tool than a delivery system for appetite, paranoia, tribal identity, and manufactured certainty. Radiohead, Black Sabbath and Iron Maiden hover in the architecture, while the repeated command at the song’s centre turns disgust into something nearly ecstatic. The target is the machine that keeps learning which wound to prod next. Listen to Kill The Algorithm below: Shaven Primates have made four songs about dependence: on lovers, on screens, on enemies, on gurus, on systems that promise relief while feeding the sickness. The riffs grind, the drums hit with factory-floor force, and the vocals move from wounded croon to open-throated accusation. The EP is held together by the recognition that private desperation and public brutality are often roommates, splitting the rent while each insists the other started the fire. Follow Shaven Primates: Instagram YouTube TikTok Facebook The post “You Prey on Those You Feed” — Oxford Quartet Shaven Primates Share “Kill The Algorithm” EP appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 牛津四人组Shaven Primates发行EP《Kill The Algorithm》，以四首粗粝的作品围绕现代社会中的依赖关系展开：从亲密关系中的情感寄托，到公共空间中的政治怨愤，再到将男性孤独转化为生意的商业逻辑，最终聚焦于社交媒体作为欲望、偏执与部落认同的输送系统。乐评将乐队的音墙与Nine Inch Nails、Placebo、Radiohead、Black Sabbath等参照系并置，指出其力量在于将私人伤口与公共焦虑转化为后朋克的紧张感、工业的磨蚀感与艺术摇滚的不安感，并融入Sex Pistols式的嘲讽与Rage Against the Machine式的攻击性。评论更接近于新闻稿与曲目解析的混合体，原创乐评深度有限。

items.body: Label: ECM Records, 2026 Personnel - Ayumi Tanaka: piano; Thomas Morgan: bass; Thomas Strønen; drums. Japanese-born, Oslo-based pianist, composer, and improviser Ayumi Tanaka presents a new trio with in-demand American bassist Thomas Morgan and Norwegian drummer Thomas Strønen. Until now, Tanaka had released two albums— Memento (2016) and Subaqueous Silence (2019)—as a leader with her former trio, featuring Christian Meaas Svendsen on bass and Per Oddvar Johansen on drums, and she’s been a wild card in Strønen’s chamber-jazz group Time Is A Blind Guide. The new trio first played together in 2024 at Oslo’s Victoria, Nasjonal Jazzscene, and Windflower consists mostly of improvised music. The album opens with the title track, which enchants with the enveloping, organic sound that stems from continuous impressionistic pianism, sophisticated bass lyricism, and the rich embrace of percussion. It is followed by “ La Source ”, an achingly beautiful ballad wrapped in idyllic contemplation. This is the only piece written by Tanaka and reveals her maturity, intelligent restraint, and fragile melodicism. Morgan brings his hypnotic bass to the fore, while Strønen injects occasional snare fluxes, deviating attention from his light-footed toms-and-cymbals maneuvers. The piece gets intriguingly layered by the end. A gentle pulse takes over “ From Us, To You ”, enhanced by muted piano hits. A tranquil aural construction flits by expertly measured brush strokes and an elucidating, supportive bass drive. This is the kind of trio that loves to let things flow naturally and spontaneously, unattached to tempo or rigid structure. The threesome integrate their sounds as a breathing whole, and that’s noticeable on the concise “ The Sea Is Still ”, introduced by Strønen’s impeccably tuned kit and unfolding with Tanaka’s shapeless fidgeting and Morgan’s unmistakable bass foundation. It’s a shame it ends so fast. “ Spring ” is another example of graceful delicacy, while “ Driftwood ” is imbued with loose freedom yet flows with a more familiar swing vibe and pace, fusing modern classical and chamber jazz elements with refined taste. Tanaka’s concept of intent anchors the ensemble’s creative abstraction. Morgan and Strønen help her flesh out atypical yet non-discordant ideas as they share their own musical perspectives. The modern, often introspective chamber textures on Windflower bring tranquilizing comfort. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Windflower ► 02 - La Source ► 06 - The Sea Is Still
items._cn_summary: 田中Ayumi领衔的钢琴三重奏专辑，由ECM于2026年发行，成员包括贝斯手Thomas Morgan和鼓手Thomas Strønen。专辑以即兴演奏为主，开篇同名曲呈现印象派钢琴、抒情低音与丰富打击乐交织的有机声响。《La Source》是田中少有的原创作品，展现出成熟的克制力与脆弱的旋律感，Morgan的低音催眠般地推进，Strønen则通过军鼓与镲片制造微妙波动。整张专辑强调三人声音的呼吸式融合，不拘泥于固定速度或结构，呈现出沉思内省的室内乐质感，现代古典与自由爵士元素以精致品味相融。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑聚焦俄乌冲突中被强制迁移至俄罗斯的两万名乌克兰儿童的悲剧，以传统民歌与原创作品交织的方式呈现。音乐以弓弦乐器为主，辅以班杜拉琴、钢琴及双陶笛，乌克兰与加拿大两组女性音乐人合作录制。歌词取材于传统歌谣关于被送往异乡劳作的少女的故事，借古喻今，映射当下被掳走儿童的命运。评论者强调，尽管题材沉重，专辑的音乐与演唱水准极高，编曲既有温柔的低吟也有阴郁激烈的段落，体现出东欧民间音乐的深沉力量与传统仪式感。这张作品以音乐为载体，将历史创伤与现实政治议题融为一体，展现了乌克兰文化在战争语境下的坚韧表达。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑汇集了圣多美和普林西比两座岛屿在七十至八十年代录制的音乐，其风格被称为Puxa，融合了merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等多种非洲葡语国家的节奏元素。乐评指出，由于岛屿面积小、录音资源匮乏，实际录制并发行的作品远少于当地音乐活动的丰富程度。多首作品展示了复杂的吉他交织层叠，主唱与和声相互呼应，贝斯与键盘时而退出舞台，将主导权完全交还给鼓组与吉他，使节奏骨架持续推进，足以支撑数小时的现场演出。文章特别提到Pedro Lima的乐队以闷音吉他的激烈riff与鼓组正面对抗，Sangazuza则展现了减法式的编排力量。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)
