items.body:
Simply lovely come-down aids by OTTO Benson, leading on from his acclaimed 2020 turn on Vegyn’s PLZ Make It Ruins with a reminder of his slept-on gem from late ’22, reissued on the NYC label behind last year’s ‘Peanut’ tape. FFO Tenniscoats, early AFX, ’00s electronica

True to the brief, Otto follows his nose for charming melodic ribbons tied in burbling rhythms across ‘Songs Before Bed’. In clearly separated halves, the first lot revolves pared-back, gently psyched guitar blessed with a sun-dazed wooze that flows from his phasing, tremolo effected licks on ‘River Dream’ thru hints of Bibio on ‘Another Long day’, and cute vignette ‘Orange Moon’. The other half is more akin his work on Vegyn’s label, sharing a timeless melodic appeal with its boss as much as sweeter ends o ‘90s AFX in the procession from endearingly naïf hook and lilting drum machine to ‘Jumping Seeds’, thru  delectable, beat-less ambient shimmer in ‘Histamine’ and the supine bewt ‘Tuning In and Out’, to the gauzy strokes of ‘Good Night Mantra’.
items._genre: ambient electronica / indie guitar / lo-fi beats
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑分为清晰的两部分：前半部分以简约迷幻吉他为骨干，使用相位与颤音效果营造出阳光慵懒的氛围，从《River Dream》的旋律线条延伸至《Another Long Day》的清新段落和《Orange Moon》的短小品。后半部分转向鼓机驱动的电子路径，与Vegyn厂牌美学相关联，旋律具有跨越时代的吸引力，参照了九十年代AFX的甜美天真气质。从《Jumping Seeds》的钩子旋律，经过《Histamine》的无鼓点环境闪光，到《Tuning In and Out》的横卧感，最终收束于《Good Night Mantra》的朦胧笔触。整体作为睡前氛围音乐定位明确，融合了独立吉他小品与轻盈电子节拍两种脉络。

items.album: Songs From The B. F. White Sacred Harp
items.excerpt: Death Is Not The End return to the soul-stir sound of deep south Sacred Harp Singers in 1993 - although it could feasibly be any time since the advent of portable tape recording - in the blessed company of the Union Grove Baptist Church, Ozark, Alabama. Feels just right in this humidity… The Wiregrass Singers' Dewey Williams... more
items.body:
Death Is Not The End return to the soul-stir sound of deep south Sacred Harp Singers in 1993 - although it could feasibly be any time since the advent of portable tape recording - in the blessed company of the Union Grove Baptist Church, Ozark, Alabama. Feels just right in this humidity…

The Wiregrass Singers' Dewey Williams began learning the shape-note tradition in his childhood. He studied under Judge Jackson, who authored the landmark 1934 hymnbook The Colored Sacred Harp. In 1971, Williams formally organized The Wiregrass Sacred Harp Singers to preserve the music full-time. This unified troupe began touring nationally and leading workshops, which ultimately launched them onto stages at the Smithsonian and Newport folk festivals up until Williams' passing in 1995 when the group disbanded. The African-American Sacred Harp tradition in the Wiregrass region has steeply declined since the start of the 21st century, due to an aging generation of singers, and today it is largely sustained through archival preservation and occasional multi-book singing meetups.

This raw recording, made at the Union Grove Baptist Church, Ozark in mid-April 1993 finds the group singing from B. F. White’s The Sacred Harp (1844), which together with his brother-in-law William Walker’s Southern Harmony (1835) formed the musical backbone of generations of Southern music and Southern musical styles.

items._genre: sacred harp / shape-note singing / a cappella folk
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑记录了1993年阿拉巴马州奥扎克联合格罗夫浸信会教堂的一次实地录音，演唱团体为Wiregrass Sacred Harp Singers。演唱内容取材于B.F. White 1844年出版的《The Sacred Harp》，与William Walker的《Southern Harmony》共同构成南方音乐传统的根基。乐评追溯了领唱者Dewey Williams的师承脉络——他师从编纂了1934年里程碑式《The Colored Sacred Harp》的Judge Jackson，并于1971年正式组建团体，致力于全时段保存这一非裔美国人圣乐传统。该团体曾巡演全国并登上史密森尼与纽波特民谣节舞台，直至1995年Williams去世后解散。文章还指出，进入21世纪后，由于演唱者群体老龄化，Wiregrass地区的非裔美国人圣乐传统急剧衰落，目前主要依靠档案保存与偶尔的多版本联合演唱活动维系。由Death Is Not The End厂牌发行，带有民间田野录音的原始质感。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由电子声学作曲家与钢琴独奏作品组合而成，收录在 Edition Wandelweiser 厂牌旗下，以极简、克制的六面板装帧呈现CD。整张专辑仅包含三个短暂的瞬间，核心是Carsten Daerr创作的温暖钢琴独奏作品，笔记中将其比作阳光映照在平静湖面上的反光，音色柔和而富有吸引力。Florian Wittenburg的电子声学创作则提供了对比性的声音维度。Edition Wandelweiser是当代古典与实验音乐领域具有独特美学主张的小众厂牌，以极简主义和沉默美学著称。该专辑适合偏好安静、内省聆听体验的听众，与学院派实验音乐传统紧密相连，但内容信息较为有限，难以全面判断其创新程度。

items.body: Norway-based producer/musician Karl Endreson’s downtempo electronic project has been active since 2006, purveying nature-inspired soundscapes mixing ambient textures and trip-hop beats with guitar and field recordings, steeped in atmosphere infused with a deep sense of melody and nostalgia. Orange Crush’s distinction is in quality control Eidolons by Orange Crush   Eidolon (/aɪˈdoʊlɒn/ Ancient Greek: εἴδωλον) – image, double, apparition, phantom, ghost; from here no great leap etymologically to the English ‘idol,’ though in ancient Greece it usually referred to a spirit-image of a person, living or dead, a shade or phantom lookalike of the human form. Album title may be significant—a knowing reference to (looka)likeness? The author may have had other ideas, sure, but be that as it may; it serves nicely as a way-in to consideration of Eidolons, 25 tracks spanning Orange Crush’s catalog, compiled, and remastered exclusively for the album, by US label Sun Sea Sky (previous S S S coverage here), with notable raids made on Halcyon Days (2020), Coastal Drive (2018), Autumn Reflections (2009) and The Fields (2006). For more about that title, read on… On the surface, Norway and Scotland have a certain affinity, which may be a factor in the eidetic relation of the music of Orange Crush to that of Boards of Canada. Norway-based producer/musician Karl Endreson’s downtempo electronic project has been active since 2006, purveying nature-inspired soundscapes mixing ambient textures and trip-hop beats with guitar and field recordings, steeped in atmosphere infused with a deep sense of melody and nostalgia. Influences are clear, and avowed, in particular BoC, other British acts from Bibio to MBV, and Danish spirit kin Syntaks and Manual (with whom OC shared a split ep (Untitled, 2008)). Likeness to BoC in others—any number of acts in three decades of IDM, from, say, Marumari and Ten and Tracer to Tycho and Clocolan—tends to be invoked in reviews with implied criticism, but the purpose here is not to bury, but to praise. Originality is but one of a number of criteria involved in evaluating a musical work, and arguably not as vital as others related to sonic and compositional sensibility. Music so closely inspired by as to be virtually derived from may recall the One on Twoism compilation series curated by the Twoism forum, a community dedicated to BoC and related, focused on various independent artists across its tracklists. However, though something of the spirit is shared, Orange Crush‘s distinction is in quality control, viz. Endreson’s ear for sound quality (see keys, guitars) and rhythm (beat tweakery), architecture and design, for all its fanboy-fueled DIY spirit, sets him apart from the cut-paste will-this-do approach of the average copyist. Notably, some Eidolons could easily have slid into the tracklist of BoC‘s Inferno (e.g. “Invocation,” “Memory Station”) and much harmless fun may be had allocating others elsewhere, e.g. “Lush Spring Feeling” to Ulrich Schnauss, “Tangerine Rush” to Casino versus Japan. Otherwise, let it be said, Orange Crush ‘evokes stillness, reflection, and connection to the natural world,’ its curators say, billing it ‘electronic music for the heart and soul’ (SUNSEASKY website), but such is the outcome of reductionism and poetics. Dancing about architecture, as some wit put it… Eidolons is available on Sun Sea Sky. [Bandcamp] Eidolons by Orange Crush  The post Orange Crush :: Eidolons (SUNSEΛSKY) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: 挪威制作人Karl Endreson的Orange Crush项目自2006年起持续创作自然主题的音景，融合氛围质感与trip-hop节拍，配合吉他与田野录音。Eidolons是横跨其多年作品的25首合集，由美国独立厂牌Sun Sea Sky独家汇编并重制，收录自《Halcyon Days》《Coastal Drive》《Autumn Reflections》《The Fields》等专辑。乐评指出其与Boards of Canada在音色与怀旧气质上的亲缘关系，并将其置于IDM谱系中讨论，但强调Endreson的差异化在于对声音品质、节奏细节与整体架构的把控能力，使作品超越了简单的风格模仿。专辑标题'幻象'的词源学引申暗示了关于相似性与原创性边界的探讨。整体而言，这是一张以品质控制见长的致敬型合集，氛围感突出，旋律性强，适合偏好电子与氛围融合的听众。

items.body: Review by tszirmay — One of my favourite US bands is Minnesota's own Ovrfwrd , a super-talented quartet whose discography has no Achilles heel. Although all the members are exceptional on their individual instruments, my very first reaction was to marvel at Rikki Davenport's exuberant and technically sound performances on the drum kit. As we all wait for their next album, the afore mentioned skin beater sent me this side-project for evaluation, which I listened to with intent. Two factors sabotaged my effort at reviewing and posting. The first was due to being completely unprepared for the stylistic difference, as is often the case with successful bands that release side or solo albums, which naturally can have a sonic slant that may wander into unchartered territories. The second was poor timing , a long European holiday followed by an avalanche of review requests, that has not abated yet in 2026. So, who are the three spirits involved anyway ? Well, we know Rikki already, so we have a fellow called Dig on bass and keyboard duties as well as guitarist Par Ljungstrom, who favours a Pat Metheny or even Andy Summers sensibility.From the very first notes on 'Dank One', its apparent that the style differs from the afore mentioned band, as it comes across as a breezy instrumental escapade with a highly organic sound, the electric guitar forging most, if not all of the lead melodies, the bass and keyboards holding down the backbone, as it is often destined to do, while the drums push it along forcefully, a few cymbal splashes for good measure. The synthesizer spotlight is a definite highlight as well, never seeking potentially off-putting wizardry, but insisting on the mood of the moment.The gentle psychedelics of 'Bin 294' provide an alternative slant as it the most developed piece even though it clocks in at 5 minutes and 15 seconds, and suggests a more groove-oriented outline, the flowing sensibility is immediately tangible on the fluttering guitar splashes, undulating bass buoys and precise percussive pontoons. As a well-crafted segue, '3 Doors' shines a feathered spotlight on the talented guitarist, who is given free reign to improvise as deemed fit, a trembling tone that skirts the edges of jazz-rock, a hint of bluesy despondence that can shift into occasional oblique settlements.Both 'Ding Dong Doodle' and 'Memfis' show the trio in full jam mode, the first a podium on which Ljungstrom really lets it rip, a three and a half exercise in playful determination that starts out nimble and serene before slipping into a colossus of thunder and lightning.The second is a funkier track (as the lightly veiled title may imply) that shines a light on Dig , whose bass work is more than commendable, and the keyboard exuberance is off the charts, a vintage organ leading the way, whilst adding copious doses of synthesizer as well. The fretboard adorns instead of leading; it is there to be the perfect foil for the ivory assault.Speaking of funk, the Dig bass options out some slapping technique that comes completely out of the blue on the propulsive 'Mini Apple'. When the shapeshifting guitar enters the fray, its bleedingly intense, Rikki hitting the cymbals and I was taken back to that Robin Trower-era masterpiece called Bridge of Sighs. If this track had a soulful and expressive singer like James Dewar, it would definitely fit.Time to lie back and reflect on 'Soaked', a breezy image of a hammock tied between two tress out in some pastoral meadow, in which a relaxed guitarist can experiment with sunshiny moodiness, the warm rays beating down on a smiling face.Why not attempt some humour while they are at it, and 'Gin n Tonic' keeps the refreshment stand busy, Dig the barman pouring some dazzling leads on the synthesizers. The second round has the guitar tearing it up like there is no tomorrow, Rikki pounding as if wielding ice picks (it can be cold in Minnesota).'8th Day' has a nearly Caribbean feel, keeping the mood bright and sassy. Think an instrumental homage to the Police, as this talented trio could easily pull it off successfully. The Andy Summers reference comes across on the mathematical exuberance displayed on 'Gopher It', with extended melodic notes instead overtly flashy technical prowess, a fitting final touch to an album I enjoyed immensely.One thing is for sure; these are three very talented dudes. And as far as context is concerned, this debut album is more than worthy of expanding their craft, as they may have a winning formula. A bold combination of vintage heritage with a modern approach. Available on Bandcamp digitally, with CD release to appear very soon. It's never too late to do a good deed.4 Ghosts of the Age
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自美国明尼苏达乐队Ovrfwld鼓手Rikki Davenport的支线项目Tre Spiritus，与贝斯手Dig及吉他手Par Ljungstrom组成的三重奏。音乐风格偏向器乐化的爵士摇滚融合，吉他主导旋律走向，贝斯与键盘构建和声骨架，鼓点推进节奏。曲风涵盖从轻快即兴到迷幻氛围的多个层面，如《Bin 294》展现流畅的律动感，《Ding Dong Doodle》则以即兴jam形式释放吉他表现力，《Memfis》则突出funk倾向与键盘主导。整体制作以器乐对话为核心，三位乐手在爵士、摇滚与funk之间自由切换，结构上偏向即兴展开而非复杂的前卫架构。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — "From the Weeping Cradle" takes us by surprise with a funky rhythm that quickly turns atonal; following the clavinet, the album's creator and composer, Dominic Sanderson, steps in, playing the Mellotron alongside the guitars. Andy Frizell's saxophone stands out, and together with the bass and guitar, they drive this opening section forward. The great thing is that, while one can trace logical influences from bands like King Crimson and Yes, they are channeled in a way that aims for something new. What is truly intriguing is when Dominic sings; he reminded me of Peter Hammill, and it is not easy to find someone willing to tackle that vocal range and emotional spectrum. Meanwhile, his guitar strumming produced fresh, almost jazzy notes that contrasted with his dark, guttural vocal responses.Of course... just as the Hamill-esque style wasn't for everyone, polarizing opinion between die-hard fans and detractors, the same may hold true for Sanderson. It's a matter of taste. What is beyond dispute, however, is the quality of the arrangements and the composition, which is highly complex, including the violin played by Tristan Apperley (alongside the bass) and constant shifts in rhythm.On "Faithless Folly," they don't take their foot off the gas; the experimental mood persists, opening with an evocative whisper that heralds a fierce flute and organ run in the style of Van Der Graaf Generator, reminiscent of a guest appearance by Robert Fripp, yet with even deeper dynamic shifts and accelerations, alongside Mellotron backing vocals. When the vocals return, the track takes on a unique character, incorporating more notes than might conventionally be expected, and managing to pull it off beautifully as part of the overall musical vision. This is undoubtedly a testament to their own creative merit. The sax is right where it needs to be, and when the guitar joins in, with a touch of The Mars Volta, it even takes on a distorted, jazzy vibe; the sax sounds like three amplified instruments, a full horn section... culminating in a free-form jam session followed by a dark finale worthy of the suites found on Hammill's early solo albums, the essential Chameleon in the Shadow of the Night or The Silent Corner and the Empty Stage."A Rite of Wrongs", aside from having a great title, is a fantastic acoustic song; it is an intimate nook within a vast, gray, and grandiose palace, where the warmth of the acoustic guitar, violin, and flute ignites the very flames visible on the album cover."Lullaby for a Broken Dream" seems to usher in a different meter, governed by other rules, more tribal, more primal and visceral. The strings and backing vocals all seem to hang by a thread that grows ever tauter, keeping pace with the saxophone; the latter then dances with Dominic's voice as he strikes once more with his most dangerous instrument, his wild vocal delivery. As we have seen, that voice has many facets, making it all the more unpredictable and bold. The music supports this with a guitar solo that climbs higher and higher, ascending even as everything around it seems to be falling. It is gravity... A passage driven by acoustic guitar and bass takes on a near-classical and flamenco feel, echoing the tradition of dark suites; then the saxophone charges in with atonal free-jazz notes, intertwining with a rock-infused, heavy-leaning flamenco guitar in a jam session reminiscent of the wildest White Stripes, before shifting into a King Crimson-esque fusion vibe... If every section of the song were assigned a color, the rainbow wouldn't be enough to cover them all, yet the whole piece comes together with perfect harmony and coherence. "Blazing Revelations" takes a different turn, and the saxophone is there for a reason, just like the violin, the flute, and Sanderson's touch, which lurks purposefully amidst the multicolored flames.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑展现出典型的折衷前卫摇滚气质，开篇以放克节奏切入迅速转为无调性段落，Mellotron、Clavinet与小提琴、长笛、萨克斯交织编配，作曲结构复杂且不断变换节奏。Dominic Sanderson的演唱被比作Peter Hammill，嗓音暗沉粗粝、情感跨度宽广，与吉他的爵士化清新弹奏形成对比。专辑融合了King Crimson式的张力、Van der Graaf Generator的键盘主导段落，以及Mars Volta的扭曲爵士质感，同时包含民谣质感的原声短篇与部落节奏的原始段落。整体制作强调作曲与编曲的内在逻辑，在致敬经典前卫摇滚语汇的同时尝试个人化表达。萨克斯在多首作品中承担旋律推动力的角色，弦乐与人声背景层制造出密室剧场般的氛围。

items.body: Recorded at London's St Bartholomew's Hospital, the new album by the former member of Simian Mobile Disco and the Last Shadow Puppets lays bare a journey of sickness and recovery Image credit: Dan Wilton James Ellis Ford’s second solo album joins a small and exclusive list of records that were made in hospitals. There’s J Dilla’s Donuts, there’s The Wind by Warren Zevon, and now there’s Lost In Another World, in this case recorded at Saint Barts in the City of London between intensive sessions of chemotherapy over a nine month period. At times it's heartwrenching, but never mawkish, and throughout there’s a sense of dignity that often comes with the knowledge that death could be just waiting around the corner. Given... items._cn_summary: 这是James Ellis Ford的第二张个人专辑，他是Simian Mobile Disco和Last Shadow Puppets的前成员。整张专辑在伦敦圣巴塞洛缪医院录制，录制时间跨度九个月，期间穿插着密集的化疗疗程。专辑记录了一段患病与康复的个人历程，情感上具有悲剧性，但处理手法保持尊严，避免了过度感伤。录音环境的特殊性——医院内部空间——为声音增添了独特的质感与氛围。这种将生命危机直接融入创作过程的方式，使作品超越了普通的个人化表达，成为一种以身体经验为基础的艺术实践。The Quietus将其与J Dilla的Donuts和Warren Zevon的The Wind并提，认为它属于那些诞生于医院环境中的稀有专辑之列。

items.body: Any album that sounds as though everybody involved remembered to wipe their feet before entering the studio should probably be regarded with suspicion. Fortunately, Wailin Storms’ The Arsonist sounds more like four people discovered a door already hanging crooked from its hinges and decided the sensible course was to make the room less structurally sound. The Durham band carries the American South around like a family curse, hauling blues, gothic rock, punk, doom, Baptist hymns and old folk dread into the same cramped quarters. Their fifth album, and first for Season of Mist, was recorded fully analogue by Matt Talbott of Hum, an appropriate choice for music that benefits from scraped edges and human error. Justin Storms wanted portions of the record to reconnect with the primitive four-track character of the band’s beginnings. “Some of these songs are more primitive and stripped down, hearkening back to the four-track recordings that the band started with,” says Storms. “The recordings contain flaws, but remain human in all the right ways. They could be a murder ballad or an old folk song that’s sung around the campfire.” Standout track Dead End provides an appropriately diseased introduction. Ben Melton’s guitar worries at Steve Stanczyk’s bass while Mark Oates pounds out a rhythm that seems increasingly annoyed about being alive. There is some Radiohead in its queasy grandeur, the poetic ecstasy of The Doors’ Jim Morrison, and plenty of The Gun Club in its bloodshot blues logic. Then Storms sings “Calm night / Birds keep plucking out our eyes” with the casual authority of a man reporting local traffic conditions. Fire has followed Storms since childhood, when his fascination with flames nearly resulted in the destruction of his family home. Here it becomes appetite, catastrophe, sex, faith and bad judgment sharing one cigarette. Flannery O’Connor would recognize the neighborhood immediately: everybody has dressed for church, salvation is theoretically available, and somebody somewhere has misplaced a can of gasoline. You Never Answered turns the miserable modern habit of staring into a phone into a deafening plea for actual contact. Elsewhere, war and ordinary social machinery feed the record’s agitation before the title track slows everything into a bruised procession. Love suddenly becomes another uncontrollable force capable of rearranging a life without requesting permission. Never Rest swells into a crescendo of horror as it unfurls a wild torrent of haunting poetry set against apocalyptic guitars and thundering drums – landing somewhere between Type O Negative and The Doors. The Arsonist finds Wailin Storms standing dangerously close to their oldest impulses: primitive rock & roll, folk horror, damaged romance and the suspicion that salvation and catastrophe may share an address. Listen to The Arsonist below and order the album here. items._cn_summary: Wailin Storms 的第五张专辑以全模拟方式录制于 Hum 主脑 Matt Talbott 工作室，主脑 Justin Storms 有意回归乐队早期四轨录音的原始质感，强调瑕疵与人味。乐队将蓝调、哥特摇滚、朋克、厄运金属、浸信会赞美诗与民谣恐惧感压缩进同一空间，呈现出类似谋杀民谣与篝火旁古老歌谣的混合气质。歌词层面大量运用美国南方哥特意象，火灾成为贯穿全片的隐喻，关联饥饿、灾难、性与信仰。器乐上吉他与贝斯互相撕扯，鼓点充满疲倦的愤怒，编制在粗粝四件套与末日音墙之间摆动。整体定位偏向有鲜明地域色彩与文学性的暗潮根脉摇滚，独立厂牌 Season of Mist 发行为其保留了地下气质。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

Weird and wonderful, it sounds
items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.
Tiny Sun -
Vanishment
(Review)
Carolina Chocolate Drops -
Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 982Le Orme is one of the longest lasting and best known Italian progressive rock bands. Le Orme was formed in Venice in 1966 by Aldo Tagliapietra (voice and guitars), Nino Smeraldi (guitars), Claudio Galietti (guitar and bass) and Marino Rebeschini (drums). Their first album, "Ad Gloriam" was released in 1968. From their psychedelic and beat initial roots, the band moved into much more increasingly sophisticated musical structures. In that line, the band released two excellent albums "Collage" in 1971 and "Uomo Di Pezza" in the following year. Their 1973 album "Felona E Sorona" is widely regarded as one of the top albums in the Italian progressive rock scene. By this time, the band consisted of Tagliapietra (mostly on bass with some guitar) along with keyboard player Tony Pagliuca and drummer Michi Dei Rossi."Felona E Sorona - Deluxe Edition (English And Italian Versions)" is a very special compilation album of Le Orme that was released in 2011. This is an economic package that includes their fourth studio album "Felona E Sorona", released in 1973, in its original Italian version, and their fifth studio album, which is the same album but in its English version and that was also released in the same year. This can be a very interesting compilation album because it includes the two versions of the album. As many of us know, "Felona E Sorona" is in general considered the best work from the band and is also considered a landmark to Italian progressive rock as one of the best and most important progressive rock albums ever made, especially in the Italian progressive rock scene. So, what we have really here is a great album in its two versions, probably at a cheaper price, and what will be a very worthwhile purchase, especially for those who are collectors and huge fans of Le Orme, fans of the Italian progressive rock or fans of the great prog music in general.As I'm going to review these two albums on Progarchives, in a more extensive way, I'm not going to do it at this moment. So, if you are interested to know, in more detail, what I'll write about them later, I invite you to read both of my reviews, in time. However, here I'm going to write something about them in a shorter way. So, of course, I'm not going to analyze them track by track, as I'm going to do, but I'm only going to make a global appreciation of both albums."Felona E Sorona" - Italian Version: "Felona E Sorona" is one of the classic albums of the Italian prog rock scene. The album quickly reached the top of the Italian charts giving the band their second gold record. Like many others, I find "Felona E Sorona" to be Le Orme's most fascinating work. In less than 35 minutes, Le Orme delivers probably their greatest masterpiece. Their high level of musicianship is evident over the all album. The focus is more on mood, song structure, and texture. As a concept work and despite the nine pieces, mostly short pieces and with a lot of variety, the album sounds very homogeneous and less like a collection of individual songs. This is an album that still has a strong influence in the world of progressive rock to the point that La Maschera Di Cera paid tribute to it by extending its theme and even going so far as to take up and transform the superb original cover. "Felona E Sorona" is a true classic of the movement and it's unforgivable not to have it if you like Italian prog rock. "Felona E Sorona" is an absolute must-buy."Felona E Sorona" - English Version: "Felona E Sorona" is a beautiful album, soaked with that 70's flavour that we all prog rock fans love. Although it's by no means technical, the band presents a unique sound that combines vocal parts that exude a unique sense of song with dramatic instrumental parts that make full use of synths and organs to portray a variety of scenes, including lyricism and thrills. It's an album of the golden years of progressive. Like their compatriots Premiata Forneria Marconi and Banco Del Mutuo Soccorso, "Felona E Sorona" was also released in the original Italian version and in the English version. At the request of Tony Stratton-Smith the owner of Charisma Records, Le Orme recorded an English version of the album with lyrics translated by Peter Hammill. It was also entitled "Felona E Sorona" and was also released in 1973. The English album is very similar, except that the vocals were more expressive and appropriate in Italian. This English version is also very good but listen to the Italian version because it's much better.Conclusion: Italian and English versions of the album give the listener the opportunity to hear the English lyrics, and yet enjoy the authentic feel of the original album. Well written notes in both Italian and English, including song lyrics. The essay in these notes gave me a proper understanding of what this album is about, as well as details about the album's production. As a bonus, there are also some band photos and copies of original mixes and vinyl stickers, both English and Italian. However, there's a poor sound quality for the English version. The volume is lower than that of the Italian version, which is a pity. Besides, I strongly prefer the Italian vocals to the English. I think escape to us some of the most important parts of the original album, which are the vocals. I can understand why many people, especially the non-Latin language speakers, prefer the English version. But, definitely, the original is always better than the copy.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)

items.body: Magic Wands released the single “Diamond Rain” on August 14, 2026 through Metropolis Records. The Los Angeles duo of vocalists and guitarists Dexy and Chris Valentine mix dream-pop with shoegaze, post-punk and goth, and the track is the first to be lifted from a new Magic Wands album due in early 2027. It is out digitally, with a self-made video posted to the band’s YouTube channel the same day. Diamond Rain by Magic Wands What Magic Wands say about ‘Diamond Rain’ The duo describe the song as deliberately open rather than fixed: “the song doesn’t have one fixed meaning. To us, it’s about moving toward the light, finding beauty after darkness and allowing people to discover their own meaning within it.” They made the accompanying video themselves and explain how the look was built: “using old cameras, lights and mirrors to create textures and effects that give it a dreamlike feeling.” “Diamond Rain” streams and downloads through Bandcamp and the usual digital services. No physical edition has been announced, and the duo have not named the 2027 album or given it a date. ‘Diamond Rain’ follows two EPs and a Peter Murphy remix The single closes an unusually busy eighteen months. The album “Cascades” arrived on October 24, 2025, trailed by the double single “Time To Dream” backed with “Armour (River Remix by Lost Signal)” the previous month. A Delerium remix of “Moonshadow” followed on March 13, 2026. Two EPs came after that. The “Wishing Well” EP, six songs issued on April 24, 2026, was preceded by its title track in February and by “Sacred Mirrors”, a January 2026 collaboration with John Ashton of The Psychedelic Furs. The six-track “Remixes” EP landed on June 12, 2026 and reworked material from “Cascades”. In between, the pair remixed Peter Murphy; Side-Line covered that single when Peter Murphy released “Swoon (Magic Wands Remix)” on May 29, 2026. About Magic Wands Magic Wands formed in Nashville in 2008 around Dexy and Chris Valentine, who share vocals and guitars, and later moved to Los Angeles. Metropolis Records describes their sound as heavily textured guitars, droning synths and ethereal vocals. The duo have released through Metropolis for over a decade. Side-Line first covered them in April 2022 around the single “Fortune”, then the single “Time” in May 2023 and the remix album and tour that August. The album “Switch” followed in 2023 and was reviewed here that September. “Cascades” came in October 2025 and drew the run of singles, remixes and EPs that “Diamond Rain” now brings to a close, with the next album set for early 2027.
items._cn_summary: Magic Wands 是一支来自洛杉矶的二人组合，由 Dexy 和 Chris Valentine 组成，以共享人声和吉他为核心。他们的音乐融合梦幻流行、自赏派、后朋克与哥特元素，Metropolis Records 将其声音描述为质感厚重的吉他、嗡鸣合成器与空灵人声。新单曲《Diamond Rain》于2026年8月发布，是其2027年初新专辑的首支单曲，使用老式相机、灯光与镜子自制MV，营造梦境般视觉效果。这首歌以开放式表达著称——乐队称它象征着走向光明、在黑暗之后寻找美感，允许听众自行解读其内涵。乐队近一年半发行密集：2025年专辑《Cascades》、多首单曲、与Delerium和Peter Murphy合作的混音作品、以及两张EP，构成了新单曲之前的完整脉络。整体音乐风格偏向暗潮与后朋克的光影交织，声音纹理丰富，但在实验性和前卫性方面较为保守。

items.body: Belgian dark electro and EBM project Deadly Sins has issued “Red”, a six-track digital EP on the Antwerp label DressCode Black. The label sets 21 August 2026 as the release date across streaming platforms; the EP went up on the label’s Bandcamp page on 12 August. C.VII produced the record and Arnte handled the mastering. The EP pairs the original with an alternate reading and four remixes: “Red”, “Red (Mystic Classic Version)”, “Red (Novakill Remix)”, “Red (Pyrroline Remix)”, “Red (Dreadfool Remix)” and “Red (SEXGUN Remix)”. DressCode Black describes the remix set as “four radically different interpretations from prominent artists within the international underground scene, alongside the atmospheric Mystic Classic Version of the original.” Red by DEADLY SINS The four remixers pull the track in different directions. Pyrroline reworks it as electro-industrial, Novakill pushes it towards the dancefloor, Dreadfool takes it into harder EBM, and SEXGUN strips it back to a minimal, repetitive form. Deadly Sins at La Luna Obscura in Ostend The release date coincides with a live appearance. Deadly Sins plays the second edition of La Luna Obscura at Elysée in Ostend, Belgium, on Friday 21 August 2026. The Friday bill also carries Haujobb, This Morn’ Omina, Cattac, Matt Hart and Skren. This Morn’ Omina’s set marks 30 years of the project, which Mika Goedrijk started in Roeselare in 1996. Haujobb last released the album “The Machine in the Ghost” in September 2024. About Deadly Sins Deadly Sins is the solo project of C.VII, one half of the Belgian EBM duo WÜLF7, which he formed in 2017 with Sebastian Blondwulf. WÜLF7 describe their own style as DEBM, short for Dark Electro Body Melancholic. Working alone as Deadly Sins, C.VII combines EBM rhythms, dark electro arrangements and industrial textures with lyrics written in the first person. The project’s first release was the EP “Preface”, also on DressCode Black. DressCode Black is based in Antwerp and operates as a sub-label of Detroit-Berlin, releasing EBM, electro, new wave and industrial records. Its catalogue includes Darkvolt, Rogue Unit, Causenation, Mindshore, The Ordure and Atoms Inc., with remix work from Rhys Fulber, CJ Bolland, Orphx, Blac Kolor and Statiqbloom across earlier titles. “Red” continues the label’s run of remix-led singles and EPs, and lands the same day Deadly Sins takes the La Luna Obscura stage.
items._cn_summary: 比利时暗潮电子项目 Deadly Sins 在安特卫普独立厂牌 DressCode Black 发行了六曲数字 EP《Red》，包含原曲、Mystic Classic 改编版及四位来自国际地下场景的艺人各自重新诠释的混音。Pyrroline 将其推向电气工业方向，Novakill 强化舞池律动，Dreadfool 走向更硬的 EBM，SEXGUN 则将其剥离为极简重复形态。制作由 C.VII 担纲，Arnte 负责母带处理。EP 发行同日，项目主理人将以 Deadly Sins 身份登上比利时奥斯坦德 La Luna Obscura 音乐节第二届时段的舞台。该厂牌长期深耕 EBM、电声、新浪潮与工业音乐领域，此作延续了以混音为核心的发行路线。整张作品以多版本拆解同一素材的方式呈现，展示了不同制作人对暗潮电子语言的多样化理解。

items.album: A Totally New Sound
items.excerpt: Smiling C trail their Shams Dinn diamond with this bounty of Washington Go-Go picks from the short-lived Aset label’s Whax, Treo, and Latonya, all recorded and originally released c. 1986-88. Like the Shams LP, A Totally New Sound brims with pure soulful optimism and home-baked charm, but rather than early Arabic rap and ‘80s... more
items.body:
Smiling C trail their Shams Dinn diamond with this bounty of Washington Go-Go picks from the short-lived Aset label’s Whax, Treo, and Latonya, all recorded and originally released c. 1986-88. Like the Shams LP, A Totally New Sound brims with pure soulful optimism and home-baked charm, but rather than early Arabic rap and ‘80s boogie, this one surveys a blindspot in most collections with some of the rarest and most special Go-Go Records in existence. 

All eight song were written by the Aset label’s in-house players, revolving song-writers Mbu Mbulu and O Jabbo, and includes their semi-released instrumental Skip, along with three beauties by the 11 year old singer Latonya which are almost worth entry alone, plus one wild one by the Whax duo, and three from Treo, the trio of Cathy Young, Delores Lidell and Linda Lawson.

Seriously, the Latonya tracks are what pop dreams are made of - precocious yet innocent, flush with colourful melodies and driven by that bustling Go-Go hustle, the super infectious Dance Time is a ready-made anthem, while Eyes Of A Child and We Will Teach The Adults weirdly also recall early ‘80s Belgian cold wave crossed with Langley Schools Music Project, or something.

The Aset Players’ Skip reveals the boogie mechanics under their pop hood, while Whax tend to the freakier side with a spot of Rick James-ian flair, and Treo’s close harmonies come out perfectly pop-wise in Demands Demands Demands, but Second Is Too Close and the forlorn romance of When Your Love Is Gone feels too weird to be pop proper, and that’s where the magick lies in this LP, between Aset’s mainstream ambition and a realness of expression that can’t be missed.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张聚焦华盛顿Go-Go场景的稀有合辑，收录了Aset厂牌旗下Whax、Treo和Latomya在1986-88年间录制的作品。专辑灵魂来自厂牌驻场词曲作者Mbu Mbulu与O Jabbo，融合了底特律Boogie的律动机制与Go-Go特有的繁忙打击乐层次。Treo三人组以紧密和声在流行与奇异之间游走，Whax则偏向Rick James式的放克怪趣，而年仅十一岁的歌手Latomya以三首早熟却纯真的歌曲成为专辑亮点，旋律色彩丰富，活力充沛。整体制作散发着家庭作坊般的真挚气息，在主流野心与真实表达的张力中形成了独特的化学反应。

items.album: DOOMED!
items.excerpt: First full collaborative LP from Open Mike Eagle & Kenny Segal after nearly twenty years of friendship and occasional collaboration. "It’s five years in a blender. It’s every troublesome misunderstanding of a half-decade relationship distorted and stretched into an absurdist black comedy mini-series on wax. It’s the sound of... more
items.body:
First full collaborative LP from Open Mike Eagle & Kenny Segal after nearly twenty years of friendship and occasional collaboration.

"It’s five years in a blender. It’s every troublesome misunderstanding of a half-decade relationship distorted and stretched into an absurdist black comedy mini-series on wax. It’s the sound of every fight we ever had, playing simultaneously. It’s several consecutive voice notes that you did not listen to, and instead read the transcription. It’s fifteen songs from iconoclastic rapper Mike Eagle and innovative producer Kenny Segal. It’s the world’s first half-whimsical break-up album. It’s DOOMED!

It’s also LA. Maybe not first and foremost, but Los Angeles runs deep in this record’s present, and its lineage. The story of any big city is also one of transplants. DJ Premier in New York, Tupac in California. If you build it, they will come. Mike and Kenny both arrived in LA as young, aspiring artists who were drawn to the scene around groundbreaking rap crew Project Blowed. They have been friends—and occasional collaborators—for almost twenty years. Despite that, DOOMED! is the first time the two have put together a full body of work. But everything happens in its time, and fate worked to bring them together at the exact moment that would allow the duo to create something extraordinary. Mike, fresh off a string of multi-producer records and processing the end of a tumultuous relationship, was in need of creative catharsis.

Meanwhile, Kenny had locked in on his next challenge after a recent string of critically acclaimed collaborations not only with rappers like billy woods, and K-the-I???, but also jazz trio Human Error Club and bluesy indie rocker Benjamin Booker.

“In recent years, Kenny made it very clear that he wasn’t trying to keep having one or two beats on my projects; he wanted to build something,” Open Mike Eagle explains. “I was able to convince him to let me use a couple beats for Neighborhood Gods Unlimited with the caveat that we would focus on our thing next. Then my relationship fell apart right when we started working, and it was like, ‘Perfect, I have a lot to say about this.’

Here are some more particularly interesting insights from the man himself:

“If DOOMED! is prestige TV, then think of “Out To Lunch” as the pilot where we meet a man who’s not all there because his head is still in yesterday, and the following as a brief synopsis. There’s a song that starts at an argument about the color of a rental car. There’s a song about trying to write a pair of lovers’ initials in wet concrete and the stick breaking. There’s a song that’s a prayer about finding the strength not to look at my ex’s social media. There’s a song about a character from Adventure Time who’s a piece of shit that I identify with. Each vision is a crashed airplane halfway on the border of dream and nightmare, bitter and sweet, sadness and freedom. Every one of Kenny’s beats is a chunk of ore from a different comet. I used each one as a canvas to paint my impression of a dead world.""

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Open Mike Eagle与制作人Kenny Segal近二十年友谊后的首次完整合作，主题围绕一段动荡关系的终结。整张专辑被形容为'半荒诞喜剧迷你剧'，十五首歌以碎片化、梦境与噩梦交织的方式展开叙事。歌词涉及争吵、分手后的社交媒体诱惑、对《探险活宝》中角色的投射等日常而荒诞的细节。制作人Kenny Segal此前与billy woods、K-the-I???等地下说唱艺人合作，风格偏向实验性制作。洛杉矶的城市基因渗透其中，两人都与传奇说唱团体Project Blowed有渊源。专辑定位为'世界首张半奇趣分手专辑'，融合个人情感宣泄与概念化叙事，介于独立嘻哈与实验说唱之间，兼具文学性与自嘲气质。

items.album: Lost In Another World
items.excerpt: Moving sideways from Warp to Domino, Simian Mobile Disco's James Ellis Ford challenges himself on his second solo full-length, crafting a set of Sakamoto-inspired synth pop from his hospital bed. Ford's always been capable of producing pitch-perfect pop - his appearance on records from everyone from the Pet Shop Boys to... more
items.body:
Moving sideways from Warp to Domino, Simian Mobile Disco's James Ellis Ford challenges himself on his second solo full-length, crafting a set of Sakamoto-inspired synth pop from his hospital bed.

Ford's always been capable of producing pitch-perfect pop - his appearance on records from everyone from the Pet Shop Boys to Depeche Mode is a testament to that - but 'Lost in Another World' is a more personal affair. It was written and produced in hospital after he'd been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia last year, "on the ward between rounds of chemo." Thankfully his condition has improved - he posted earlier this month that he's got no more treatment in store - but the album stands as a vulnerable reflection of a difficult time. Ford describes it as a "pep talk", and it draws on some of his most enduring influences, Yellow Magic Orchestra and Japan, to channel its complicated tangle of emotions. 

On the opening track (and lead single) 'Overtones', Ford's voice hovers over plasticky rhythmelodic sequences and rubbery '80s drums and you'd be forgiven for assuming it's a lost city pop demo. Ford doesn't let the energy fall off, either, waltzing through slow-motion melancholia on the tentatively beautiful 'Here Today' and John Foxx-style synth pop on 'This Too Shall Pass'. Ultimately, it's surprisingly hopeful material, infused with genuine feeling.
items._genre: synth pop / art pop / minimal wave
items._cn_summary: 这是James Ellis Ford的第二张个人专辑，从Warp转投Domino厂牌。整张专辑在他被诊断出急性髓性白血病期间，于医院病床上写就完成，化疗间隙的创作使它带有私人的脆弱感。音乐上以合成器流行为主体，坂本龙一式的简洁编排是核心骨架，Yellow Magic Orchestra与Japan的影子清晰可辨——'Overtones'有着80年代city pop的弹性鼓机与塑料质感旋律线，'Here Today'转向慢速忧郁的华尔兹节奏，'This Too Shall Pass'则贴近John Foxx那种冷峻的合成器流行。情感层面虽是阴暗处境下的产物，却流露出意外的希望感，Ford本人将其定义为一次自我激励。对偏好电子与暗潮的听众而言，其合成器质感和情绪氛围有一定吸引力，但整体仍属合成器流行范畴，实验性与先锋性较为有限。

items.album: Cathedral
items.artist: John Carpenter, Cody Carpenter, & Daniel Davies
items.excerpt: Scoring a graphic novel based on a dream he had in 2024, John Carpenter gets the band back together, turning in an album that'll delight fans of 'Lost Themes'. We know full well that Hollywood doesn't seem interested in making Carpenter's films a reality any more - he's said as much, quite publicly. So what's the next best... more
items.body:
Scoring a graphic novel based on a dream he had in 2024, John Carpenter gets the band back together, turning in an album that'll delight fans of 'Lost Themes'.

We know full well that Hollywood doesn't seem interested in making Carpenter's films a reality any more - he's said as much, quite publicly. So what's the next best thing? Well, a graphic novel. 'Cathedral' was written by Carpenter alongside his wife (and long-time creative partner) Sandy King and, like all great Carpenter projects, it had to have a home-brewed score to ease it along. So who better to make the dream a reality than his regular bandmates Cody Carpenter and Daniel Davies? Chronologically, this one fits in right after 2024's 'Lost Themes No. 4: Noir', but fans of Carpenter's earlier (eerier) biz will be happy to hear that he's reaching a little further back this time. 

There's of course the hard rock influence that's been present since at least 'They Live', but every so often there's a glimmer of the earworm-laden synth pop that elevated 'Escape from New York', and the iconic 'Assault on Precinct 13'. Just peep the 'Halloween'-style piano breakdown on 'Inside Out', the 'In the Mouth of Madness' mood on opener 'Primeval' or the classic horror flex of 'Abandoned Cathedral', with its organs, orchestral swells and all-important Mellotron choirs.
items._genre: synth / film score / horror / dark ambient / progressive electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是约翰·卡彭特与其子科迪·卡彭特及丹尼尔·戴维斯为同名图像小说创作的配乐，延续了卡彭特自《失落主题》以来的合作模式。作品在合成器主导的电影配乐框架内融合了多种元素：硬摇滚式的riff段落、合成器流行旋律线、教堂管风琴与弦乐铺陈、以及梅洛特朗合唱音色。整体氛围回归其更早期作品的诡异特质，钢琴段落让人联想到《万圣节》的标志性手法，开篇曲则带有《约翰·卡彭特之疯狂》的气质。作为图像小说的配套作品，它服务于叙事场景，具有较强的画面感与情绪引导功能，但并未在合成器电影配乐的类型框架内做出显著的实验性突破。

Night After Night by Escape With Romeo ‘Night After Night’ tracklist and credits “Night After Night” runs 14 tracks: “Edit Me Out”, “No Turning Back
items.body: German post-punk and darkwave act Escape With Romeo released their 13th studio album, “Night After Night”, on August 7, 2026 through Zeitklang. The Cologne band’s new release arrives on CD digipak and digital, and follows the group’s 2024 comeback album “Suspicious Bliss”. Night After Night by Escape With Romeo ‘Night After Night’ tracklist and credits “Night After Night” runs 14 tracks: “Edit Me Out”, “No Turning Back”, “Sound and the Fury”, “Something That Lasts”, “New World Order”, “Cancel Anytime”, “I Need Something Stronger”, “Fear’s a Ghost”, “Little Did I Know”, “Night After Night”, “Skyscraper Spiders”, “I’m My Own Worst Enemy”, “You Need the Drugs” and “Wrong Side of Town Pt. 2”. All songs are written by singer, guitarist and songwriter Thomas Elbern, except “You Need the Drugs”, a cover of the 2013 WestBam track featuring Richard Butler of the Psychedelic Furs, credited here to its writers Klaus Jankuhn, Maximilian Lenz and Butler. The album was recorded, mixed and produced by Elbern and drummer Frenzy Erl at Zeitklang in Brühl and Highline in Munich between January 2025 and June 2026, and mastered by Erl. Elbern handles vocals, guitars, synths, vocoder and samples, with Frenzy Erl on drums, Tobias Schwartz on bass and Stella Tonon on vocals. Artwork and graphic design are by schmalfett.com. Themes and rollout The band describes “Night After Night” as harder, more emotional and more direct than “Suspicious Bliss”, the direction Elbern set out to push further at the start of 2025. Songs including “No Turning Back” and “New World Order” address what the band calls a dystopian zeitgeist shaped by AI, while “Skyscraper Spiders” and “Wrong Side of Town Pt. 2” extend the mood signalled by the single “Fear’s a Ghost”. Press materials for the release describe it as “somewhere between post-rock, trip-hop, and the much overused term post-punk.” “Night After Night” was preceded by the singles “Fear’s a Ghost”, released on February 6, 2026, and “Sound and the Fury”, which Side-Line covered as the third single from the album in March 2026. The band will support the album with a Germany tour in autumn 2026, performing as a trio and mixing songs from “Night After Night” with material from across its history. About Escape With Romeo Escape With Romeo was founded in Cologne in 1989 by singer and guitarist Thomas Elbern, who had previously fronted the new wave band Seltsame Zustände and played guitar and wrote songs for Pink Turns Blue. The band’s early catalog appeared through Sound Factory, starting with the self-titled “Escape With Romeo” in 1990 and continuing with “Autumn on Venus” (1991), “Next Stop Eternally” (1993), “Blast of Silence” (1996) and “How Far Can You Go” (1998), a run that included the early single “Somebody”, the band’s best-known track from that period. Keyboardist Martin Pott joined from the second album onward. From 2001 the band’s releases moved to Zeitklang, the label Elbern runs himself, starting with “Come Here White Light” (2001) and continuing through “Love Alchemy” (2002), “Psalms of Survival” (2004), “Emotional Iceage” (2007), “Samsara” (2012) and “After the Future” (2015). Escape With Romeo announced its farewell in 2017, played a final tour in 2018 and had dissolved following festival appearances in 2019. The band returned in 2022 with the double compilation “Based on a True Story – Best of Escape With Romeo”, which led into “Suspicious Bliss”, released on November 1, 2024 as the first new studio album since “After the Future”. The 2026 rollout for “Night After Night” opened with “Fear’s a Ghost” in February, followed by “Sound and the Fury” in March, and now arrives with the album itself on August 7, 2026 via Zeitklang.
items._cn_summary: 德国科隆后朋克与暗潮乐队Escape With Romeo推出第十一张录音室专辑，以十四首作品延续自2024年回归专辑《Suspicious Bliss》以来的创作脉络。Thomas Elbern包揽词曲创作，联手鼓手Frenzy Erl在Brühl的Zeitklang与慕尼黑Highline两地完成制作，涵盖录音、混音及母带处理全流程。专辑横跨后摇滚、trip-hop与后朋克三种底色，主题聚焦人工智能时代背景下的反乌托邦情绪，歌曲如《No Turning Back》《New World Order》直接介入社会议题。先行单曲《Fear's a Ghost》《Sound and the Fury》分别在2026年初陆续释出，乐队计划秋季以三人编制于德国巡演，乐曲将横贯新旧作品。整体定位介于情绪张力与电子质感之间，属于独立厂牌序列内的稳健续作。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Cornwall's anachronistic Arthurian spacemen return with their seventh full-length studio album release since their formation (in Edinburgh) in 2010 and second in two years (which is unusually fast for them). 1. "Song of the Rainforest" (21:20) a vocal-less and more keyboard-generated epic than the usual Emerald Dawn offerings. Also, it feels as if the presence and contributions of Dave Greenaway and Tom Jackson here are on the same level of importance (and dynamics) as those of Ally and Tree. (36/40)- i. "Balance" - after a long 90-second intro of cave dripping sounds and two alternating sustained organ chords slowly establishing their pace and fullness and then the entrance and establishment of bass and drums into an awesome funk-lite vamp groove of two gorgeous Mellotron-like chords Ally enters with his seering electric guitar to deliver one of his best guitar solos ever--for five minutes! The contagious groove established by Dave Greenaway and Tom Jackson is awesome. - ii. Incursions - a stop-and-pause precedes a very slow switch to Smooth Reggae groove over which Ally solos with his tenor sax. As Trees synth strings enter (and Ally's tenor sax desists), the beat is sped up (we're now into the ninth minute), which prompts Ally to switch to his soprano sax--which gives Tree a little more room and license to embellish with her variety of synth strings riffs: often matching or meeting Ally's sax lines with her own.- iii. "Loss" - in the 11th minute another interlude of synth strings intervals paves the way for a heavier, almost ominous motif to set up with Tom's more tribalistic tom-tom-centered (synthetic talking drum?) drumming and Dave's heavily-wowed bass play being stomped over by some deep monster-saw keyboard and guitar riffs. The keyboards continue riffing--kind of soloing--for a couple of minutes over this motif before . . . - iv. "Regret" - the 14th minute has the establishment of a peaceful, perhaps sad motif of jungle/tropical sounds (including Tree's Amazonian flute) woven loosely around one another until the 18th minute when saw synth chords take over and Ally returns to shredding emotionally on his guitar. One of the most evocative, sensitive, and surprisingly tight--even thoughtful--sections of any Emerald Dawn song I've ever encountered. 2. "Rivers of Tears" (14:58) opens with a jaunty journey of jazz-classical-sounding solo piano play. Among the most impressive and pretty keyboard play I've ever heard from Tree! At 1:40 bass, drums, and, eventually, Ally's "reverberated-into-the-background" electric guitar slowly enter. Tree continues to tinkle the ivories within and behind the guitar, bass, and drums while adding some washes of synth strings to the mix as Ally continues shredding (as he does). Then Ally stops, making room for Tree to expand her piano note play as Tom and Dave slowly, gradually slow down and drop out. a pause/break at 3:30 results in the unleashing of Tree's reverb-drenched voice over only the banks of synth strings chords and still tinkling piano note play (mostly in progressing arpeggios)--which eventually becomes just synth strings as we enter into another little pause around 5:30. Here Tree establishes a chord progression with the repetition of four descending arpeggiated chords over which the rhythm section joins in and Ally deploys his tenor sax. Another pause at the seven-minute mark leads into a transference of the play of the descending chord pattern to synth strings as Tom and Dave kick back and Ally switches to electric guitar. Here Dave's bass playing is a bit rote and uninventive while the embellishments that Tom adds to his drumming feel a bit forced and "required" while Ally's guitar shredding sounds/feels . . . the same as ever. A little pause at the end of the tenth minute is filled with Tree's vocal lines until the band re-emerges with a kind of two-chord "tropical" vamp. Yet another stop and transition at 11:45 as the band shifts into a much more dark and ominous section--launched off as Tree shouts out a "Poison. Into. It's veins." declaration. This section could almost be coming from NIL or KING CRIMSON--even with Tree's operatic high-note repeat delivery of the word "poison." The motif then morphs in the second half of the 14th minute into something more akin to a Led Zeppelin descending chord progression--which it plays out to the song's end with embellishing accents coming from Ally's synths and Tom's drums. Not bad! (26.375/30)- i. "The Natural Cycle" - ii. "Disruption" 3. "Paradise" (8:56) opening with some excitingly pregnant synthesizer play--chords, bass, and peppy upper register riffs--which subside when Tree's plaintive, melancholy voice enters at 0:33 to introduce the song's theme. By the one minute mark she pauses wherein Tom and Mark enter with a cool, jazzy, STING "Englishman in New York"-like motif (which then happens to support Tree's "Englishman in New York" vocal melody lines). Nice bass line beneath Tree's organ chords as Ally enters with a bluesier Gilmour-like approach to his injections of guitar riffs and flurries. Around the four-minute mark the band slows things down, Tree's voice softens, while Mark and Tom's play kind of moves into greater prominence as Ally and Tree's keyboard play slides more into the background of the mix. Interesting! And I like it: I like having the bass and drums mixed in front of the keys, guitars, and saxes. The synth strings and guitar soloing in the next two minutes feel much more like the sound palette of Polish NeoProg masters COLLAGE's great textures on their Moonshine masterpiece (especially "The Blues"). In the seventh minute one of the keys begins to repeat and develop a melody line from THE MOODY BLUES' "Nights in White Satin," to which Tom backs down for a bit, but then everybody ramps up again into a fully-COLLAGE motif in which the synth strings continue soloing as other synth chords continue to deploy the "Nights in White Satin" chords and melody-reminders. Brilliant! And this is how they choose to end the song, the album! Awesome! Despite the "borrowing" of the sound palette and melody/chords, I finally feel as if The Emerald Dawn have arrived to the gates of top-tier prog, the symphonic side! (18.75/20)- i. "Losing Paradise"- ii. "Harmony Regained"Total Time 45:14I like the more sophisticated complexities ED are injecting into their compositions as it diminishes the dreaded monotony wrought of their old style of endlessly jamming over simple and often drawn-out single- and/or double-chorded vamps. Either their music theory has improved or they've decided to let go of the stoner-rock approach to song-rendering and employ more symphonic structuring for their music--whatever it is, I like it!A-/4.5 stars; a stunningly-improved advancement of compositional design yields the best album of The Emerald Dawn's career--one that has them knocking on the door of the Valhalla of the Symphonic Prog masters! I'm bumping up this rating into masterpiece status for the surprising display of growth as well as this being, in my opinion, Emerald Dawn's best album yet.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了新派前卫摇滚的传统路线，以键盘为主导构建长篇器乐叙事。长达二十余分钟的丛林主题作品通过模拟合成器弦乐、萨克斯独奏与吉他即兴的交替推进，在章节化结构中模拟热带雨声与部落鼓点氛围。第二首曲目以爵士风格钢琴开场，融入钢琴与电吉他之间的对话，配合贝斯与鼓的渐进式构建。整体制作偏向学院派前卫摇滚的经典范式，在配器与和声展开上较为工整，但未触及实验电子、自由即兴或当代古典等领域，合成器音色以传统模拟堆叠为主，融合深度有限。与用户偏好的实验前卫、爵士即兴及暗潮电子风格存在较大距离。

items.body: ITCH have made a debut record called “House of Ghosts” available to stream on Escape.ai, a distribution platform and creator marketplace for generative AI and game-technology work founded by John Gaeta, an American visual effects designer, inventor, and creative director. The project describes the album like this: “House of Ghosts is a dark, alternative journey through memory, identity, loss, and the parts of ourselves that refuse to disappear. Split between ANIMUS and ANIMA, the album explores masculine and feminine inner worlds as two haunted sides of the same soul.” Ten tracks are posted with official audio and full lyrics: “Somewhere to Hide“, “Two”, “Temp”, “Throne”, “Alone”, “Time”, “Wrong”, “Son”, “Keep Your Roots” and “Void”. The lyrics deal with grief and absence (“Time takes everything”), sibling violence (“There were two. Then there was one”), suppressed anger (“It’s not anger, it’s a temperature”) and isolation (“I’m alone in my skin”). No writer, performer, producer or engineer is named against any of them. Due to the ban on AI music on several platforms, the album will probably only be available on Escape.ai for the moment being. About Escape.ai Escape.ai is a next-generation entertainment streaming and content distribution platform dedicated to pioneering the future of digital storytelling. Founded by Academy Award-winning visual effects designer John Gaeta (The Matrix), the platform serves as a curated, premium showcase for “Neo Cinema” and “Neo Play”. Unlike open social media feeds where AI content is frequently lost in the noise, Escape.ai positions itself as a prestige destination for premium, human-authored stories that are super-amplified by technology. The network champions independent creators, offering them a way to scale their original intellectual property and achieve blockbuster-level world-building without relying on traditional, rigid Hollywood studio pipelines. The network is actively streaming across major platforms like Roku and The Roku Channel, Amazon Fire TV, Samsung Smart TVs, and LG TVs, with expansion onto Apple TV and PC environments.
items._cn_summary: ITCH将首张专辑《House of Ghosts》发布于Escape.ai平台，该平台由《黑客帝国》视觉特效设计师John Gaeta创立，专为生成式AI和游戏技术内容服务。专辑被描述为一段穿越记忆、身份认同、失落与自我残存部分的黑暗另类旅程，以ANIMUS与ANIMA两部分展开，探索同一灵魂中男性与女性的内在世界。十首曲目涵盖悲痛与缺失、兄弟间暴力、被压抑的愤怒与孤立等主题，但所有曲目均未标注创作者、表演者、制作人或录音师。由于多家平台禁止AI音乐，该作品目前仅在Escape.ai上可访问。这篇报道更接近行业新闻而非音乐评论，未涉及实际音乐分析。

items.body: Pittsburgh industrial project ShadowMouth and Cleveland vocal trio The Elder Goths released the double single “The Promise of Alchemy/The Death of Chemistry” on 12 August 2026 through Death of the Party Records. The two tracks are the final preview of ShadowMouth’s debut album “Modern Alchemy”, due in autumn 2026. How ShadowMouth and The Elder Goths built the two tracks Rick Polo and Brooks Farris wrote and performed the music. The Elder Goths, made up of Cassandra Bishop, Lauren O’Janpa and Gina Schultz, sing on both sides. Bishop wrote the lyrics for “The Promise of Alchemy”, which runs 2:29, and Schultz wrote the lyrics for “The Death of Chemistry”, which runs 2:24. Farris produced, engineered and mastered the pair at Electric Fox Studios. Polo had not met the three singers before he asked them to record, and he describes the approach as a gamble that changed the shape of the release. “These songs were the result of me taking a shot in the dark and reaching out The Elder Goths group, who I had never met before, and asked if they would provide some of the striking beautifully haunting harmonies that are immediately apparent when first hearing their work,” Polo stated. “But it turned out to be so much more than I could have imagined. The end result was an intense and and really heartfelt delivery which absolutely blew me away. This collaboration felt too important not to highlight. So we decided to release this a single ahead of the record.” The double single is available on Bandcamp. The Promise of Alchemy/The Death of Chemistry by ShadowMouth & The Elder Goths About ShadowMouth ShadowMouth formed in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania in 2023 as the project of songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Rick Polo, who also plays in Baroque Monody and Heck Vektor. Producer and drummer Brooks Farris of Electric Fox Studios completes the working pair. The project opened with the double single “Poison Nostalgia/Twenty Four Hours” on 4 October 2024, with Dombroski guesting on “Poison Nostalgia”. The debut EP “Purification By Fire” followed on 22 November 2024. Four singles came next: “False (Prophets) Profits” on 20 January 2025, “Your Words, Not Mine” on 21 May 2025, “We Are Sentient” on 1 August 2025 and “DOOM SCROLLERS vs HOLY ROLLERS” on 29 October 2025. The Elder Goths formed in 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio, after Cassandra Bishop, Lauren O’Janpa and Gina Schultz met through the city’s underground scene. “The Promise of Alchemy/The Death of Chemistry” is their first recorded appearance with ShadowMouth. With the twin tracks out, ShadowMouth close a run of seven releases in under two years and move to “Modern Alchemy”, the project’s first album.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章本质上是一篇新闻稿，介绍了ShadowMouth与The Elder Goths合作的双单曲发行信息。文章主要陈述了发行日期、厂牌、制作人、词曲作者分工以及ShadowMouth项目的发展历程。ShadowMouth来自匹兹堡工业音乐场景，The Elder Goths是克利夫兰的地下人声组合，Polo与三位从未谋面的歌手展开合作，由Farris在Electric Fox Studios完成制作、录音和母带处理。文章几乎没有对音乐本身的艺术特征、声响设计或创作理念进行深入评述，仅引用了Polo对合作感受的简短陈述。内容偏向信息性报道，缺乏乐评应有的分析与鉴赏维度。

items.body: Oxford band Shaven Primates released the four-track EP “Kill The Algorithm” on TAD Records on 31 July 2026. The EP runs 17 minutes and 53 seconds. What Shaven Primates address on ‘Kill The Algorithm’ The EP opens with “Saviour” (4:26), then moves through “Pioneer Way” (3:30) and “Feed” (4:28) before the title track “Kill The Algorithm” (5:28). Across the four songs the band take on dependency, tabloid conditioning, grievance politics and the mechanics of social media. “Pioneer Way” sets its argument in a Britain of workplace exhaustion and scapegoating, with the line “Commonplace everyday wreck of the UK”. The title track turns on the repeated command of its own name. Shaven Primates describe themselves on Bandcamp as “a 5-piece dark-wave, art-rock, post-punk band that seeks to push the boundaries of the genre”, adding that their “music is a narrative of human emotion and experience; fear, love and anger resonate through the orchestration, giving a deeply cathartic release”. “Kill The Algorithm” is on Spotify. The band’s Bandcamp page currently lists their three earlier releases only, so the EP cannot be bought there yet. About Shaven Primates Shaven Primates are based in Oxford, UK, and mix darkwave, art-rock and post-punk with harder guitar work. The band’s own summary of that mix is short: their music is “a narrative of human emotion and experience”. Their Bandcamp discography begins with “Child Of Dirt” on 26 November 2021, followed by “Birds Aren’t Real” on 28 July 2023 and “Chasing The Dragon” on 13 December 2024. Neither Discogs nor Wikipedia holds an entry for the band, so the Bandcamp listings remain the clearest record of their releases. “Kill The Algorithm” is their first release since “Chasing The Dragon” in December 2024, and the first to carry the TAD Records imprint.
items._cn_summary: 牛津乐队Shaven Primates在独立厂牌TAD Records发行了四曲EP《Kill The Algorithm》，全长约18分钟。乐队自定位为五人的暗潮、艺术摇滚、后朋克组合，融合较硬的吉他元素。作品围绕依赖症、小报操控、怨恨政治及社交媒体机制等社会议题展开，标题曲以重复命令式的hook为核心，Pioneer Way以英国职场疲惫与替罪叙事为切入点。乐队在Bandcamp上自我描述其音乐为关于人类情感与体验的叙事，试图突破类型边界。这是该乐队自2024年12月《Chasing The Dragon》以来的首张新作，也是首次使用TAD Records厂牌发行的作品。文本本身偏新闻通稿性质，缺乏深入的乐评分析与音乐性描述。

items.body: 45 Grave released the album “Pick Your Poison” on 14 August 2012 through Frontier Records. The Los Angeles deathrock band’s album turns 14 this year and stood as its first collection of new material in 27 years, following the group’s 1985 breakup after “Sleep in Safety.” Dinah Cancer had reformed 45 Grave in 2004 and rebuilt the lineup several times over the following years. By 2010, the band settled into a configuration of Cancer on vocals, guitarist Frank Agnew (the Adolescents, T.S.O.L.), bassist Brandden Blackwell and drummer Tom Coyne, the lineup that recorded “Pick Your Poison.” The album mixes newly written songs with older, previously unrecorded material and a re-worked version of “Night of the Demons,” for which a video was produced. “Pick Your Poison” contains ten tracks: “Pick Your Poison,” “Night of the Demons,” “Child of Fear,” “Akira,” “A Desert Dream,” “Lucky 214,” “Highway 666,” “Johnny,” “Sorceress” and “Winds of Change.” Frontier Records issued the album on CD and vinyl. Pick Your Poison by 45 Grave About 45 Grave 45 Grave formed in Los Angeles in 1979, growing out of a related project called Vox Pop. The original lineup paired vocalist Dinah Cancer, formerly of Castration Squad, with guitarist Paul B. Cutler, bassist Rob Graves (also known as Rob Ritter, formerly of the Bags and the Gun Club) and drummer Don Bolles of the Germs. The band’s name came from a thrift-store button reading “WE DIG 45 GRAVE.” Alongside Christian Death, 45 Grave is recognized as one of the earliest American gothic rock acts, developing a hybrid of horror punk and gothic rock that came to be known as deathrock. The band’s sole studio album from its original run, “Sleep in Safety,” followed the 1981 single “Black Cross” and built on the earlier fast-paced version of “Partytime,” later slowed down and reworked for the album. A remixed version of “Partytime” appeared on the soundtrack to the 1985 film “The Return of the Living Dead” and became an MTV staple. 45 Grave broke up in 1985. A brief reunion in 1988 produced the live album “Only the Good Die Young,” but the band split again after bassist Rob Graves died in 1990. Dinah Cancer revived 45 Grave in 2004 to mark the band’s 25th anniversary, working through several lineup changes before settling by 2010 on guitarist Frank Agnew, bassist Brandden Blackwell and drummer Tom Coyne. That lineup recorded “Pick Your Poison,” released on Frontier Records on 14 August 2012 as the band’s first collection of new material in 27 years. Guitarist Dylan Thomas, formerly of the Dickies, joined in 2014, and the band has continued to perform since, including a two-day billing at the Cruel World festival in Pasadena in 2022 alongside Bauhaus, Devo, Blondie and Morrissey.
items._cn_summary: 本文是关于45 Grave乐队专辑《Pick Your Poison》发行14周年的回顾性新闻稿。专辑于2012年8月14日由Frontier Records发行，是乐队1985年解散后27年来首张全新作品，融合了新创作歌曲、未发表的旧作以及《Night of the Demons》的重新编排版本。45 Grave 1979年成立于洛杉矶，是美国最早将恐怖朋克与哥特摇滚融合并发展出死亡摇滚（deathrock）风格的乐队之一，与Christian Death齐名。原阵容包括主唱Dinah Cancer、吉他手Paul B. Cutler、贝斯手Rob Graves和Germs乐队的鼓手Don Bolles。本文本质上是乐队历史与专辑发行信息的整理，并未对音乐本身进行实质性乐评分析。作为死亡摇滚代表，该专辑在风格分类上贴近用户暗潮偏好，但缺乏对声音设计、实验性或跨类型融合的深入探讨，且文章为新闻性质而非原创乐评。

items.album: The Arms of Someone New expand ‘Love, Power & Justice’ to 38 tracks on Projekt
items.excerpt: Projekt has released the 40th anniversary deluxe edition of “Love, Power & Justice” by The Arms of Someone New. The set went up on 14 August 2026 as a name-your-price download on the label’s Bandcamp page, and runs to 38 tracks across three parts. The material dates from 1986, when Mel Eberle and Steve Jones recorded it in Champaign-Urbana, Illinois. Projekt first issued it on CD in July 2000 through its Projekt: Archive imprint. The 2026 edition returns to the original tapes.
items.body: Projekt has released the 40th anniversary deluxe edition of “Love, Power & Justice” by The Arms of Someone New. The set went up on 14 August 2026 as a name-your-price download on the label’s Bandcamp page, and runs to 38 tracks across three parts. The material dates from 1986, when Mel Eberle and Steve Jones recorded it in Champaign-Urbana, Illinois. Projekt first issued it on CD in July 2000 through its Projekt: Archive imprint. The 2026 edition returns to the original tapes. Love, Power & Justice (2026 40th anniversary deluxe edition) by The Arms of Someone New What the ‘Love, Power & Justice’ deluxe edition contains The first part is a new 2026 mix of the eleven-track album: “Silhouette”, “Hollywood”, “No City Fun”, “Next Year in Jerusalem”, “Summer Dress”, “Your Evening At Home”, “The Sense of an Ending”, “Believe Me”, “Our Town”, “Everything At Once” and the opening piece. The second part collects fifteen previously unreleased and alternate recordings from the same period, among them “Dear Friend”, “The Far Cafe”, “Dreaming of Home”, “4 O’Clock”, “Finding My Way Back Home”, “December 1910 (Vietnam instrumental)”, “Vietnam (Business is Business)”, “Carry the Day” and “Lady on Train”, plus 4-track versions of “The Sense of an Ending” and “Summer Dress”, demo versions of “Summer Dress”, “In Between” and “Radio Now”, and a 2026 remaster of “Uptown”. The third part restores the 1986 mix in a 2026 remaster, so the set carries both readings of the album in full. The artwork has been reworked for the reissue. Projekt also still lists final copies of the 2000 CD in a jewel box. Eberle and Jones will host a listening party on Saturday 29 August 2026 at 20:00 CEST, running through the expanded edition in text chat on Bandcamp. About The Arms of Someone New Mel Eberle and Steve Jones formed The Arms of Someone New in 1983 while students in Champaign-Urbana, Illinois. Their reference points were The Beatles and psychedelia on one side and the melancholy end of Factory Records and The Cure around “Faith” on the other. They worked with simple synthesizers, a Roland TR-707 drum machine and heavily reverbed guitars, with vocals kept low in the arrangements. Their debut album “Susan Sleepwalking” appeared in 1985 on their own Office Records imprint, with Nick Rudd contributing guitar and vocals to two tracks. “Love, Power & Justice” followed, recorded with contributions from musicians who would go on to form the dream pop act Area, including guitarist Henry Frayne, later of Lanterna, and Lynn Canfield. Frayne holds writing credits on “Hollywood” and “Believe Me”; Canfield on “Our Town” and “Uptown”. Brendan Gamble also played on the sessions. Projekt has handled the duo’s catalogue since the 2000 CD. The label put “Tape Recordings 1983-1985” on Bandcamp in March 2026, and issued a three-disc 40th anniversary edition of “Susan Sleepwalking” in October 2025. The “Love, Power & Justice” set completes that pair, and is the first time the album has been remixed rather than reissued as recorded.
items._cn_summary: Projekt厂牌发行了The Arms of Someone New 1986年专辑《Love, Power & Justice》40周年豪华版，收录38首曲目，包含2026年新混音、15首未发行及替代录音、以及1986年原始混音的修复版。文章详细介绍了乐队成员Mel Eberle和Steve Jones在伊利诺伊大学香槟分校时期的学生创作背景，其音乐参照Beatles与迷幻摇滚，以及Factory Records和The Cure《Faith》前后的忧郁气质，使用简单合成器、Roland TR-707鼓机和大量混响吉他。专辑还包含后来组成dream pop乐队Area的乐手参与。原文主要是新闻发布性质的发行通告，未提供实质性乐评或音乐深度分析。
